This might not necessarily be an undesirable development, if the reasons behind the pick-up in inflation were about to fade soon, bringing inflation swiftly to its target. However, inflation expectations have adjusted and shifted upwards, with financial market and consumer survey indicators pointing to inflation between 2% and 3% in the medium and longer-term.[2] Moreover, expected inflation is becoming an important element in price setting in euro area firms, as shown by the ECB survey[3] High inflation - coupled with labour market tightness - has also triggered calls for higher wage rises. The ECBs experimental wage tracker so far points to a moderate increase in wage growth in this year and the next, below the projected inflation in the euro area. However, the longer the high inflation rates persist, the likelier it is that they will be transmitted to higher wage growth and potentially lead to a wage-price spiral. In the medium term, therefore it seems possible that inflation will settle at higher levels than we have observed in the recent years, even after the existing supply shocks fade. We could face a switch to a higher inflation regime, as some of the drivers of past deflationary pressures have lost steam, such as global trade liberalisation and the integration of low- wage Chinese workers to the global economy. At the same time, some structural inflationary factors are gaining momentum, namely the green transition, strengthening of the EUs strategic autonomy and the reorganisation of global supply chains with possible nearshoring. There will still be some deflationary forces at play, such as rapid digital transformation, other innovation and elevated debt levels, but there is a question as to whether these could overcome the inflationary forces. Let me now turn to monetary policy. Given the high inflation in the euro area, reaching 8.1% annually in May and ranging from 5.4% in Malta to 20.1% in Estonia, together with strengthening inflation expectations, we need to make further steps towards normalisation of our monetary policy. After we ended net asset purchases under the special pandemic programme in March this year, we are now winding down also other asset purchases. Soon, preferably by July, net asset purchases should be fully completed. This would allow for the first ECB rate hike since 2011. The next policy steps will depend on incoming data and prospects for approaching our 2% inflation target in the medium term. Given the uncertain economic outlook, it is important to move on gradually. By being able to flexibly reinvest maturing bonds from the pandemic portfolio, we will continue to work against increased fragmentation in the bond markets. While is a priority for the Eurosystem to navigate the challenges of elevated inflation, monetary policy interacts with fiscal and other policies. Fiscal and monetary policy consider each others actions when designing policy measures. Acting within their own mandates, the two policies can be mutually reinforcing. Stabilisation of the economy after the pandemic shock is a great example of this! However, in times of high inflation and slowing economic growth - that put low-income households in a particularly difficult position - mutual policy support is a greater challenge. In order not to hinder the moderation of inflation, fiscal support should be targeted at the most vulnerable households and businesses. Excessive and too general mitigation of the burden of rising living costs would further stimulate aggregate demand and, in turn, the growth of prices. Governments should also carefully consider potential increases in minimum wages and the wages of civil servants. It is important not to fuel the risk of second round-effects from the currently high inflation and rising inflation expectations being transmitted to higher wage and price pressures in the euro area. Due to high inflation and the expected normalisation of our monetary policy, borrowing in the financial markets has become more costly for sovereigns, banks and corporates. Similarly, the bank lending rates for households and corporates have also started to rise, though at a slower pace. Despite considerable increases in the yields of sovereign bonds, the costs of borrowing by the euro area governments are still manageable. Average yields that governments pay on their outstanding debt remain low in historical terms. Moreover, with high inflation and further economic growth, government revenues have also increased. However, given the elevated public debt levels of several countries and the slowdown in economic growth, further tightening of government borrowing conditions will put pressures on fiscal policies. At the same time, governments are facing rising costs related to population ageing, and the need to strengthen the resilience of health systems and ramp-up public investments in support of the green transition. Let me conclude this part with being more general. Fiscal policy should support price and broader macroeconomic stability. The suspension of EU fiscal rules should not be a reason to delay the return of fiscal policy to a sustainable path. Regardless of the rules, financial markets are starting to respond more to the perceived fiscal health of individual countries than in the last two years. This brings me to my last point. The actions of governments and central banks can also bemutually reinforcing and complementary in tackling structural challenges, such as climate change. The primary role in this regard lies with governments, as they have the power and democratic legitimacy to adopt legislation that compel industries and individuals to act sustainably. Nevertheless, there are also areas where central banks can and should contribute. Climate change is affecting our economies and thus price and financial stability, which lie at the heart of central banks mandates. This urges us to take climate-related considerations into account in the conduct of monetary and macroprudential policies and in the supervision of banks. In July last year, the Eurosystem central banks concretised our commitments and adopted a roadmap on climate-related actions. Regarding monetary policy, we agreed to include climate-related factors in macroeconomic modelling and monetary policy operations, more specifically the collateral framework and corporate asset purchases. Related to banking supervision, our activities are focused on the disclosure and assessment of climate risks. This year, together with the banks, we are performing the first climate stress tests, the results of which will be available soon. Regarding our investments that are not related to the implementation of monetary policy, Banka Slovenije is increasing the share of green and other sustainable bonds. We also abstain from investing in firms in the tobacco and arms industries, and firms causing major environmental harm. In the future, we plan to further enhance our socially responsible investment framework by setting targets that are even more ambitious. Next year we will start measuring and reporting carbon footprints, and other indicators of socially responsible and sustainable investing. There are several challenges along the road, such as availability and quality of climate-related data. However, we strive for green, which is also the colour of our logo. To conclude. We are facing a number of challenges, among which price stabilisation and financial stability are the priorities for the Eurosystem. However, challenges can also be opportunities. And by acting together, as we have done over the last two years, we will manage and take advantage of them. [1] On 9 June 2022. [2] Five-year forward ILS rate currently stands at 2.3% and three-year- ahead inflation expectations from the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey shifted from 2.0% to 2.9% in March. 5 Year 5 Year Forward Inflation Expectation I MacroTrends [3] The globalisation of inflation (europa.eu)

Title: Address by Tina umer, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Slovenia, at the Bank Association Banking Conference of SloveniaDeputy Governor addressed the participants of the banking conference, organised by the Bank Association of Slovenia on 16 June 2022.
text: Address by Tina zumer, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Slovenia, at the Banking Conference of the Bank of Slovenia Association 16.06.2022 / Public appearances The impact of Russian aggression on the normalisation of monetary policy Dear Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Speakers and Organizers of this Event, Dear Guests, Over the past two years, economic and financial developments have been particularly intense. This year, however, was marked shortly after the start by Russia's attack on Ukraine, which developed into a devastating war and a new shock to our economies before the fight against the pandemic was truly over. Supply-side constraints have increased further since we saw the first signs of easing them at the end of last year. Prices of energy products and other raw materials also increased. This is a typical example of a shock that raises inflation and slows economic growth. This is a particular challenge for monetary policy. With inflation rising, the first decisions at the ECB level regarding the start of monetary policy normalisation were taken at the end of last year. We are now moving on to new steps, as I will explain below, together with the economic circumstances. The normalisation of monetary policy and the changed macroeconomic situation have a direct and indirect impact on the banking system, which I will discuss in the second part of my speech. *** Following the sudden and deep recession caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the euro area economy has recovered faster than expected and faster than in past crises. In the first quarter of this year, the activity of the euro area economy was 0.5% higher than the pre-pandemic level, while that of Slovenia was already more than 7%. A swift and coordinated response from monetary, fiscal and other policies has been key to a swift recovery, in addition to progress on vaccinations. You have also made an important contribution from the banks, which entered the pandemic crisis significantly more resilient than they did into the global financial crisis. However, the rapid and simultaneous recovery in global demand  in addition to supply-side constraints  has led to global supply chain disruptions and higher inflation. The rise in prices in this context  and after their modest rise or decline in 2020  was not unexpected, but it is more pronounced and persistent than we expected. The war and sanctions against Russia have further increased inflation. In May, it exceeded 8% in the euro area and Slovenia, and could be even higher in the next few months. Inflation is becoming more broad-based. For Slovenia, the spread of inflationary pressures is well illustrated by the fact that the share of goods in the consumer basket increased from around 20% in autumn last year to more than 60% in April, with price growth of more than 5%. Despite the higher cost of living and the devastating war at the EU's doorstep, economic growth in the euro area and in our country continues, albeit at a slower pace than it would otherwise be. Business and consumer expectations for the coming months are less encouraging. A decline in GDP in the euro area in the coming quarters cannot be completely ruled out, but for the time being there are several arguments on the side of continued economic growth, which is the baseline scenario of our June forecasts. The impact of the war on GDP and inflation is already reflected in the recent June forecasts for the euro area and Slovenia. GDP growth in the euro area has been revised down by almost one percentage point this year compared to the March forecasts, while the inflation forecast has risen by just under two percentage points. Much of the forecast revisions are due to the war and related sanctions. In the forecasts published yesterday by the Bank of Slovenia, Slovenia also revised the outlook for economic growth. This has been revised upwards to 5.8% for this year, but only due to a strong carry-over of activity from the previous year, while the deteriorated outlook is reducing current economic growth by around two percentage points this year. At the same time, we  mainly due to higher energy and food prices  significantly raised the inflation forecast for this year, to 9%. *** From a longer-term perspective, this year's slowdown in economic growth, even in the absence of external shocks, should not come as much of a surprise. Taking aside this external pause in economic growth in the euro area since 2013, given the unusually rapid recovery from the pandemic, the upward phase is longer than the region's historical average of less than 8 years. The high position of the euro economy in the business cycle is reflected in the record high number of employees, the lowest unemployment rate and high capacity utilisation. In the euro area and Slovenia, we are facing high inflation and high valuations and further growth of real estate. This year, in particular, it has been additionally supported by the rapid growth of housing lending. At the same time, our monetary policy  after a protracted period of deflationary pressures and the pandemic shock  remains extremely accommodative, which is a unique situation. The situation is all the more challenging given that we are simultaneously facing increased financial vulnerability in the euro area due to the high indebtedness of some countries and companies, the overvaluation of real estate and the accumulated risks in non-bank financial institutions. How this came about is easier to understand if we place the situation in an even longer time horizon. As Claudio Borio pointed out in May at the Bank of Slovenia's 30th anniversary conference, in recent decades we have witnessed two megatrends that have contributed to the accumulation of financial vulnerabilities. The first is globalisation, which has had a disinflationary effect and contributed to looser monetary policy. The second is financial liberalization. Both have contributed to financial booms and downward price corrections becoming more frequent than they were decades ago. Such megatrends, on the other hand, bring about changes that could lead inflation to stabilise at a (slightly) higher level than before the pandemic even after the supply shocks have subsided. Some disinflationary factors, such as the liberalization of world trade, will lose strength. At the same time, some structural inflationary factors are strengthening, namely the green transition and the strengthening of the EU's strategic autonomy and the resilience of supply chains. Some deflationary forces, such as digitalisation, will also still be present. The question is whether these will be able to overcome inflationary pressures and prevent a transition to a regime of higher or more volatile inflation than before the pandemic. *** Let me now turn to monetary policy. Given the high inflation that is becoming increasingly broad-based, and which is already partly translating into inflation expectations and slightly higher wage growth, the monetary policy priority is clear. Otherwise, we cannot influence supply shocks, nor energy prices. Our task is to consolidate confidence in medium-term price stability through credible and timely action and to prevent inflation expectations from being broadened. This requires a continuation of the normalisation of monetary policy that we started last December: Last started to reduce net asset purchases in the Eurosystem. At the end of March, we concluded net purchases under the PEPP special programme. As of July, we will close our net purchases under the APP. We will continue to reinvest the principal payments due in full. In July, we plan to raise our key interest rates by 25 basis points for the first time in eleven years. We expect a further increase in September, which  depending on the data and new forecasts  may be even bigger. With regard to On the current outlook, we expect a gradual but sequential increase in key interest rates beyond September. At the same time, we will ensure that inflation stabilises at 2% over the medium term. *** The impact of monetary policy normalisation on banks will be multifaceted. Over a prolonged period of extremely low interest rates, banks' interest margins have fallen sharply, and the rise in central bank rates opens up the possibility of a partial recovery. Normalisation of interest rates may benefit banks mainly in the short term, until an increase in active interest rates is followed by passive interest rates. The benefits of higher central bank interest rates will also be limited because there has been a sharp increase in fixed interest rates on loans in recent years. In March, the stock of all loans to non-financial corporations and households accounted for about 40% of such loans, while housing loans accounted for half. In addition, higher uncertainty, lower economic growth and interest rate hikes are likely to contribute to a moderation in bank lending. High inflation and macroeconomic risks can worsen the quality of a bank's portfolio and put downward pressure on the impairment of claims and provisioning and other costs on banks. So, despite some of the relief that the normalization of interest rates brings to banks, the situation in the banking system will not be easy. In most Slovenian banks, you maintain relatively high liquidity. Capital is above regulatory requirements and guidance, but the surpluses are lower than the average of systemically important banks in the euro area. However, there are also significant differences between banks. Some of the most vulnerable would need capital reinforcements if the Swiss franc law were to be enacted. Banks are also exposed to the risk of a further decline in securities prices and, in the medium term, to the risk of a correction in house prices. As these are already visibly overvalued, and credit and property price growth continues to rise rapidly, we are introducing sectoral capital buffers for systemic risks as of 2023. The Slovenian financial system is not significantly directly exposed to Russia and Ukraine. However, there are rather uncertain consequences that will have an indirect and delayed impact on economies, bank customers and, consequently, banks. Looking further and broader, Slovenian banks share the challenges of most other European banks related to international competitiveness and sustainability of business models. Into In the recent period, interest income has been partially replaced by higher non-interest income, especially royalties, where you are significantly upwards and rank in the top quarter of EU countries. Last year, you were also at the European summit on return on capital, but mainly because of the decomposition of impairments and provisions. The environment requires you to make significant investments in digital infrastructure, innovate, connect with fintechs and strengthen resilience to cyber risks. Address you also started climate risks. This year, we are jointly conducting the first climate stress tests, albeit in a simplified form for smaller banks. This is a lesson for all of us. With With the continuation of consolidation, the Slovenian banking market is gradually becoming somewhat less fragmented. However, the time is probably still coming for bolder moves and pan-European bank integration that would more decisively address the challenge of the competitiveness of banks in the region. *** Dear bank representatives, speakers and other esteemed guests, We have become accustomed to the precarious situation over the last two years. We have shown that together we can cope well with unpredictable challenges. There are more of them ahead. The answer is to work together and build resilience. The importance of investing in it has also been shown by the pandemic crisis, which has been a litmus test of the effectiveness of banking system reforms over the last decade. I wish you interesting discussions and pleasant socializing.
text_original: Nagovor Tine umer, namestnice guvernerja Banke Slovenije, na Banni konferenci Zdruenja bank Slovenije 16.06.2022 / Javni nastopi Vpliv ruske agresije na normalizacijo denarne politike Spotovane dame in gospodje, dragi govorci in organizatorji tega dogodka, dragi gostje, v zadnjih dveh letih je bilogospodarsko in nanno dogajanje posebej intenzivno. Letonje leto pa je e kmalu po zaetku zaznamoval ruski napad na Ukrajino, ki se je razvil v uniujoo vojno in nov ok za naa gospodarstva, e preden je boj s pandemijo zares konan. Omejitve na strani ponudbe so se e dodatno poveale, potem ko smo konec lanskega leta zaznali prve znake njihovega popuanja. Prav tako so se dodatno poviale cene energentov in ostalih surovin. Gre za tipien primer oka, ki zviuje inacijo in upoasnjuje gospodarsko rast. To je za denarno politiko poseben izziv. Ob zvievanju inacije smo na ravni ECB prve odloitve glede prietka normalizacije denarne politike sprejeli konec lanskega leta. Sedaj prehajamo na nove korake, kot bom skupaj z gospodarskimi okoliinami pojasnila v nadaljevanju. Normalizacija denarne politike in spremenjene makroekonomske razmere imata neposreden in posreden vpliv na banni sistem, o katerem bom spregovorila v drugem delu govora. *** Evrsko gospodarstvo je po nenadni in globoki recesiji zaradi pandemije COVID-19 okrevalo hitreje od naih priakovanjin hitreje kot v preteklih krizah. Aktivnost evrskega gospodarstva je bila v prvem letonjem etrtletju od predpandemine ravni vija za 0,5 %, slovenskega pa e za ve kot 7 %. Hiter in usklajen odziv denarne, skalne in drugih politik je bil -poleg napredka pri cepljenju -kljunega pomena za hitro okrevanje. Pomembno ste prispevale tudi banke, ki ste v pandemsko krizo vstopile bistveno bolj odporne kot v globalno nanno krizo. Hitro in simultano okrevanje povpraevanja po svetu pa je  poleg omejitev na strani ponudbe -privedlo do globalnih motenj v dobavnih verigah in vije inacije. Rast cen v teh razmerah -in po njihovi skromni rasti oziroma upadanju v letu 2020 -ni bila nepriakovana, je pa izraziteja in vztrajneja, kot smo priakovali. Vojna in sankcije proti Rusiji so inacijo dodatno zviale. Meseca maja je v evrskem obmoju in Sloveniji presegala 8 %, v prihodnjih nekaj mesecih pa bi lahko bila e vija. Inacija postaja vse ire osnovana. Za Slovenijo irjenje inacijskih pritiskov dobro ponazarja dejstvo, da se je dele dobrin v potroni koarici z ve kot 5-odstotno rastjo cen poveal z okoli 20 % jeseni lani na dobrih 60 % aprila. Kljub vijim ivljenjskim strokom in uniujoi vojni pred vrati EU se gospodarska rast v evrskem obmoju in pri nas nadaljuje, eprav poasneje, kot bi se sicer. Priakovanja podjetij in potronikov za prihodnje mesece so manj vzpodbudna. Upada BDP v evrskem obmoju v prihodnjih etrtletij ne moremo povsem izkljuiti, vendar je zaenkrat ve argumentov na strani nadaljevanja gospodarske rasti, kar je osnovni scenarij naih junijskih napovedi. Vpliv vojne na BDP in inacijo se e odraa v sveih, junijskih napovedi za evrsko obmoje in Slovenijo. Rast BDP v evrskem obmoju je bila za letos  glede na napovedi iz marca -revidirana navzdol za skoraj eno odstotno toko, napoved inacije pa se je zviala za malo manj kot dve odstotni toki. Veji del revizij napovedi je prav posledica vojne in z njo povezanih sankcij. Za Slovenijo smo v veraj objavljenih napovedih Banke Slovenije prav tako spremenili obete za gospodarsko rast. Ta je sicer za letonje leto bila popravljena navzgor na 5.8 %, vendar izkljuno zaradi monega prenosa aktivnosti iz prejnjega leta, medtem ko poslabani obeti zniujejo tekoo gospodarsko rast, in sicer za okoli dve odstotni toki v tem letu. Hkrati smo  predvsem zaradi vijih cen energentov in hrane  obutno poviali napoved inacije za letos, in sicer na 9 %. *** Z dolgoroneje perspektive letonja upoasnitev gospodarske rasti tudi v primeru odsotnosti zunanjih okov ne bi smela biti veje preseneenje. e glede na neobiajno hitro okrevanje po pandemiji odmislimo to zunanjo prekinitev gospodarske rasti, ki v evrskem obmoju traja od leta 2013, faza vzpona traja dlje od zgodovinskega povpreja v regiji, ki znaa manj kot 8 let. Na visok poloaj evrskega gospodarstva v poslovnem ciklu kaejo rekordno visoko tevilo zaposlenih, najnija stopnja brezposelnosti in visoka izkorienost proizvodnih zmogljivosti. V evrskem obmoju in Sloveniji se sooamo z visoko inacijo ter visokim vrednotenjem in nadaljnjo rastjo nepreminin. Predvsem pri nas jo letos dodatno podpira tudi hitra rast stanovanjskega kreditiranja. Hkrati pa je naadenarna politika -po dolgotrajnem obdobju deacijskih pritiskov in pandemskem oku -e vedno izjemno spodbujevalna, kar je edinstvena situacija. Situacija je e toliko bolj zahtevna, ker se v evrskem obmoju hkrati sooamo s poveano nanno ranljivostjozaradi visoke zadolenosti nekaterih drav in podjetij, precenjenosti nepreminin in nakopienih tveganji v nebannih nannih institucijah. Kako je do tega prilo, laje razumemo, e situacijo umestimo v e dalji asovni horizont. Kot je maja na konferenci ob 30. obletnici Banke Slovenije izpostavil Claudio Borio, smo bili v zadnjih desetletjih pria dvema megatrendoma, ki sta prispevala h kopienju nannih ranljivosti. Prvi je globalizacija, ki je delovala dezinacijsko in prispevala k ohlapneji denarni politiki. Drugi je nanna liberalizacija. Oboje je prispevalo k temu, da so nanni razcveti in korekcije cen navzdol pogosteji kot pred desetletji. Takni megatrendi pa prinaajo spremembe, pod vplivom katerih bi se lahko inacija tudi po umiritvi ponudbenih okov ustalila na (malo) viji ravni kot pred pandemijo. Nekateri dezinacijski dejavniki, kot je liberalizacija svetovne trgovine, bodo izgubili mo. Hkrati se krepijo nekateri strukturni inacijski dejavniki, in sicer zeleni prehod ter krepitev strateke avtonomije EU in odpornosti oskrbovalnih verig. e vedno bodo prisotne tudi nekatere deacijske sile, kot je digitalizacija. Vpraanje pa je, ali bodo te lahko premagale inacijske pritiske in prepreile prehod v reim vije ali bolj volatilne inacije kot pred pandemijo. *** Naj sedaj preidem na denarno politiko. Glede na visoko inacijo, ki postaja vse ire osnovana, in ki delno e prehaja v inacijska priakovanja ter v nekoliko vijo rast pla, je prioriteta denarne politike jasna. Na ponudbene oke, prav tako ne na cene energentov, sicer ne moremo vplivati. Naa naloga pa je, da s kredibilnim in pravoasnim ukrepanjem utrdimo zaupanje v srednjerono stabilnost cen in prepreimo razsidranje inacijskih priakovanj. To zahteva nadaljevanje normalizacije denarne politike, ki smo jo zaeli lani decembra: Lani smo v Evrosistemu prieli zmanjevati neto nakupe vrednostnih papirjev. Konec marca smo zakljuili z neto nakupi v okviru izrednega programa PEPP. Z julijem bomo zakljuili neto nakupe v okviru programa APP. Zapadle glavnice bomo e naprej v celoti reinvestirali. Julija nameravamo prvi po enajstih letihzviati nae kljune obrestne mere, in sicer za 25 bazinih tok. Septembra priakujemo nadaljnje zvianje, ki bo  odvisno od podatkov in novih napovedi -lahko tudi veje. Glede na trenutne obete tudi po septembru priakujemopostopno, vendar zaporedno dvigovanje kljunih obrestih mer. Ob tem bomo zagotovili, da se inflacija na srednji rok stabilizira pri 2%. *** Vpliv normalizacije denarne politike na banke bo veplasten. V daljem obdobju izjemno nizkih obrestnih mer so seobrestne mare bank mono zniale, dvig centralno bannih obrestnih mer pa odpira monost, da se delno obnovijo. Normalizacija obrestnih mer lahko bankam koristi predvsem na kratek rok, dokler ne bodo zvianju aktivnih obrestnih mer sledile e pasivne obrestne mere. Koristi bank od vijih centralno-bannih obrestnih mer bodo omejene tudi, ker je v zadnjih letih prilo do monega porasta ksnega obrestovanja pri posojilih. Marca je bilo v stanju vseh posojil nenannim drubam in gospodinjstvom taknih posojil priblino 40%, v stanju stanovanjskih posojil pa polovica. Poleg tega bodo vija negotovosti, nija gospodarska rast in zvianje obrestnih mer verjetno pripevali k umirjanju bannega kreditiranja. Visoka inacija in makroekonomska tveganja lahko poslabajo kakovost bannega portfelja in ustvarijo pritisk na oslabitev vrednosti terjatev in oblikovanje rezervacij in na druge stroke bank. Kljub nekaj olajanja, ki jih za banke prinaa normalizacija obrestnih mer, torej razmere v bannem sistemu ne bodo enostavne. V veini slovenskih bank ohranjate razmeroma visoko likvidnost. Kapital imate nad regulatornimi zahtevami in smernicami, vendar so preseki niji kot v povpreju sistemsko pomembnih bank v evrskem obmoju. Med bankami pa so tudi precejnje razlike. Nekaj najbolj izpostavljenih bi v primeru uveljavitve zakona o vicarskih frankih potrebovalo kapitalske okrepitve. Banke ste izpostavljene tudi tveganju nadaljnjega znievanjacen vrednostnih papirjev, na srednji rok pa tudi tveganjukorekcije cen nepreminin. Ker so te e vidno precenjene, rast kreditov in cen nepreminin pa e naprej hitro naraa, z letom 2023 uvajamo sektorska kapitalska blailnika sistemskih tveganj. Slovenski nanni sistem ni pomembneje neposredno izpostavljen do Rusije in Ukrajine. Vendar pa so precej negotove posledice, ki bodo posredno in z zamikom vplivale na gospodarstva, komitente bank in posledino banke. e se ozremo dlje in ire, slovenske banke delite izzive veine drugih evropski bank, povezane z mednarodno konkurennostjo in vzdrnostjo poslovnih modelov. V zadnjem obdobju stenizke obrestne prihodke delno nadomeale z vijimi neobrestnimi prihodki, predvsem opravninami, kjer precej odstopate navzgor in se uvrate v najvijo etrtino drav EU. Lani ste bile pri evropskem vrhu tudi podonosnosti kapitala, vendar predvsem zaradi razgrajevanja oslabitev in rezervacij. Okolje od vas zahteva precejnje investicije v digitalno infrastrukturo, inoviranje, povezovanje s ntechi ter krepitev odpornosti na kibernetska tveganja. Naslavljati ste prieli tudi podnebna tveganja. Letos skupaj izvajamo prve klimatske stresne teste, za manje banke sicer v poenostavljeni obliki. To je una za vse nas. Z nadaljevanjem konsolidacije postaja slovenski banni trg postopno nekoliko manj fragmentiran. as za drzneje poteze in vseevropsko povezovanje bank, ki bi odloneje naslovilo izziv konkurennosti bank v regiji, pa najbr e prihaja. *** Spotovani predstavniki bank, govorci in drugi cenjeni gostje, na negotove razmere smo se v zadnjih ve kot dveh letih e navadili. Pokazali smo, da se skupaj dobro spoprimemo tudi z nepredvidljivimi izzivi. Pred nami jih je ve. Odgovor nanje je sodelovanje in krepitev odpornosti. Kako pomembna so vlaganja vanjo, je pokazala tudi pandemska kriza, ki je bila lakmusov papir uinkovitosti reform bannega sistema v zadnjem desetletju. elim vam zanimive razprave in prijetno druenje.

Title: Address by Governor Botjan Vaslet at the presentation of the OECD report for SloveniaThe event was organised by the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Slovenia.
text: Address by Governor Bostjan Vasle at the presentation of the OECD report for Slovenia 04.07.2022 / Public appearances The spoken word counts. Dear participants in today's presentation of the OECD report, very welcome. First of all, I would like to thank the Minister of Finance for inviting me to today's event. The presentation of the OECD report is an opportunity to exchange expert views with the views of policymakers, which has always led to a very high-quality debate in the past. That is why I consider myself honored to be able to participate in today's panel. Thanks, of course, to the OECD for producing another excellent report. In addition to an in-depth analysis, it is always a great advantage of an OECD report to compare an individual member with the entire group of OECD countries, which cannot be done from a purely national perspective. In response, I will focus on four points. Firstly, on economic growth, namely on the current and on our expectations. I will analyze what are the causes of the current rapid growth and what are the factors that will determine it in the future. In what follows, I will focus on inflation, its drivers and the policies needed to bring it down. In the third point, I will touch on the banking system, and finally on the contribution of the Bank of Slovenia to digitalisation. *** Let me start with economic growth. In recent years, our economies have been facing two shocks that are exceptional from a historical point of view: the pandemic, which was a global phenomenon, and Russia's military aggression on European soil, which is having the greatest impact on European economies. Slovenia has been relatively successful in dealing with the pandemic crisis. The activity curve was similar to that of most EMU members, but at a slightly faster pace. We reached the pre-pandemic level of activity at the end of last year. This is due to two factors: the relatively rapid containment of the last wave of the pandemic and comparatively larger fiscal measures. We entered this year with a good starting point, which was interrupted by the Russian aggression against Ukraine. Growth in individual quarters will therefore be significantly slower than in the same quarters last year, but nevertheless positive. Our "real-time" forecasting models (so-called "now-casting" models) point to continued good growth in the second and third quarters at around 1.0 percent. Taking into account the technical effect of the "high carry-over", the Bank of Slovenia therefore has a significantly higher growth forecast (5.8%) than the OECD (4.6%). Therefore, if we turn our gaze forward, to the medium term, I fully agree with the OECD's findings and recommendations. Slovenia is lagging behind in terms of productivity growth, as the level has practically stagnated for many years, which weakens the potential for further growth. In addition, Slovenian society is ageing, which is a trend in most developed countries, but this process is one of the fastest in Slovenia. Without adjustments, which are also mentioned in the report, it will not be possible to increase growth potential. And without adjustments, pressures on the sustainability of public finances will also increase. Last but not least, we have seen the importance of their manageability during both crises, the pandemic and the current military, when the space of public finances to contribute to the mitigation of external shocks is a key factor that differentiates individual countries. *** Let me now touch on inflation. In Slovenia, this is a particularly sensitive topic. Problems with high inflation accompanied the disintegration of the former Yugoslavia. However, the subsequent period of high inflation, in the period immediately before the adoption of the euro, was the last economic problem that we successfully addressed, so that we were able to adopt the euro about 15 years ago. The consequences on our economy, as well as the social problems caused by high inflation, remain on the minds of many of us. However, the current inflation is due to factors other than the two mentioned. This time, we are not talking about inappropriate economic policies or about the deep structural problems of our economy. Existing inflation is due to external factors. The impact of both health and military crises is currently reflected in price growth even more than in economic growth. Namely, the measures to contain the pandemic included shutting down a significant part of our economies while maintaining the disposable income of the population. The inability to spend, the inability to travel and restrictions on production are factors that have had deflationary tendencies. And, of course, the other way around: the withdrawal of preventive measures, i.e. the release of demand while maintaining disruptions in supply chains, led to a rise in inflation last year. At the beginning of this year, this trend was accelerated by Russian aggression, which led to a rapid increase in energy and food prices. The persistence of energy pressures has also changed the nature of inflation. Growth in energy prices is increasingly being passed on to other groups, and now Slovenia accounts for over two-thirds of the price index with growth exceeding 5%. To prevent inflation from becoming more sustainable, action is needed on several levels. The most important is, of course, the geopolitical framework and the measures taken to stabilise it. In the context of economic policies, however, the key one is the one that I know best  monetary policy adjustment. At the ECB level, we have already begun the normalisation of monetary policy at the transition to this year, which has resulted in (i) the completion of new purchases under both QE programmes, (ii) the conclusion that the conditions set out in the forward guidance have been met, and (iii) the expected interest rate hike  by 0.25 percentage points at the July meeting and then by the planned 0.5 percentage points in September. *** As far as the banking system is concerned, the report does not pay particular attention to it this time, which is good news. After major problems with the banking system in the previous crisis, which began at the end of 2008, the Slovenian banking system has so far withstood this current crisis, both pandemic and military, without major consequences. There are three reasons for this: (i) increased capital solidity of banks, which is also accompanied by better governance in banks; (ii) a different regulatory environment  the previous financial crisis strengthened the EU-wide system of banking supervision, harmonised approaches and ensured greater capital soundness for banks; (iii) support to the ECB and national fiscal policies directly to banks and indirectly to the maintenance of the financial stability of businesses and citizens. Key indicators of banks' financial soundness therefore remain favourable. Nevertheless, banks, like the economy as a whole, face structural challenges: (i) how to find profitable business models, (ii) how to adapt to technological challenges that are changing their competitive environment, and (iii) how to catch the train on environmental adjustments to maintain their presence in a changed market. Without effective responses to these challenges, we cannot expect banks in Slovenia to move closer to banks in the more advanced economies of the euro area. *** Finally, let me use the technological changes affecting banks' operations as a starting point to address a special chapter of this year's Economic Review of Slovenia  digitalisation. The report focuses on the digitalisation processes of the real economy, but digitalisation is equally important in the field of economic policies. At the ECB, we are aware of the importance and opportunities that digitalisation also brings to the area of finance and finance. That is why we have decided to start the research phase of the introduction of a digital euro, which opens up the possibility of its actual introduction in 2026. We will systematically examine the different options for its introduction, how they would affect the conduct of monetary policy and what implications they would have for the rest of the banking and financial system. We want to make sure that the digital euro also retains all the key elements that we are currently providing with existing money. To mention only the key ones: security, stability, accessibility and privacy protection.
text_original: Nagovor guvernerja Botjana Vasleta na predstavitvi poroila OECD za Slovenijo 04.07.2022 / Javni nastopi Velja govorjena beseda. Spotovani udeleenci dananje predstavitve poroila OECD, lepo pozdravljeni. Najprej zahvala ministru za nance za povabilo na dananji dogodek. Predstavitev poroila OECD je prilonost za izmenjavo mnenj strokovnjakov s pogledom oblikovalcev politik, ki je v preteklosti vedno privedla do zelo kakovostne razprave. Zato si tejem v ast, da lahko sodelujem na dananjem panelu. Zahvala pa seveda tudi OECD za pripravo ponovno izvrstnega poroila. Poleg poglobljene analize je vedno velika prednost OECD poroila, da primerja posamezno lanico s celotno skupino OECD drav, esar ni mogoe narediti zgolj z nacionalnim pogledom. V odzivu se bom osredotoil na tiri toke. Najprej na gospodarsko rast, in sicer na trenutno in na naa priakovanja. Analiziral bom, kaj so vzroki za trenutno hitro rast in kaj so dejavniki, ki jo bodo doloali v prihodnosti. V nadaljevanju se bom osredotoil na inacijo, njene dejavnike in politike, ki so potrebne za njeno umiritev. V tretji toki se bom dotaknil bannega sistema, na koncu pa e prispevka Banke Slovenije k digitalizaciji. *** Naj zanem z gospodarsko rastjo. Nae ekonomije se v zadnjih letih sooajo z dvema okoma, ki sta izjemna z zgodovinskega vidika: pandemija, ki je bila globalni pojav, in vojaka agresija Rusije na evropskih tleh, ki pa ima najveje posledice na evropska gospodarstva. Slovenija je bila pri sooanju s pandemino krizo relativno uspena. Krivulja gospodarske aktivnosti je bila sicer podobna kot v veini lanic EMU, ampak nekoliko hitreja. Pred-pandemino raven aktivnosti smo namre dosegli e ob koncu lanskega leta. To je posledica dveh dejavnikov: relativno hitrega obvladanja zadnjega vala pandemije in primerjalno vejih skalnih ukrepov. V letonje leto smo tako vstopili z dobrim izhodiem, kar pa je prekinila ruska agresija na Ukrajino. Rast v posameznih etrtletjih bo zato znatno poasneja kot v enakih etrtletjih lanskega leta, ampak kljub temu pozitivna. Nai modeli "sprotnega" napovedovanja (t. I. now-casting modeli) kaejo na nadaljevanje dobre rasti v drugem in tretjem etrtletju po okoli 1,0odstotnih stopnjah. Ob upotevanju tehninega uinka "visokega prenosa" imamo zato v Banki Slovenije znatno vijo napoved rasti (5,8 %) kot OECD (4,6 %). e torej preusmerimo pogled naprej, v srednjerono obdobje, pa se v celoti strinjam z ugotovitvami in priporoili OECD. Slovenija zaostaja v rasti produktivnost, saj nivo praktino stagnira e vrsto let, kar slabi potencial za nadaljnjo rast. Poleg tega se slovenska druba stara, kar je sicer trend veine razvitih drav, vendar je ta proces pri nas med hitrejimi. Brez prilagoditev, ki so omenjene tudi v poroilu, ne bo mogoe poveati potenciala za rast. Prav tako pa bodo brez prilagoditev pritiski na vzdrnost javnih nanc edalje veji. Pomen njihove obvladljivosti pa smo nenazadnje videli v asu obeh kriz, pandemine in trenutne vojake, ko je prostor javnih nanc, da prispevajo k blaitvi zunanjih okov, kljuen dejavnik, ki diferencira posamezne drave. *** Naj se sedaj dotaknem inacije. V Sloveniji je to posebej obutljiva tema. Teave z visoko inacijo so spremljale razpad nekdanje Jugoslavije. Kasneje obdobje visoke inacije, v obdobju neposredno pred prevzemom evra, pa je bil zadnji ekonomski problem, ki smo ga uspeno naslovili, da smo lahko pred priblino 15 leti prevzeli evro. Posledice na nao ekonomijo in tudi drubeni problemi, ki jih je povzroila visoka inacija, ostajajo v razmiljanjih marsikoga izmed nas. Vendar je trenutna inacija posledica druganih dejavnikov, kot sta bile obe omenjeni. Tokrat ne govorimo o neprimernih ekonomskih politikah ali o globokih strukturnih problemih nae ekonomije. Obstojea inacija je posledica zunanjih dejavnikov. Uinek obeh kriz, zdravstvene in vojake, se namre trenutno e bolj kot na gospodarski rasti odraa na rasti cen. Namre, ukrepi za omejitev pandemije so zajemali zaprtje znatnega dela naih gospodarstev ob hkratnem ohranjanju razpololjivega dohodka prebivalstva. Nezmonost troenja, nezmonost potovanja in omejitve v proizvodnji so dejavniki, ki so imeli deacijske tendence. In seveda obratno: umik preventivnih ukrepov, to je sprostitev povpraevanja ob hkratnem ohranjanju moten v dobavnih verigah, so v lanskem letu privedli do naraanja inacije. V zaetku letonjega leta je ta trend pospeila e ruska agresija, ki je privedla do hitrega povianja cen energentov in hrane. Zaradi dolgotrajnosti energetskih pritiskov se je spremenila tudi narava inacije. Rast cen energentov se v vse veji meri prenaa tudi v druge skupine in sedaj imamo v Sloveniji preko dve tretjini indeksa cen z rastjo, ki presega 5 %. Da inacija ne bi postala trajneja, je potrebno ukrepanje na ve nivojih. Najpomembneji je seveda geopolitini okvir in ukrepanje za njegovo stabilizacijo. V okviru ekonomskih politik pa je kljuna tista, ki jo najbolje poznam -prilagoditev denarne politike. Na ravni ECB smo e ob prehodu v letonje leto zaeli z normalizacijo denarne politike, ki je tekom minulih mesecev letonjega leta rezultirala: (i) v zakljuku novih nakupov v okviru obeh programov QE, (ii) ugotovitvi, da so izpolnjeni pogoji iz prihodnje usmeritve denarne politike (t. i. forward guidance), in (iii) priakovanem dvigu obrestne mere  na julijski seji za 0,25 o. t. in nato septembra za nartovane 0,5 o. t. *** Kar se tie bannega sistema, mu poroilo tokrat ne posvea posebne pozornosti, kar je dobra novica. Potem ko smo imeli v prejnji krizi, ki se je zaela konec leta 2008, velike teave z bannim sistemom, je slovenski banni sistem tokratni krizi, pandemino in vojako, zaenkrat prenesel brez vejih posledic. Razlogi za to so trije: (i) veja kapitalska trdnost bank, ki jo spremlja tudi bolje upravljanje v bankah; (ii) drugano regulatorno okolje  prejnja nanna kriza je okrepila vseevropski sistem nadzora nad bankami, poenotila pristope in zagotovila vejo kapitalsko trdnost bank; (iii) podpora ECB in nacionalnih skalnih politik neposredno bankam in posredno ohranjanju nanne stabilnosti podjetij in dravljanov. Kljuni pokazatelji nanne trdnosti bank torej ostajajo ugodni. Kljub temu pa so banke, podobno kot celotno gospodarstvo, pred strukturnimi izzivi: (i) kako najti dobikonosne poslovne modele, (ii) kako se prilagoditi na tehnoloke izzive, ki spreminjajo njihovo konkurenno okolje, in (iii) kako ujeti vlak glede okoljskih prilagoditev, da ohranijo prisotnost na spremenjenem trgu. Brez uinkovitih odgovorov na te izzive ne moremo priakovati, da se bodo banke v Sloveniji pribliale bankam v razvitejih ekonomijah evrskega obmoja. *** Naj na koncu tehnoloke spremembe, ki vplivajo na poslovanje bank, uporabim kot iztonico, da naslovim posebno poglavje tokratnega ekonomskega pregleda Slovenije  digitalizacijo. V poroilu je poudarek na procesih digitalizacije realne ekonomije, vendar je digitalizacija enako pomembna tudi na podroju ekonomskih politik. V ECB se zavedamo pomena in prilonosti, ki jih digitalizacija prinaa tudi na podroje denarnitva in nanc. Zato smo se odloili za zaetek raziskovalne faze uvedbe digitalnega evra, ki odpira monost njegove dejanske uvedbe leta 2026. Sistematino bomo prouili razline monosti njegove uvedbe, kako bi vplivale na vodenje denarne politike in kakne posledice bi imele za preostali del bannega in nannega sistema. Zagotoviti elimo, da bo tudi digitalni evro ohranil vse kljune elemente, ki jih sedaj zagotavljamo z obstojeim denarjem. e omenim samo kljune: varnost, stabilnost, dostopnost in varovanje zasebnosti.

Title: Governor statement following the Governing Council's monetary meetingThe members of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank continue to decisively normalise monetary policy. We raised the key ECB interest rates by 75 basis points, the second consecutive increase this year, after a long period of unchanged interest rates. Interest rate hikes and their impact on financing conditions will contribute to ensuring that current inflationary pressures do not extend beyond the medium term.
text: BANKA SLOVENIJE EVROSISTEM Governors statement following the ECBs Governing Council monetary policy meeting 09/09/2022 / Press release The euro area recorded favourable economic growth in the first half of this year, expecting this growth to slow down significantly over the coming quarters. The forecast published today predicts 3.1% growth this year, with the growth forecast slowing to 0.9% next year due to Russias military aggression. Inflation is expected to reach 8.1% on average this year, then it is expected to decline gradually in the coming year. In these circumstances members of the European Central Bank Governing Council have decided to move forward decisively with the normalisation of monetary policy. We have raised ECBs key interest rates by 75 basis points. After a protracted period of unchanged interest rates, this is the second consecutive interest rate hike this year. The interest rate hikes and their impact on the financing conditions will prevent current inflation expectations from extending over the medium term. After favourable economic growth in the first half of the year, the outlook for economic growth in the euro area is expected to deteriorate significantly in the remainder of the year. In the wake of the economic downturn on energy markets due to the continued Russian military aggression in the Ukraine and the minor but still evident restrictions in supply chains, the stagnation in activity is currently limited to manufacturing. However, due to increasing living costs and uncertainty regarding future economic trends, growth in demand for services, which grew significantly after the economy was re- opened following the lifting of measures associated with the coronavirus, has also cooled down. The inflation rate increased to 9.1% in August. In light of strong price pressure along the price chain, inflation pressures continue to broaden, while the level of core inflation, which excludes energy prices and food, rose to 4.3% in August. Despite slightly lower year-on-year growth, high energy prices continue to be the main factor in headline inflation. Their 38.3% year- on-year growth is the result, in particular, of extremely high electricity and gas prices. The forecasts that members of the ECBs Governing Council discussed at yesterdays meeting indicate that the level of economic activity over the medium term will be lower than in previous forecasts, while growth in prices will continue to increase. This years 3.1% economic growth is expected to slow down in the coming year to 0.9%, and strengthen again to 1.9% in 2024. Due to strong cost pressures, inflation is expected to persist at high levels for a bit longer and reach 8.1% on average this year. Assuming that the circumstances on energy markets stabilise, disruptions to supply chains are eliminated and cost pressures normalise, inflation is expected to decline going forward and reach 5.5% in 2023 and 2.3% in 2024. In addition to the core forecast, members of the Governing Council of the ECB were also apprised of the adverse scenario, which assumes the complete and permanent suspension of energy deliveries from Russia and the partial suspension of production in the euro area. In light of this adverse scenario, real GDP would contract by 0.9% in the coming year, with inflation reaching 6.9%. Borrowing costs have thus increased additionally both in the public and private sectors since the July session of the Governing Council. Their increase reflects the expectations of market participants of continued interest rate hikes in the Eurosystem aimed at slowing inflation. Like in other countries in the euro area, the yield on 10-year Slovenian government bonds has also grown, i.e. to around 2.6%. The premium over the 10-year German government bond, the yield of which is around 1.6%, remained at a similar level of that at the end of July. Borrowing costs also increased for the private sector of the euro area, both in the bond and equities segments. The scope of net issued private sector shares and bonds still remains robust, which also applies to lending to non-financial corporations by banks. Based on the latest economic trends and new forecasts, the ECB Governing Council has decided to move forward decisively with the normalisation of monetary policy. We have raised all three ECB key interest rates by 75 basis points. This is the second consecutive interest rate hike this year after a protracted period of unchanged interest rates, following the July 50 basis point hike. Here we anticipate the further raising of interest rates also going forward, with the level of the rises depending on medium-term inflation outlooks. The interest rate hikes and their impact on the financing conditions will prevent current inflation expectations from extending over the medium term. The aim of the members of the ECBs Governing Council is for inflation to stabilise at 2% over the medium term.

Title: Deputy Governor Tina umer, Deputy Governor, presented current developments in the field of monetary policy and capital markets to the participants at the Pension and Disability Insurance Conference.
text: Address by Tina zumer, Deputy Governor, at the Conference on Pension and Disability Insurance 12.09.2022 / Public appearances The spoken word is valid Monetary Policy and Capital Markets Pension and Disability Insurance Conference, Portoroz, 12/09/2022 Dear ladies and gentlemen, dear speakers and organizers of this event, dear guests, In the last two years, economic and financial developments have been particularly intense. While we were still struggling with the pandemic and its consequences, the beginning of this year marked the beginning of Russia's military aggression against Ukraine, which developed into a devastating war and a new shock to our economies. Uncertainty and volatility in financial and commodity markets have increased tremendously. Such an environment is a particular challenge for monetary policy. Against the backdrop of persistent increases in inflation at the ECB level, we are continuing the decisive further normalisation of monetary policy, which we started at the end of last year. The key ECB interest rates were raised by 75 basis points last week, moving into positive interest rate range for the first time since 2011. Given the current economic circumstances, the monetary policy priority is clear, as I will explain below. The normalisation of monetary policy and the changed macroeconomic situation are having a direct and indirect impact on the financial and capital markets, which I will discuss in the second part of my speech. I will also touch on the Capital Markets Union, which would help the development and resilience of Europe's financial sector and economy and support the necessary green transition. It is necessary both to address climate challenges and to ensure our energy security. Pension funds also play a key role in its development. Despite the negative shocks, it can be said that both our and the euro area economies have shown a high degree of resilience. The economic recovery from the pandemic has been swift, much faster and stronger than expected. Economic policies, including monetary policy, have managed to provide sufficient support to the economy, and economic agents have managed to adapt relatively successfully to the new situation. Favourable economic growth continued in the first half of this year, with record-high employment and low unemployment. However, the outlook for economic growth in Slovenia and the euro area as a whole is deteriorating over the rest of the year. High energy prices, continued Russian military aggression in Ukraine and ongoing supply chain constraints are expected to lead to a significant slowdown in economic growth. The higher cost of living and uncertainty about future economic developments are also cooling the growth in demand for services, which has risen sharply since the lifting of coronavirus-related measures. According to the latest ECB forecasts published last week, we expect the euro economy to stagnate later this week and the beginning of the next. While a decline in GDP in the euro area in the coming quarters cannot be completely ruled out, it does not represent our baseline. We do not expect a decline in GDP for Slovenia either; Model estimates for the third quarter currently point to low but still positive growth. In addition to the baseline, we have prepared an adverse scenario within the Eurosystem, which assumes a complete and permanent interruption of energy supplies from Russia and a partial halt in production in the euro area, according to which real GDP would shrink by 0.9% next year, in contrast to the baseline scenario according to which we expect 0.9% growth. Inflation in Slovenia and the euro area remains high and is expected to remain above our target of 2% for some time to come. For the euro area, inflation is expected to be 8.1% this year and 5.5% and 2.3% over the next two years. In addition to the pandemic, the situation on the commodity market  energy and other  has been further exacerbated by Russia's military aggression in Ukraine. Inflation also reflects the uneven recovery in supply and demand. For example; During the pandemic, there was above-average demand for durable goods, the supply of which was hampered by supply disruptions, and in the last year  after the end of restrictive measures  demand for services, especially travel, increased sharply. Inflation has been rising continuously since the end of 2020. The euro area average was already 9.1% in August, while in Slovenia it climbed to 11.5%. In the light of strong price chain pressures, inflationary pressures continue to spread, with core inflation, which excludes energy and food prices, strengthening to 4.3% in the euro area and 6.2% in Slovenia in August. Inflation is thus becoming more widely based; In addition to energy and food prices, prices of goods and services are also rising steadily. Higher inflation requires a decisive response from the Eurosystem's central banks. Supply shocks cannot be influenced, nor can energy prices. Our task, however, is to consolidate confidence in medium-term price stability through credible and decisive action and to prevent inflation expectations from being broadened. Already in June, our macroeconomic forecasts for the euro area confirmed that inflation would exceed our 2% target over the medium term. As a result, we ended our net purchases under the APP in early July, and raised interest rates by a total of 125 basis points at the July and then September meetings last week, thus exiting the negative interest rate zone. Further interest rate hikes are expected in the future, with the size of the hikes depending on the medium-term inflation outlook. In doing so, we are continuing our transition from a highly accommodative monetary policy stance  amid a protracted period of deflationary pressures and a pandemic shock  to an interest rate range that will ensure inflation returns to our 2% medium-term aim. Interest rate hikes have an impact on broader financing conditions and thus on demand and inflation expectations, which, if they were to be "unwinded", would make it difficult for inflation to stabilise at 2% in the medium term. How have our decisions been reflected in the capital market? Capital markets inform monetary policy on the one hand and reflect its stance on the other. They are one of the key elements in the transposition of central bank decisions into financing conditions and, consequently, the influence of central banks on the macroeconomic environment. Since the July meeting of the Governing Council, borrowing costs have risen further in both the public and private sectors. The increase reflects market participants' expectations that we will continue to raise interest rates in the Eurosystem with a view to containing inflation. Similarly to other euro area countries, the yield on the 10-year bond of the Republic of Slovenia also rose to around 2.6%. The mark-up on the 10-year German bond, which has a yield of around 1.6%, remained at similar levels to the end of July. Borrowing costs for the euro area private sector also increased, both in the bond and equity segments. While the volume of net issuance of private sector shares and bonds remains robust, as does bank lending to non-financial corporations. However, during the normalisation of monetary policy, financial markets may become overly sensitive and spreads may increase. Such financial fragmentation could paralyze the functioning of the monetary policy transmission mechanism. In monetary union, however, it is crucial that our monetary policy stance is reflected in a homogeneous manner across all Member States, which is why we accompanied the July interest rate hike with the announcement of a new monetary policy instrument, the so-called TPI, the transmission protection instrument. In addition, we are already flexibly reinvesting the principal payments of maturing bonds under the PEPP. In the longer term, in order to address the problem of fragmentation, it will be necessary to accelerate financial integration, including the integration of capital markets. An important step is the roadmap to create a Capital Markets Union, a single European capital market. This provides for the unification and simplification of legislation and procedures, including in the area of insolvency, increased transparency and accessibility through a single platform, facilitation of participation for small and medium-sized enterprises, revival of securitisation, strengthening of supervision, harmonisation of withholding taxes within the EU, incentives for so-called longer-term investment funds, and others. From a monetary policy perspective, the CMU also translates more effectively into financial conditions. The deepening of capital markets will increase the share of market-based financing in the financing of the corporate sector in the euro area. As financial market valuations tend to react more quickly to changes in monetary policy, the pass-through of key interest rates to financial conditions would proceed more quickly and potentially have a more effective impact on the real economy. From the perspective of the wider operation of central banks, the creation of a single capital market also has implications for financial stability. The development of a wider range of financial instruments can protect economies from disruptions that may affect the banking sector, thereby enhancing financial stability. At the same time, the need for those non-standard monetary policy measures that undermine bank lending to households and firms is decreasing. In the case of the ECB's instruments, I am thinking primarily of targeted longer-term refinancing operations. From this point of view, the Bank of Slovenia supports efforts to create an effective Capital Markets Union and a robust financial market of the European Union. An integrated and deeper capital market would provide new sources of financing for the Slovenian and European economies. It would make it significantly easier for small and medium-sized enterprises in particular to obtain finance and lower the cost of raising capital, attract more foreign investment and better support long-term projects, including the green transition. It would increase investment opportunities for savers across the European Union and make it easier to invest across borders. A Capital Markets Union will make the European Union's financial system more stable, resilient and competitive. Let me conclude. In the light of persistently high inflation, central banks responded by resolutely normalising monetary policy, which also affects financial and capital markets. The effective and efficient functioning of the European and monetary union will require further integration of capital markets. Pension funds, which are becoming increasingly important as society ages, play a key role in the expansion and deepening of the European capital market. Not only from the point of view of the ageing of the population, but also from the point of view of the development of the capital market, it is necessary or desirable to reform pension systems. Pension funds are one of the most long-term investors and are thus indispensable in financing the decarbonization of society, which is a long-term but inevitable process with long-term projects. Achieving climate neutrality by 2050 will require enormous financial resources that national budgets and banks will not be able to provide on their own. I wish you interesting discussions and pleasant socializing.
text_original: Nagovor Tine umer, namestnice guvernerja, na Konferenci pokojninskega in invalidskega zavarovanja 12.09.2022 / Javni nastopi Velja govorjena beseda Denarna politika in kapitalski trgi Konferenca pokojninskega in invalidskega zavarovanja, Portoro, 12. 9. 2022 Spotovane dame in spotovani gospodje, dragi govorci in organizatorji tega dogodka, dragi gostje, v zadnjih dveh letih je bilo gospodarsko in nanno dogajanje posebej intenzivno. Ob tem ko smo se e borili s pandemijo in njenimi posledicami, je zaetek letonjega leta zaznamoval zaetek ruske vojake agresije na Ukrajino, ki se je razvil v uniujoo vojno in nov ok za naa gospodarstva. Izjemno se je poveala negotovost ter volatilnost na nannih trgih in trgih surovin. Takno okolje je za denarno politiko poseben izziv. Ob vztrajnem zvievanju inacije na ravni ECB nadaljujemo z odlono nadaljnjo normalizacijo denarne politike, ki smo jo prieli konec lanskega leta. Kljune obrestne mere ECB smo prejnji teden dvignili za 75 bazinih tok in s tem prvi po letu 2011 preli v obmoje pozitivnih obrestnih mer. Glede na trenutne gospodarske okoliine je prioriteta denarne politike jasna, kot bom pojasnila v nadaljevanju. Normalizacija denarne politike in spremenjene makroekonomske razmere imajo neposreden in posreden vpliv na nanne in kapitalske trge, o katerem bom spregovorila v drugem delu govora. Dotaknila se bom tudi unije kapitalskih trgov, ki bi pripomogla k razvoju in odpornosti evropskega nannega sektorja in gospodarstva ter podpirala nujen zeleni prehod. Nujen tako zaradi naslavljanja podnebnih izzivov kot zagotavljanja nae energetske varnosti. In pri njenem razvoju imajo eno kljunih vlog tudi pokojninski skladi. Kljub negativnim okom lahko reemo, da sta tako nae kot evrsko gospodarstvo izkazala visoko stopnjo odpornosti. Gospodarsko okrevanje po pandemiji je bilo hitro, mnogo hitreje in moneje od priakovanj. Ekonomske politike, tudi denarna politika, so namre uspele zagotoviti dovoljno mero podpore gospodarstvu, gospodarski subjekti pa so se uspeli relativno uspeno prilagoditi novim razmeram. Ugodna gospodarska rast se je nadaljevala tudi v prvi polovici letonjega leta, in sicer ob rekordno visoki zaposlenosti in nizki brezposelnosti. Vendar se izgledi za gospodarsko rast v Sloveniji in celotnem evrskem obmoju v nadaljevanju leta poslabujejo. Visoke cene energentov, nadaljevanje ruske vojake agresije v Ukrajini ter e vedno prisotne omejitve v dobavnih verigah bodo po priakovanjih vplivali na obutno upoasnitev gospodarske rasti. Zaradi vijih ivljenjskih strokov in negotovosti glede prihodnjih gospodarskih gibanj se ohlaja tudi rast povpraevanja po storitvah, ki je mono poraslo po umiku ukrepov, povezanih s koronavirusom. Po zadnjih napovedih ECB, objavljenih prejnji teden, priakujemo stagnacijo evrskega gospodarstva v nadaljevanju tega in zaetku prihodnjega. Upada BDP v evrskem obmoju v prihodnjih etrtletij sicer ne moremo povsem izkljuiti, vendar ne predstavlja naega osnovnega scenarija. Tudi za Slovenijo upada BDP ne priakujemo; modelske ocene za tretje etrtletje trenutno nakazujejo nizko, vendar e vedno pozitivno rast. Smo pa v okviru Evrosistema pripravil poleg osnovnega tudi neugodni scenarij, ki predpostavlja popolno in trajno prekinitev dobav energentov iz Rusije in delne zaustavitve proizvodnje v evrskem obmoju, po katerem bi se realni BDP prihodnje leto skril za 0,9 % v nasprotju z osnovnim scenarijem, po katerem priakujemo 0,9 % rast. Inacija v Sloveniji in evrskem obmoju ostaja visoka in bo po priakovanjih ostala nad naim ciljem 2 % e nekaj asa. Za evrsko obmoje priakujemo inacijo 8,1 % v tem letu ter 5,5 % in 2,3 % v naslednjih dveh letih. Situacijo na trgu surovin  energetskih in ostalih  je poleg pandemije dodatno zaostrila ruska vojaka agresija v Ukrajini. Prav tako se na inaciji odraa neenakomerno okrevanje ponudbe in povpraevanja. Na primer; v asu pandemije smo nadpovpreno povpraevali po trajnih dobrinah, katerih dobava je bila oteena zaradi motenj v dobavi, v zadnjem letu  po prenehanju omejevalnih ukrepov  pa je mono poraslo povpraevanje po storitvah, predvsem potovanjih. Inacija tako kontinuirano naraa e od konca leta 2020. V povpreju evrskega obmoja je bila avgusta e 9,1-odstotna, v Sloveniji pa se je povzpela na 11,5 %. V lui monih pritiskov vzdol cenovne verige se inacijski pritiski e naprej irijo, mera osnovne inacije, ki izkljuuje cene energentov in hrane, pa se je avgusta okrepila na 4,3 % v evrskem obmoju in 6,2 % v Sloveniji. Inacija tako postaja vse ire osnovana; poleg cen energentov in hrane vztrajno naraajo tudi cene blaga in storitev. Vija inacija terja od centralnih bank Evrosistema odloen odziv. Na ponudbene oke sicer ne moremo vplivati, prav tako ne na cene energentov. Naa naloga pa je, da s kredibilnim in odlonim ukrepanjem utrdimo zaupanje v srednjerono stabilnost cen in prepreimo razsidranje inacijskih priakovanj. e junija so nae napovedi makroekonomskih gibanj za evrsko obmoje potrdile, da bo inacija v srednjeronem obdobju presegala na 2-odstotni cilj. Posledino smo v zaetku julija zakljuili z izvajanjem neto nakupov v okviru programa APP, na julijski in nato e na septembrski seji prejnji teden pa smo dvignili obrestne mere za skupno 125 bazinih tok in tako izli iz obmoja negativnih obrestnih mer. Nadaljnje dvige obrestnih mer priakujemo tudi v prihodnje, pri emer bodo velikosti dvigov odvisne od srednjeronih inacijskih izgledov. Tako nadaljujemo prehod iz izjemno spodbujevalne denarne politike  prisotne ob dolgotrajnem obdobju deacijskih pritiskov in pandemskem oku  v obmoje obrestnih mer, ki bodo zagotavljali vrnitev inacije na na 2-odstotni srednjeroni cilj. Dvigi obrestnih mer vplivajo na ire pogoje nanciranja in s tem na povpraevanje in inacijska priakovanja, ki bi v primeru njihovega razsidranja oteevala stabilizacijo inacije na srednji rok pri 2 %. Kako so se nae odloitve odrazile na kapitalskem trgu? Kapitalski trgi na eni strani informirajo denarno politiko in na drugi strani odraajo njeno naravnanost. So eden kljunih elementov prenosa odloitev centralnih bank v pogoje nanciranja in posledino vpliva centralnih bank na makroekonomsko okolje. Od julijske seje Sveta ECB so stroki zadolevanja dodatno porasli tako v javnem kot zasebnem sektorju. Njihovo zvianje odraa priakovanja trnih udeleencev, da bomo v Evrosistemu nadaljevali z dvigovanjem obrestnih mer, z namenom, da umirimo inacijo. Podobno kot v ostalih dravah evrskega obmoja je porasla tudi donosnost 10-letne obveznice Republike Slovenije, in sicer na okoli 2,6 %. Pribitek nad 10-letno nemko obveznico, katere donosnost znaa okoli 1,6 %, pa je ostal na podobnih ravneh kot konec julija. Porasli so tudi stroki zadolevanja za privatni sektor evrskega obmoja, tako na obveznikem kot delnikem segmentu. Obseg neto izdaj delnic in obveznic privatnega sektorja sicer e vedno ostaja robusten, podobno je z bannim kreditiranjem nenannih drub. V asu normalizacije denarne politike pa lahko prihaja do prekomernih obutljivosti nannih trgov in poveanja pribitkov. Takna nanna fragmentacija bi lahko ohromila delovanje transmisijskega mehanizma denarne politike. V denarni uniji pa je kljuno, da se naravnanost nae denarne politike odraa homogeno v vseh dravah lanicah, zato smo julijski dvig obrestnih mer pospremili z najavo novega instrumenta denarne politike, tako imenovanega TPI, instrumenta za zaito transmisije. Polega tega pa e danes eksibilno reinvestiramo glavnice zapadlih obveznic v sklopu programa PEPP. Na dalji rok bo za naslavljanje problema fragmentacije nujna pospeitev nanne integracije, tudi integracije kapitalskih trgov. Pomemben korak predstavlja nart za vzpostavitev Unije kapitalskih trgov, torej enotnega evropskega kapitalskega trga. Ta predvideva poenotenje in poenostavitev zakonodaje in postopkov, med drugim tudi na insolvennem podroju, poveanje preglednosti in dostopnosti preko enotne platforme, olajanje udelebe majhnim in srednje velikim podjetjem, oivitev listninjenja, okrepitev nadzora, poenotenje davnih odtegljajev znotraj EU, spodbude za t. i. sklade dolgoronejih nalob in drugo. Z vidika denarne politike Unija kapitalskih trgov prinaa tudi uinkoviteji prenos ukrepanja v nanne pogoje. S poglabljanjem kapitalskih trgov se bo namre poveal dele trnega nanciranja v nanciranju podjetnikega sektorja v evrskem obmoju. Ker se vrednotenja na nannih trgih praviloma hitreje odzovejo na spremembe v denarni politiki, bi prenos kljunih obrestnih mer v nanne pogoje stekel hitreje in se potencialno uinkoviteje odrazil v realnem gospodarstvu. Z vidika irega delovanja centralnih bank ima vzpostavitev enotnega kapitalskega trga implikacije tudi za nanno stabilnost. Razvoj irega nabora nannih instrumentov lahko zaiti gospodarstva pred motnjami, ki lahko prizadenejo banni sektor, s imer se krepi nanna stabilnost. Hkrati se zmanjuje potreba po tistih nestandardnih ukrepih denarne politike, ki podirajo banno kreditiranje gospodinjstev in podjetij. Tu v primeru instrumentarija ECB mislim predvsem na ciljno usmerjene operacije dolgoronejega renanciranja. S tega vidika v Banki Slovenije podpiramo napore za oblikovanje uinkovite Unije kapitalskih trgov in trdnega nannega trga Evropske unije. Povezan in globlji kapitalski trg bi namre omogoal nove vire nanciranja slovenskega in evropskega gospodarstva. Zlasti malim in srednje velikim podjetjem bi pomembno olajal pridobivanje nannih sredstev in znial stroke zbiranja kapitala, privabil bi ve tujih nalob ter bolje podpiral dolgorone projekte, vkljuno z zelenim prehodom. Varevalcem po celotni Evropski uniji bi se poveale nalobene monosti in olajalo ezmejno vlaganje. Finanni sistem Evropske unije bo z Unijo kapitalskih trgov stabilneji, odporneji in konkurenneji. Naj zakljuim. V lui vztrajno visoke inacije smo se centralne banke odzvale z odlono normalizacijo denarne politike, ki vpliva tudi na nanne in kapitalske trge. Za uspeno in uinkovito delovanje evropske in denarne unije bo potrebna nadaljnja integracija kapitalskih trgov. Pokojninski skladi, ki s staranjem drube postajajo vse pomembneji, imajo eno kljunih vlog pri iritvi in poglabljanju evropskega kapitalskega trga. Ne le z vidika staranja prebivalstva, tudi z vidika razvoja kapitalskega trga je potrebna oziroma zaelena prenova pokojninskih sistemov. Pokojninski skladi spadajo (spadate) med ene najbolj dolgoronih investitorjev in so (ste) tako nepogreljivi tudi pri nanciranju dekarbonizacije drube, ki je dolgotrajen, vendar neizogiben proces z dolgoronimi projekti. Za doseganje podnebne nevtralnosti do leta 2050 bodo potrebna ogromna nanna sredstva, ki jih dravni prorauni in banke ne bodo mogli zagotoviti sami. elim vam zanimive razprave in prijetno druenje.

Title: Governor for Saturday's annex Governor Botjan Vasle touched on the current situation in his discussion for Delo.
text: Governor's interview for Saturday's Supplement 19.09.2022 / Public appearances Journalist: Miha Jenko; Published: Work, September 17, 2021 Mr. Governor, have you had the last few weeks when you're probably paying bills, shopping at the store, when do you feel like things are getting irritated, too expensive? Of course, I also notice that prices are changing faster than they have in the past. A year ago, could you have imagined the current situation, with record inflation of 11 percent in Slovenia and only slightly less in the euro area  and that the ECB will raise interest rates twice this year? Our baseline scenario of what will happen in the year ahead was, of course, quite different from the current situation last year. A year ago, we could not have imagined that we would have a military conflict on European soil on such a large scale, which would have such drastic consequences for the global energy market and the global food market. The situation has changed significantly, and so have our assumptions, our assumptions and our actions. As a governor, you participate in the Council of the European Central Bank, which last Thursday raised key interest rates for the second time this year, this time by 75 basis points, the most since the introduction of the euro. Was this decision taken unanimously? The debate within the ECB's Governing Council has changed considerably in recent months. Not so long ago, we had the problem that inflation was too low and remained below the target level. During the post-pandemic recovery, prices began to rise gradually, mainly due to the fact that our economies opened up to travel and spend again. This entailed the normalisation of energy prices. Initial inflation was therefore assessed as something that would fade over the months. So as something transitory? Yes. It was about returning energy prices to pre-crisis levels and restoring population consumption. Earlier this year, there were additional shocks in the international environment. The Russian military aggression in Ukraine has significantly changed the trends in the energy and raw materials markets in general, including in the field of food. This has caused inflation to be more protracted and to start spilling over into other areas and into other prices. At that time, the mood within the Governing Council also began to change. A growing number of governors have argued that this kind of inflation will have to be reacted to by changing interest rates. Especially those of us who also have personal experience of our countries with high inflation warned a little earlier that interest rates would have to be changed. The decision we took last Thursday was taken unanimously. How do you see the relationship between pigeons and vultures at the ECB? Where do you fit in your circle of colleagues? With the nature of inflation changing, as inflation increased, as the proportion of goods and services that are depreciated increased, and as the realisation prevailed that there were still many pressures in the background that could affect price growth in the future, sentiment among governors began to change. More and more of us were advocating that we should also start acting with monetary policy. Given my personal experience from two periods of high inflation  in our former country and later in Slovenia before the adoption of the euro  I was among those who began to warn very early on of the danger of rising inflation and the need for action. As a governor, do you vote at all meetings of the Governing Council? A rotation system is in place within the Board of Governors. Which means that the governors do not have voting rights all the time, but these are distributed according to a pre-published voting schedule. In a year, I have no voting rights for two to three months. For example, in September and for the next two months, I do not have the right to vote within the Council. That doesn't mean I don't have the opportunity to present my point of view and defend it  and to influence the debate in that way as well. The fact is that decisions in most cases are taken without a formal vote. The mood, the sentiment, where the majority is leaning, is clear from the debate itself. How will the increase in interest rates be felt in Slovenia, the population and the economy? Loans are and will be, of course, more expensive. What else can we expect? The key implication of both the hikes, as well as those we are planning at future meetings, will be that we will contribute to inflation starting to gradually moderate. And that it will return to our target, to about two percent. With our decisions, we will once again ensure stable price growth and thus a stable financial environment, which is a value for businesses, for the population and also for the state. How concretely will residents feel this? With the gradual normalisation of interest rates, our savings in banks will return to positive interest. So those who save in banks will get interest again.
