Those who have high deposit amounts will come out of negative interest and will no longer pay banks. What does this mean for borrowers? For all those who have loans, it will also end an era when loans, both housing and consumer, were extremely cheap. We will return to a normal situation where credit comes at a price. Yes, but what will be this normalization dynamic, as you call it? We know that the President of the ECB also announced at the last press conference that interest rates will continue to rise. Where will the ECB auction the money? With normalisation, interest rates will reach a point where our policy will no longer be markedly accommodating. At the same time, we do not plan for policy to tighten in order to further hamper economic growth. We are planning a few more consecutive interest rate hikes. However, what that level will be  we have the next meeting in six weeks, then another before the end of the year, and shortly thereafter in early 2023  will also depend on how quickly inflation starts to calm down. Right now, I'm estimating somewhere at the level of two percent. How high do you expect inflation to be in the coming months? A lot will depend on what is happening in the international environment what the geopolitical changes will be. If the situation on the international energy and raw materials market does not deteriorate significantly, our central assumption is that price growth will stop in the coming months and then remain elevated for several quarters to come. In the second half of 2023, we could already enter a period when inflation will gradually moderate. Can you serve concrete numbers? For this year, for the euro area, we forecast that inflation will exceed eight percent, next year it will fall to 5.5 percent, and in 2024 it will be very close to our target with a few tenths above two percent. The trends for Slovenia are similar, as the main factors have a similar impact on all Member States. Inflation is expected to rise sharply this year, at around nine per cent, with a drop below five per cent next year and just over two per cent in 2024. Of course, central banks are also preparing harsher scenarios. Could inflation be noticeably higher than we are feeling now? In the event that the situation in Ukraine were to further aggravate, to lead to additional congestion and turmoil in the commodity and energy markets, this would spill over into their prices and higher inflation in the euro area. The economic outlook in Slovenia and in the euro area is getting worse, and due to record-high inflation, central banks are forced to take action by raising interest rates, which they would not otherwise do in the event of an economic cooling. So how serious is the risk of recession in the euro area now, and also in our country in 2023? The forecasts for Germany are already going in this direction. In terms of economic growth, this year will have two faces. The first half of the year was still very favourable in terms of growth, both in Slovenia and in the euro area. Some indicators suggest that some of this momentum of growth will carry over into the third quarter. However, because of all the risks we have discussed, growth rates will be significantly lower in the coming quarters. Of course, we do not rule out the possibility of a stagnation in economic growth, it may be a quarter when it will even decline. However, on average this year, we expect positive growth in both Slovenia and the euro area. Next year as well, but lower than this year. Then, in 2024, growth could start to pick up again. But to what extent can the ECB and other central banks now have an impact on inflation by raising interest rates? They have no influence on the production, supply and prices of gas, oil, food, which are the main generators of inflation. Nor can they directly address speculators on the energy markets. Hold. It is very difficult to use monetary policy to address one-off shocks, especially those that are temporary. However, our prevailing assessment is that the current inflation has become different and that only one group of products, namely energy products, is no longer being auctioned. Two-thirds of prices are already rising by more than five per cent, meaning inflation has already become broad-based. There are high risks of second-round effects and further pass-throughs of higher prices. It is therefore appropriate and necessary to respond to a situation where we have a combination of supply and demand factors with interest rates. How broadly is the wage-inflation spiral anchored in Slovenia now? In the chain that you mentioned, we are now somewhere in the middle. The primary drivers of inflation that started to emerge last year, through higher energy prices, have already begun to spill over into other commodity prices, and in particular services. The vast majority of the products that make up the consumer price index are now being auctioned. Indeed, there are still limited pressures over wages. We pay close attention to this element. We are showing the first signs in the form of very high demands, but we are not yet at the stage where inflation would also be driven by higher wage growth. Even in some banks, which you are the regulator of, they are already diligently raising salaries, adjusting them for inflation and raising operating costs. How do you track the growth of salaries and costs in banks? At the moment, there are no developments in this sector that are significantly different from other parts of the economy. How solid and liquid are the banks in our country? The indicators of the entire banking system in Slovenia remain stable and solid. In terms of both liquidity and capital adequacy, the developments related to the coronavirus and the Russian military aggression have not worsened the situation in our banking system. Banks' loan portfolios also remained stable. In the last two years, during the COVID crisis, this indicator has even improved for Slovenian banks. Our bankers have been in a bad mood for some time because of your 2019 macroprudential measure, which restricts lending to the population. They say it's an anti-market measure that restricts their business and prevents people from making purchases and investments. How do you respond to them? I believe that the situation we are observing in the country speaks for itself. People have begun to realize that higher interest rates will also mean higher costs of servicing their debt. Our macroprudential measure, adopted years ago, is precisely a response to this changed situation. We already assumed at that time that the low interest rates at the time had a limited lifespan and estimated that there would be a reversal in the economic cycle, so we took this measure to safeguard the financial stability of the system. The measure gave rise to a lot of debate at the time, but now that the situation has changed, it is becoming increasingly clear why we had to adopt it and what we achieved with it. Are you planning any adjustments in the area of macroprudential policy? We are closely monitoring what is happening with banks' portfolios, how the changes will affect their business, and considering whether it may be necessary to change our range of macroprudential instruments. It used to be the case that we had too many banks, that our banking system was too fragmented. This year, there was a quick solution for Sberbank, which landed under the auspices of NLB. Will any further bank rescue operation be needed in the future? Sberbank was a unique bank in terms of ownership. The owners came from Russia, and this was the reason why, after the Russian aggression in Ukraine, there was an increased distrust in this bank. We estimate that this event was unique. Other banks have a different ownership structure and are now operating quite successfully. Therefore, we do not expect similar episodes in the future. As far as the size and structure of the market is concerned, we have an interesting situation in our country. There are a relatively large number of banks operating on the market, and we are at the tail end of the European monetary union in terms of their total assets relative to GDP. We have the relatively smallest banking system in terms of volume. What does this mean? This means that banks operating on the Slovenian market do not manage to exploit their business potential to the same extent as banks in the countries with which we usually compare themselves. We discuss with banks their business models, what services and products they offer to their clients, and apparently this volume is smaller in Slovenia than in other countries. Progress in this area would, in my opinion, be one of the ways to improve this current situation in our market. What do you see as long-term trends in our banking system? Is the so-called consolidation over? My assessment is that the consolidation of the banking system is not yet complete. However, a possible greater concentration in the market will not be enough, it will also be necessary to consider what business strategies our banks have, what else they can offer to the economy and the population. Economic growth will obviously slow down significantly, and the problems of part of the economy will increase with more expensive money. Do you expect more liquidity problems for companies and thus more non-performing loans? One of the consequences of the previous financial crisis was that companies began to behave differently. More and more companies use their own funds for their investments, rather than bank ones, and use alternative sources of financing. They borrow from their business partners, with whom they are involved in supply chains. If we look at the volume of loans granted by Slovenian banks to Slovenian companies today, it is significantly lower than it was in the years before the outbreak of the financial crisis. Nevertheless, it is true that when the economic situation deteriorates, their financial situation usually deteriorates. Is this already happening, is it already known in banks? At the moment, this is not yet known. However, if this changes, the national central banks, and also the ECB at the level of the euro area, now have a very different institutional framework and different, better methods of supervising bank portfolios. We estimate that things will remain manageable. Stagflation is not our baseline scenario, ECB President Christine Lagarde said in an interview with Delo a good four months ago. Is such an assessment still valid for the euro area, is there a need for any correction or addition? Our central scenario remains that we will record positive economic growth this year at the level of the euro area as a whole and that we will continue to have economic growth of around one percent next year. At the same time, we expect inflation to moderate in the coming quarters and to start to decline in the coming year. Of course, this kind of thinking depends a lot on what happens in the international environment. Deviations are possible. We are aware of the great risks that lie ahead, but this is not our central, most likely scenario at the moment. But what are the big risks that you mention now, apart from the consequences of the war in Ukraine, of course? The fact is that in the last two or three years, we are facing two major events that were practically impossible to predict. First, it was the outbreak of the covid crisis. The last time we recorded something similar was a hundred years ago. The second thing was Russia's military aggression in Ukraine. That is, an attack by one superpower on a smaller country on European soil. That hasn't happened for more than 70 years, either. When we talk about what the weaknesses of our economies and the common European economy are, the fact is that the situation is quite different from what it was during the previous economic crisis. At that time, the crisis was caused by imbalances within the economy, by structural problems that had accumulated in our economies. At the moment, however, the biggest risk factor is precisely how the war in Ukraine will unravel. This remains the first and by far the biggest risk. Despite these unique events that we have seen recently, we have shown a great deal of resilience as residents and as our economies and businesses. The overall course of economic growth in recent quarters has been relatively favourable and better than what most expected, first with the outbreak and unraveling of the COVID crisis and then also with the Russian aggression. It is important that, even in the months ahead, we do not underestimate this adaptability of businesses and residents. Can the Bank of Slovenia, as part of the Eurosystem, take any measures to reduce inflation on its own? No, monetary policy remains common. It is decided at the level of the euro area as a whole. The Bank of Slovenia cannot take measures to address inflation on its own. We decide on measures against inflation together, at the level of the Board of Governors. The ECB has also bought quite a few Slovenian government bonds, among others? True, as with other Member States, the size of the purchases was linked to our equity stake in the ECB. What does this mean for the future, since these purchases will obviously be gone? At the moment, we have already stopped making new asset purchases, but we are in the so-called reinvestment phase, when all maturing securities are replaced with new ones. The next logical step is to discuss how to stop this phase of reinvestment. Monetary policy is tightening, money and borrowing are becoming more expensive. What does Slovenia have to pay attention to now as a small and open country? Assuming that we emerge from this crisis situation, which is linked to international events, within a reasonable time, other economic policies, fiscal and income policy, will have to start dealing with structural issues again. Differences in the performance of individual countries will depend on how they cope with the structural changes that we have witnessed in recent years and decades. Two or three questions are constantly on the table here. The first has to do with demographic change, how individual countries are able to cope with the changed demographic picture. The second is how efficient we are in our business, so it's a question of productivity. The differences between countries will result from how we as a whole society are able to produce products and goods efficiently. Both issues are also reflected in public finances. Small countries are particularly vulnerable, so it will be important to maintain the stability and soundness of our public finances in order to protect ourselves against possible shocks coming from the common financial markets. Each country must take care of itself, first and foremost, to keep its fiscal policy under control and within sustainable frameworks. How do you assess our government's responses and actions to inflation and energy and food costs? Do you support a reduction in VAT rates for energy products? Are you in favor of introducing a cap on energy prices? In the initial phase of the energy crisis and the resulting elevated inflation, many governments took additional measures to mitigate the effects of price increases, especially for the most vulnerable groups of the population. In this situation, I believe that these measures were appropriate and that Slovenia is not deviating from this prevailing trend. What about the energy intervention legislation, including the Gas Purchase Guarantee Act, which was unanimously passed by the National Assembly in an extraordinary session on Tuesday? Here, too, in recent months, we have witnessed unique developments as a result of Russian aggression. In principle, we support the response of individual governments and the European Commission. We consider it necessary for these measures to be coordinated between countries, because this is a global phenomenon that cannot be solved at national level. You inherited the problem of expropriated owners of subordinated bank bonds as governor. On Tuesday, the Court of Justice of the EU handed down a ruling on the law on judicial protection for holders of banks' qualifying liabilities. In the BS you note that the judgment supports your views that the law is controversial from the point of view of monetary financing and the financial independence of the central bank. You add that it is necessary to prepare a new law that will comprehensively regulate this area and will be in line with the European legal order and our constitutional system. What solution do you have in mind specifically? It's true that this is an issue that I inherited when I arrived at the bank. At the same time, at the beginning of my mandate, I made it clear that I wanted to contribute to resolving this issue. And how are you going to do it now? My basic orientation is to clear things up. To provide all those who think they have been harmed with a convenient way for the courts, which alone have jurisdiction to address this issue, ultimately decide whether there may have been anything wrong with these proceedings. And whether there may have been any harm. The law drafted by the government at the time was controversial from the point of view of the key principles of the central bank's operation  in our opinion, it constituted monetary financing, but at the same time it interfered with our ability to dispose of reserves and thus our independence in the field of expertise. This was also upheld by the EU Court of Justice on Tuesday. Our contribution is that we have now invited eminent legal experts from Slovenia and abroad to cooperate  to contribute expert starting points for the new law, which would enable those who think they have been harmed to go to court. Namely, a law that will be in line with the Slovenian legal order and the rules of our operation in the euro area. But when will this law be presented to the public, especially to those who feel harmed? The Act cannot be proposed by the Bank of Slovenia and is prepared by the Government or the Ministry of Finance. The proposals, which will be prepared by the aforementioned legal experts, will be part of the considerations that the government will be able to take into account when drafting the new law. Are you currently in contact with the government and the Ministry of Finance in this regard? As usual, we are in contact with both of them, especially with the Ministry of Finance, and in our talks with the Minister so far, we have also touched on the regulation of this issue. Major changes have taken place within the Governing Board of the Bank of Slovenia in recent months. You got a new Lieutenant Governor, one of the Lieutenant Governors resigned at the same time. What is the chemistry in the world now with colleagues coming and going? It is true that as many as three members of the Governing Board of the Bank of Slovenia will be replaced in a short time. One replacement occurred recently, and two calls for the vice governor are currently in the process. From my point of view, it is crucial that the BS Council remains a professional body, that it operates according to professional principles. We managed to do that during my tenure. I expect the world to continue to act on these principles. In January 2019, when you began your six-year term as governor, did you think that such turbulent times awaited you, Slovenia and the euro area in the coming years? No, of course not. My expectation at the time was that I would deal mainly with the normal movement of the economic cycle and the necessary monetary policy response to it. At that time, there were already signs that economic growth could gradually slow down. Of course, no one expected that the coming years would be marked by such huge shocks. The Covid crisis has taken up a huge amount of time in the area of our basic priorities, including the functioning of the central bank. This year, however, Russian aggression has once again completely changed the situation and has led to these major changes in monetary policy that we are witnessing.
text_original: Intervju guvernerja za Sobotno prilogo 19.09.2022 / Javni nastopi Novinar: Miha Jenko; Objavljeno: Delo, 17. september 2021 Gospod guverner, imate zadnje tedne, ko verjetno plaujete polonice, nakupujete v trgovini, kdaj obutek, da se stvari draijo, preve draijo? Seveda, tudi sam opaam, da se cene spreminjajo hitreje, kot so se v preteklosti. Bi si pred letom dni lahko zamislili zdajnjo situacijo, z rekordno inacijo, ki v Sloveniji znaa 11 odstotkov, v evrskem obmoju pa le nekaj manj  in da boste zato v ECB letos e dvakrat krepko zviali obrestne mere? Na osnovni scenarij, kaj se bo dogajalo v letu, ki je pred nami, je bil seveda lani precej drugaen od trenutnih razmer. Pred enim letom si nismo predstavljali, da bomo imeli na evropskih tleh vojaki spopad tako velikega obsega, ki bo imel tako drastine posledice na globalni trg energentov in globalni trg hrane. Razmere so se bistveno spremenile, s tem pa so se spremenili tudi nae predpostavke, naa predvidevanja in nae ukrepanje. Kot guverner sodelujete v svetu Evropske centralne banke, ki je prejnji etrtek e drugi letos dvignil kljune obrestne mere, tokrat za 75 bazinih tok, najve po uvedbi evra. Je bila ta odloitev sprejeta soglasno? Razprava znotraj sveta guvernerjev ECB se je v zadnjih mesecih precej spremenila. e nedolgo nazaj smo imeli teavo, da je bila inacija prenizka in je vztrajala pod ciljnim nivojem. V asu postpandeminega okrevanja so cene zaele postopoma naraati, kar je bilo predvsem posledica dejstva, da so se nae ekonomije odprle, da je bilo spet mogoe potovati in troiti. To je za sabo potegnilo normalizacijo cen energentov. Zaetna inacija je bila zato ocenjena kot nekaj, kar bo z meseci izzvenelo. Torej kot nekaj prehodnega? Da. lo je za vrnitev cen energije na predkrizne ravni in obnovitev troenja prebivalstva. V zaetku letonjega leta so se zgodili dodatni oki v mednarodnem okolju. Prilo je do ruske vojake agresije v Ukrajini, ki je bistveno spremenila gibanja na trgih energentov in surovin nasploh, tudi na podroju hrane. To je povzroilo, da je inacija dolgotrajneja in da se je zaela prelivati tudi na druga podroja in v druge cene. Takrat se je zaelo spreminjati tudi razpoloenje znotraj sveta ECB. Vse ve guvernerjev nas je zagovarjalo stalie, da bo treba na tovrstno inacijo reagirati s spremembo obrestnih mer. Zlasti tisti, ki imamo tudi osebne izkunje naih drav z visoko inacijo, smo nekoliko prej opozarjali, da bo treba spremeniti obrestne mere. Odloitev, ki smo jo sprejeli prejnji etrtek, je bila sicer sprejeta soglasno. Kako vidite razmerja med t. i. golobi in jastrebi v ECB? Kam se v krogu kolegov pritevate vi? S tem, ko se je spremenila narava inacije, ko se je ta zviala, ko se je zvial dele proizvodov in storitev, ki se drai, ko je prevladalo spoznanje, da ostajajo v ozadju e tevilni pritiski, ki lahko vplivajo na rast cen tudi v prihodnje, se je sentiment med guvernerji zael spreminjati. Vse ve nas je zagovarjalo stalie, da zanemo ukrepati tudi z denarno politiko. Glede na moje osebne izkunje iz dveh obdobij visoke inacije  v nai nekdanji dravi in kasneje e v Sloveniji pred prevzemom evra  sem bil med tistimi, ki so e zelo zgodaj zaeli opozarjati na nevarnost razraanja inacije in na potrebo po ukrepanju. Ali kot guverner glasujete na vseh sejah sveta ECB? V okviru sveta guvernerjev je uveljavljen sistem rotacije. Kar pomeni, da guvernerji nimamo glasovalnih pravic ves as, ampak so te porazdeljene v skladu z vnaprej objavljenim urnikom glasovanja. V letu dni tako dva do tri mesece nimam glasovalnih pravic. V septembru in prihodnjih dveh mesecih na primer nimam glasovalne pravice znotraj sveta. To ne pomeni, da nimam monosti predstaviti svojega stalia in ga zagovarjati  in tudi na ta nain vplivati na razpravo. Dejstvo je, da se odloitve v veini primerov sprejemajo brez formalnega glasovanja. Razpoloenje, sentiment, kam se nagiba veina, sta jasna e iz same razprave. Kako bomo zvianje obrestnih mer obutili v Sloveniji, prebivalci in gospodarstvo? Posojila so in bodo seveda draja. Kaj e lahko priakujemo? Kljuna posledica, ki jo bosta imela oba dviga in tudi tisti, ki jih nartujemo na prihodnjih sejah, bo, da bomo s tem prispevali k temu, da se bo inacija zaela postopoma umirjati. In da se bo vrnila na na cilj, na priblino dva odstotka. Z naimi odloitvami bomo spet zagotovili stabilno rast cen in s tem stabilno nanno okolje, ki je vrednota za podjetja, za prebivalstvo in tudi za dravo. Kako konkretno bodo to obutili prebivalci? Nai prihranki v bankah bodo s postopno normalizacijo obrestnih mer zopet pozitivno obrestovani. Tisti, ki torej varujejo v bankah, bodo spet dobili obresti. Tisti, ki imajo visoke zneske vlog, bodo izli iz negativnih obresti in ne bodo ve plaevali bankam. Kaj to pomeni za posojilojemalce? Za vse, ki imajo posojila, se bo prav tako konalo obdobje, ko so bila posojila, stanovanjska in potronika, izredno poceni. Vrnili se bomo v normalne razmere, ko imajo krediti svojo ceno. Da, a kakna bo ta dinamika normalizacije, kot ji pravite? Vemo, da je tudi predsednica ECB na zadnji novinarski konferenci napovedala, da se bodo obrestne mere e naprej viale. Do kam bo ECB draila denar? Z normalizacijo bomo z obrestnimi merami prili do toke, ko naa politika ne bo ve izrazito spodbujevalna. Hkrati ne nartujemo, da bi bila politika zaostrovalna, da bi dodatno zavirala gospodarsko rast. Nartujemo e nekaj zaporednih dvigov obrestnih mer. Kakna pa bo ta viina  naslednjo sejo imamo ez est tednov, nato e eno pred iztekom leta in kmalu nato e v zaetku leta 2023 , bo odvisno tudi od tega, kako hitro se bo inacija zaela umirjati. Trenutno ocenjujem nekje na ravni dveh odstotkov. Kako visoko inacijo priakujete v prihodnjih mesecih? Precej bo odvisno od dogajanja v mednarodnem okolju, kakne bodo geopolitine spremembe. e se razmere na mednarodnem trgu energentov in surovin ne bodo bistveno zaostrile, je naa osrednja predpostavka, da se bo rast cen v prihodnjih mesecih ustavila, nato pa ostala poviana e nekaj prihodnjih etrtletij. V drugi polovici 2023 bi e lahko prili v obdobje, ko se bo inacija postopoma umirjala. Lahko postreete s konkretnimi tevilkami? Za letos za evrsko obmoje napovedujemo, da bo inacija presegla osem odstotkov, prihodnje leto se bo zniala na 5,5 odstotka, v letu 2024 pa se bo z nekaj desetinkami nad dvema odstotkoma e zelo pribliala naemu cilju. Gibanja za Slovenijo so podobna, saj glavni dejavniki podobno vplivajo na vse lanice. Za letos priakujemo visoko rast inacije, na ravni priblino devet odstotkov, prihodnje leto pa znianje pod pet odstotkov, v letu 2024 pa na nekaj ez dva odstotka. V centralnih bankah seveda pripravljate tudi ostreje scenarije. Je lahko inacija opazno vija, kot jo obutimo zdaj? V primeru, da bi se razmere v Ukrajini dodatno zaostrile, da bi prilo do dodatnih zastojev in pretresov na trgu surovin, energentov, bi se to prelilo v njihove cene in vijo inacijo v evrskem obmoju. Gospodarske napovedi pri nas in v evrodeeli so edalje slabe, zaradi rekordno visoke inacije pa so centralne banke prisiljene ukrepati z vianjem obrestnih mer, esar sicer ob gospodarskem ohlajanju ne bi poele. Kako resna je zato zdaj nevarnost recesije v evrskem obmoju in tudi pri nas v 2023? Napovedi za Nemijo e gredo v to smer. Glede gospodarske rasti bo letonje leto imelo dva obraza. Prvo polletje je bilo, kar zadeva rast, tako v Sloveniji kot v evrskem obmoju e zelo ugodno. Nekaj kazalnikov kae, da se bo del tega momenta rasti prenesel tudi v tretje etrtletje. Vendar bodo zaradi vseh tveganj, o katerih sva govorila, stopnje rasti v prihodnjih etrtletjih bistveno nije. Seveda ne izkljuujemo monosti zastoja gospodarske rasti, mogoe bo kako etrtletje, ko bo ta celo upadla. A v povpreju letonjega leta tako v Sloveniji kot v evrskem obmoju priakujemo pozitivno rast. Prihodnje leto prav tako, a nijo kot letos. Potem, v letu 2024, pa bi se rast lahko ponovno zaela krepiti. Do kolikne mere pa lahko zdaj ECB in druge centralne banke z vianjem obresti sploh vplivajo na inacijo? Saj nimajo vpliva na proizvodnjo, dobavo in cene plina, nafte, hrane, ki so glavni generatorji inacije. In tudi ne morejo neposredno nasloviti pekulantov na energetskih trgih. Dri. Z denarno politiko je zelo teko naslavljati enkratne oke, sploh tiste, ki so zaasni. Vendar je naa prevladujoa ocena, da je trenutna inacija postala drugana in da se ne drai ve le ena skupina proizvodov, konkretno energenti. Dve tretjini cen se e drai za ve kot pet odstotkov, kar pomeni, da je inacija e postala ire osnovana. Obstajajo velika tveganja, da bo prilo do sekundarnih uinkov in nadaljnjih prenosov vijih cen. Na razmere, ko imamo kombinacijo dejavnikov ponudbe in povpraevanja, je zato primerno in potrebno odreagirati z obrestnimi merami. Kako na iroko je zdaj plano-inacijska spirala zasidrana inacija v Sloveniji? V verigi, ki ste jo omenili, smo zdaj nekje na sredini. Primarni dejavniki inacije, ki so se zaeli pojavljati lani, prek vijih cen energentov, so se e zaeli prelivati v druge cene proizvodov in zlasti storitev. Zdaj se drai velika veina proizvodov, ki sestavljajo indeks cen ivljenjskih potrebin. Res pa so e vedno omejeni pritiski prek pla. Na ta element smo zelo pozorni. Kaejo se prvi znaki v obliki zahtev, ki so zelo visoke, a e nismo v fazi, ko bi inacijo poganjale tudi vije rasti pla. Tudi v nekaterih bankah, ki ste jim vi regulator, e pridno viajo plae, jih prilagajajo inaciji in viajo operativne stroke. Kako kaj spremljate rast pla in strokov v bankah? V tem trenutku v tem sektorju e ne prihaja do gibanj, ki bi bila znailno drugana od drugih delov gospodarstva. Kako trdne, likvidne pa so banke pri nas? Kazalniki celotnega bannega sistema v Sloveniji so e vedno stabilni in solidni. Tako na podroju likvidnosti kot kapitalske ustreznosti dogajanja, povezana s koronavirusom in rusko vojako agresijo, niso poslabala razmer v naem bannem sistemu. Prav tako so kreditni portfelji bank ostali stabilni. V zadnjih dveh letih, v asu covidne krize, se je ta kazalnik za slovenske banke celo izboljal. Nai bankirji so e nekaj asa slabe volje zaradi vaega makrobonitetnega ukrepa iz leta 2019, ki omejuje kreditiranje prebivalstva. Pravijo, da je to protitren ukrep, ki jim omejuje poslovanje, ljudem pa onemogoa nakupe in nalobe. Kako jim odgovarjate? Ocenjujem, da razmere, ki jih opaamo v dravi, govorijo same zase. Ljudje so se zaeli zavedati, da bodo vije obrestne mere pomenile tudi vije stroke servisiranja njihovega dolga. Na makrobonitetni ukrep, sprejet pred leti, je prav odgovor na te spremenjene razmere. Mi smo e takrat predpostavili, da imajo tedanje nizke obrestne mere omejeno dobo trajanja, in ocenili, da bo prilo do preobrata v gospodarskem ciklu, zato smo sprejeli ta ukrep, da obvarujemo nanno stabilnost sistema. Ukrep je tedaj sproil precej razprave, zdaj, ko so se razmere spremenile, pa postaja vse bolj jasno, zakaj smo ga morali sprejeti in kaj smo z njim dosegli. Ali nartujete kakne prilagoditve na podroju makrobonitetne politike? Pozorno spremljamo, kaj se dogaja s portfelji bank, kako bodo spremembe vplivale na njihovo poslovanje, in razmiljamo, ali bo morda treba spremeniti na nabor makrobonitetnih intrumentov. Vasih je veljalo, da imamo pri nas preve bank, da je na banni sistem preve razdrobljen. Letos je prilo do hitre reitve za Sberbanko, ki je pristala pod okriljem NLB. Bo v prihodnje potrebna e kakna operacija reevanja kake banke? Sberbanka je bila edinstvena banka z vidika lastnitva. Lastniki so prihajali iz Rusije in to je bil razlog, zakaj je po ruski agresiji v Ukrajini prilo do poveanega nezaupanja v to banko. Ocenjujemo, da je bil ta dogodek unikaten. Druge banke imajo drugano lastniko strukturo in zdaj poslujejo povsem uspeno. Zato ne priakujemo podobnih epizod v prihodnje. Kar zadeva velikost in strukturo trga, imamo pri nas zanimivo situacijo. Na trgu deluje relativno veliko tevilo bank, kar zadeva njihovo skupno bilanno vsoto v primerjavi z BDP, pa smo na samem repu znotraj evropske monetarne unije. Po obsegu imamo relativno najmanji banni sistem. Kaj to pomeni? To pomeni, da bankam, ki poslujejo na slovenskem trgu, s svojimi poslovnimi modeli in pristopi ne uspe v enaki meri izkoristiti potenciala za poslovanje, kot to uspeva bankam v dravah, s katerimi se ponavadi primerjamo. Z bankami razpravljamo o njihovih poslovnih modelih, kakne storitve in produkte ponujajo svojim komitentom, in oitno je ta obseg v Sloveniji manji kot v drugih dravah. Napredek na tem podroju bi bil po mojem mnenju ena izmed poti, kako izboljati to zateeno stanje na naem trgu. Kakne vidite dolgorone trende v naem bannem sistemu? Je t. i. konsolidacija konana? Moja ocena je, da konsolidacija bannega sistema e ni konana. A morebitna veja koncentracija na trgu e ne bo dovolj, treba bo razmisliti tudi, kakne poslovne strategije imajo nae banke, kaj e lahko ponudijo gospodarstvu in prebivalstvu. Gospodarska rast se bo oitno precej upoasnila, teave dela gospodarstva pa se bodo ob drajem denarju veale. Priakujete veje likvidnostne teave podjetij in s tem ve slabih posojil? Ena od posledic prejnje nanne krize je bila, da so se podjetja zaela drugae obnaati. Vse ve podjetij za svoje investicije uporablja lastna in ne banna sredstva, uporabljajo alternativne vire nanciranja. Zadolujejo se pri svojih poslovnih partnerjih, s katerimi so vpeta v dobavne verige. e danes pogledamo obseg kreditov, ki jih dajo slovenske banke slovenskim podjetjem, je ta znatno manji, kot je bil v letih pred izbruhom nanne krize. Kljub temu pa velja, da se ob poslabanju gospodarskih razmer obiajno poslaba tudi njihov nanni poloaj. Se to e dogaja, se e pozna tudi v bankah? V tem trenutku se to e ne pozna. e pa se bo to spremenilo, imamo nacionalne centralne banke in tudi ECB na ravni evrskega obmoja zdaj precej drugaen institucionalni okvir in drugane, bolje metode nadzora bannih portfeljev. Ocenjujemo, da bodo stvari ostale obvladljive. Stagacija ni na osnovni scenarij, je dejala predsednica ECB Christine Lagarde v intervjuju za Delo pred dobrimi tirimi meseci. Je zdaj taka ocena za evrsko obmoje e aktualna, je potrebna kakega popravka, dopolnitve? Na osrednji scenarij ostaja, da bomo letos na ravni celotnega evrskega obmoja beleili pozitivno gospodarsko rast in da bomo tudi v prihodnjem letu imeli gospodarsko rast, ki bo dosegla priblino en odstotek. Hkrati pa priakujemo, da se bo inacija v prihodnjih etrtletjih umirila in da se bo v prihodnjem letu zaela zmanjevati. Seveda je takno razmiljanje precej odvisno od tega, kar se bo dogajalo v mednarodnem okolju. Mona so odstopanja. Zavedamo se velikih tveganj, ki so pred nami, vendar to v tem trenutku ni na osrednji, najbolj verjetni scenarij. Katera pa so zdaj velika tveganja, ki jih omenjate, poleg seveda posledic vojne v Ukrajini? Dejstvo je, da se v zadnjih dveh, treh letih sooamo z dvema velikima dogodkoma, ki ju je bilo praktino nemogoe napovedati. Najprej je bil to izbruh covidne krize. Nekaj podobnega smo nazadnje zabeleili pred stotimi leti. Druga stvar je bila ruska vojaka agresija v Ukrajini. Torej napad ene velesile na manjo dravo na evropskih tleh. To se prav tako ni zgodilo e ve kot 70 let. Ko govorimo o tem, kaj so slabosti naih ekonomij in skupne evropske ekonomije, je dejstvo, da je situacija precej drugana, kot je bila ob prejnji gospodarski krizi. Takrat je kriza nastala zaradi neravnovesij znotraj ekonomije, zaradi strukturnih problemov, ki so se nakopiili v naih gospodarstvih. V tem trenutku pa je najveji dejavnik tveganja prav to, kako se bo razpletla vojna v Ukrajini. To ostaja prvo in dale najveje tveganje. Kljub tem enkratnim dogodkom, ki smo jih beleili v zadnjem asu, smo kot prebivalci in kot naa gospodarstva, podjetja pokazali veliko mero odpornosti. Celoten potek gospodarske rasti v zadnjih etrtletjih je bil relativno ugoden in bolji od tega, kar je veina priakovala, najprej ob izbruhu in razpletu covidne krize in nato tudi ob ruski agresiji. Pomembno je, da tudi v mesecih, ki so pred nami, ne podcenjujemo te zmonosti prilagajanja podjetij in prebivalcev. Ali lahko Banka Slovenije kot del evrosistema sama sprejme kak ukrep za znianje inacije? Ne, denarna politika ostaja skupna. O njej odloamo na ravni celote evrskega obmoja. Banka Slovenije sama ne more sprejemati ukrepov, s katerimi bi naslavljala inacijo. O ukrepih zoper inacijo odloamo skupaj, na ravni sveta guvernerjev. ECB je poleg drugih nakupila tudi kar precej slovenskih dravnih obveznic? Dri, enako kot pri ostalih lanicah je bila velikost nakupov povezana z naim kapitalskim deleem v ECB. Kaj to pomeni za naprej, saj teh nakupov oitno ne bo ve? V tem trenutku smo e prekinili z novimi nakupi vrednostnih papirjev, smo pa v tako imenovani fazi reinvestiranja, ko vse vrednostne papirje, ki zapadejo, nadomestimo z novimi. Naslednji logini korak je, da se bomo pogovorili, kako prenehati s to fazo reinvestiranja. Denarna politika se zaostruje, denar in zadolevanje postajata draja. Na kaj mora zdaj Slovenija paziti kot majhna in odprta drava? Ob predpostavki, da bomo v razumnem asu izli iz teh kriznih razmer, ki so povezane z mednarodnimi dogodki, se bodo druge ekonomske politike, skalna in dohodkovna politika, morale spet zaeti ukvarjati s strukturnimi vpraanji. Razlike v uspenosti posameznih drav bodo odvisne od tega, kako se bodo te spopadale s strukturnimi spremembami, ki smo jim pria v zadnjih letih in desetletjih. Dve ali tri vpraanja so tu stalno na mizi. Prvo je povezano z demografskimi spremembami, kako smo se posamezne drave sposobne sooiti s spremenjeno demografsko sliko. Drugo pa je, kako uinkoviti smo pri naem poslovanju, torej gre za vpraanje produktivnosti. Razlike med dravami bodo izhajale iz tega, kako smo kot celotna druba sposobni uinkovito proizvajati proizvode in dobrine. Obe vpraanji se odraata tudi v javnih nancah. Majhne drave smo e posebej izpostavljene, zato bo pomembno, da ohranimo stabilnost in trdnost naih javnih nanc in se s tem zavarujemo pred morebitnimi oki, ki bi prili s skupnih nannih trgov. Vsaka drava mora poskrbeti predvsem zase, da ima svojo skalno politiko pod nadzorom in v vzdrnih okvirih. Kako ocenjujete odzive in ukrepe nae vlade na inacijo in energetsko in prehransko draginjo? Podpirate znianje stopenj DDV za energente? Ste za uvedbo kapice na cene energije? V zaetni fazi energetske krize in posledino poviane inacije so tevilne vlade sprejele dodatne ukrepe, da so ublaile posledice dvigov cen, e posebej za najbolj ranljive skupine prebivalstva. V teh razmerah ocenjujem, da so bili ti ukrepi primerni in v Sloveniji ne odstopamo od tega prevladujoega trenda. Kaj pa interventna energetska zakonodaja, vkljuno s porotvenim zakonom za nakup plina, ki jo je v torek na izredni seji soglasno sprejel dravni zbor? Tudi tu smo v zadnjih mesecih pria edinstvenim gibanjem, ki so posledica ruske agresije. Naeloma podpiramo odziv posameznih vlad in evropske komisije. Zdi se nam potrebno, da so ti ukrepi usklajeni med dravami, ker gre za globalni pojav, ki ga ne moremo reiti na nacionalni ravni. Problematiko razlaenih lastnikov podrejenih bannih obveznic ste sicer kot guverner podedovali. Sodie EU je v torek razglasilo sodbo glede zakona o sodnem varstvu imetnikov kvaliciranih obveznosti bank. V BS ugotavljate, da sodba pritrjuje vaim staliem, da je zakon sporen z vidika monetarnega nanciranja in nanne neodvisnosti centralne banke. Ob tem dodajate, da je nujna priprava novega zakona, ki bo celovito urejal to podroje in bo skladen z evropskim pravnim redom in nao ustavno ureditvijo. Kakno reitev imate konkretno v mislih? Dri, da je to vpraanje, ki sem ga podedoval ob prihodu v banko. Hkrati sem tedaj, na zaetku mandata, izrazil jasno stalie, da elim prispevati k reitvi tega vpraanja. In kako boste zdaj to storili? Moja osnovna usmeritev je, da se stvari razistijo. Da se vsem tistim, ki mislijo, da so bili okodovani, omogoi primerna pot, da sodia, ki so edina pristojna za naslovitev tega vpraanja, na koncu odloijo, ali je bilo morebiti v teh postopkih karkoli narobe. In ali je morebiti prilo do kakrnegakoli okodovanja. Zakon, ki ga je pripravila takratna vlada, je bil sporen z vidika kljunih principov delovanja centralne banke  po naem mnenju je predstavljal monetarno nanciranje, hkrati pa je posegal v nao monost razpolaganja z rezervami in s tem v nao neodvisnost na strokovnem podroju. Temu je v torek pritrdilo tudi sodie EU. Na prispevek je, da smo zdaj povabili k sodelovanju ugledne pravne strokovnjake iz Slovenije in tujine  da prispevajo strokovna izhodia za nov zakon, ki bi tem, ki mislijo, da so bili okodovani, omogoil pot do sodi. In sicer taknega zakona, ki bo skladen s slovenskim pravnim redom in pravili naega delovanja v evrskem obmoju. Kdaj pa bo ta zakon predstavljen javnosti, predvsem tistim, ki se utijo okodovane? Zakona ne more predlagati Banka Slovenije, pripravi ga vlada oziroma ministrstvo za nance. Predlogi, ki jih bodo pripravili omenjeni pravni strokovnjaki, bodo del razmisleka, ki ga bo vlada lahko upotevala pri pripravi novega zakona. Ste v zvezi s tem zdaj v stikih z vlado in nannim ministrstvom? Kot obiajno, smo v stiku z obema, e zlasti z ministrstvom za nance, in v dosedanjih pogovorih z ministrom sva se dotaknila tudi ureditve tega vpraanja. Znotraj sveta Banke Slovenije je v zadnjih mesecih prilo do vejih sprememb. Dobili ste novega viceguvernerja, ena od viceguvernerk je soasno odstopila. Kakna je zdaj kemija v svetu ob prihodih in odhodih kolegov? Dri, v kratkem asu se bodo zamenjali kar trije lani sveta Banke Slovenije. Do ene zamenjave je prilo pred kratkim, dva razpisa za viceguvernerja sta trenutno v postopku. Z mojega vidika je kljuno, da svet BS ostane strokovno telo, da deluje po strokovnih naelih. To nam je v asu mojega delovanja uspelo. Priakujem, da bo svet deloval po teh principih tudi v prihodnje. Ste si januarja 2019, ko ste nastopili estletni mandat guvernerja, mislili, da v naslednjih letih vas, Slovenijo in evrsko obmoje akajo tako turbulentni asi? Ne, seveda ne. Moje takratno priakovanje je bilo, da se bom ukvarjal preteno z normalnim gibanjem gospodarskega cikla in potrebnim odzivom denarne politike nanj. Takrat so se e kazali znaki, da bi lahko prilo do postopnega umirjanja gospodarske rasti. Seveda pa nihe ni priakoval, da bodo naslednja leta zaznamovana s tako velikimi oki. Covidna kriza nam je vzela ogromno asa na podroju naih osnovnih prioritet, tudi pri delovanju centralne banke. Letos pa je ruska agresija spet popolnoma spremenila razmere in privedla do teh velikih sprememb denarne politike, ki smo jim pria.

Title: Address by Governor Botjan Vaslet at the Green Transition Conference: investments and price developments The Bank of Slovenia hosted a conference on the green transition with the European Investment Bank. Speech is only available in English.
text: BANKA SLOVENIJE EV R OS I ST E M Opening remarks by Bostjan Vasle, Governor of Banka Slovenije, at the conference Towards the Green Transition: Investment and Prices 09/29/2022 / Public apperances The spoken word applies. Dear ladies and gentlemen, distinguished guests, it is my great pleasure to welcome you here at the conference on green transition jointly organized with our colleagues from the European Investment Bank. Summer is officially over but this usually pleasant months were also marked by some very unpleasent facts. It was the hottest summer on record in Europe and the third hottest ever globally. It was accompanied by a lack of rainfall, raging fires and receded rivers across the globe. This worsened the European energy crisis and global shortage of staple crops. The end of summer brings new discomfort. As the cold months approach, the key concerns are related to  the security of energy supply  high inflation  and expected substantial slowdown in economic growth. *** Energy and food remain the dominant drivers of high inflation, although the high price growth has increasingly spread to other items as well in the Eurosystem, we have responded by normalizing our monetary policy, first by abandoning net purchases of securities, and from July on, with normalisation of our key interest rates first increases after eleven years. We expect to raise them further over the next several meetings. My impression is that current pace is appropriate response to elevated inflation, and we should continue with it through next few meetings. But that is not the end of normalisation process. Purchases programmes will have to be modified in order to support our efforts to reduce inflation. Our response is critical to reduce inflation pressures and to avoid de- anchoring of inflation expectations and a possible wage-price spiral. *** Our policy, however, cannot address supply-side constraints. The covid- related supply-side disruptions and the Russian invasion of Ukraine exposed fragilities of our food and energy systems, and our high dependence on foreign supply of raw materials and technologies, including those highly important for green and digital transition. The reaction of many firms was an increase in inventories, which added fuel to rising prices. In addition to the diversification of our supply network, sustainable solutions require ramping up investments in renewable energy sources and other production capacities, and development of new, greener technologies and critical infrastructure. And the green transition itself will require significant public and private investments. The European Commission estimates that reaching the 2030 climate target requires additional annual private and public investments of approximately 5 hundred billion of euros. This represents around 4 % of last year's GDP at the EU level an amount that could already trigger a new investment momentum in Europe. *** Such large-scale investments require the mobilization of various funding sources:  from bank lending  capital markets  and public funds. Banks are still the main source of financing for European enterprises. As supervisors, we encourage them to:  systematically assess  disclose  and manage the climate risks in their portfolios. We - central banks - try to be a good example:  in terms of greening of our own investment portfolios  and in terms of disclosure of our carbon footprint. Climate change considerations are also part of monetary policy decisions as they can affect price stability and financial stability for that matter. *** Capital markets are expected to play a key role in mobilising and allocating financing to green projects. After the European investment bank issued the worlds first green bond in 2007, the global green and ESG bond markets have expanded significantly but they still represent a low percentage of new bond issuances. There are plentiful needs and incentives for vast green and other investment but there are also constraints, domestic and those at the global level. *** Dear speakers and panellists, dear guests, I believe that today there will be an excellent opportunity to shed more light on these questions and challenges and to discuss what each of us can - and should - do to contribute to greener and more sustainable policies. By that Im giving the floor to co-hosts of todays conference the European Investment Bank, dear Ricardo, the floor is yours.

Title: Primo Dolenc's address at the Expert Meeting of Members of Supervisory Boards and Management Boards Primo Dolenc spoke about the impact of inflation on monetary policy and interest rate risk at the Expert Meeting of Members of Supervisory Boards and Management Board of Banks, organised by the Bank Association of Slovenia.
text: Address by Primoz Dolenc at the Expert Meeting of Members of Supervisory Boards and Management Boards of Banks 05.10.2022 / Public appearances The spoken word counts. Dear ladies and gentlemen, dear bankers! Thank you very much for inviting me to your traditional meeting, where, as always, current topics and speakers are chosen. I'm supposed to talk about inflation and its impact on monetary policy and interest rate risk in banks. Given that my colleagues will also join the meeting at a later date, who will describe the macroeconomic situation in Slovenia and beyond in more detail and present the Financial Stability Report, I will try to present only a few key highlights on this topic or something more, without going into details. I will therefore present two topics, namely monetary policy in relation to the current economic situation and the impact of the intertwining of these factors on banks' operations, with an emphasis on interest rate risk. In the last two years, two and a half years, economic and financial developments have been particularly intense. While we were still struggling with the pandemic and its consequences, the beginning of this year marked the beginning of Russia's military aggression against Ukraine, which developed into a devastating war and a new shock to our economies. Uncertainty and volatility in financial and commodity markets have increased tremendously. Such an environment is a particular challenge for monetary policy. Amid a steady increase in inflation at the ECB level, we are continuing the decisive normalisation of monetary policy that we started at the end of last year. In September, key ECB interest rates moved into positive interest rate territory for the first time since 2011 with a further 75 basis points. Given the current economic circumstances, the monetary policy priority is clear, as I will explain below, but it has also been made public. Despite the negative shocks, it can be said that both our and the euro area economies have shown a high degree of resilience. The economic recovery from the pandemic has been swift, much faster and stronger than expected. Economic policies, including monetary policy, have managed to provide sufficient support to the economy, and economic agents have managed to adapt relatively successfully to the new situation. Favourable economic growth continued in the first half of this year, with record-high employment and low unemployment. Thus, annual economic growth in the euro area was 3.9% in the second quarter, while in Slovenia it was much higher, at more than 8%, due to a combination of various factors. Private consumption and exports are still important determinants of the economic situation in Slovenia. However, the outlook for economic growth in Slovenia and the euro area as a whole is deteriorating over the course of the year and beyond. High energy prices, continued Russian military aggression in Ukraine and ongoing supply chain constraints are expected to lead to a significant slowdown in economic growth. The higher cost of living and uncertainty about future economic developments are also cooling the growth in demand for services, which has risen sharply since the lifting of coronavirus-related measures. According to the latest ECB forecasts published in September, we expect the euro area economy to stagnate later this year and at the beginning of next. While a decline in GDP in the euro area in the coming quarters cannot be completely ruled out, it does not represent our baseline. We do not expect a decline in GDP for Slovenia either; Model estimates for the third quarter currently point to low but still positive growth. However, in addition to the baseline, the Eurosystem has prepared an adverse scenario that assumes a complete and permanent disruption of energy supplies from Russia and a partial halt in production in the euro area, according to which real GDP would contract by 0.9% next year, in contrast to the baseline scenario of 0.9% growth. Inflation in Slovenia and the euro area has been rising continuously since the end of 2020, remains high and is expected to remain above our target of 2% for some time to come. According to the latest data, inflation in the euro area was 9.1%, with a wide range between individual Member States (it was between 6.5% in France and even over 20% in the Baltic States). In August, inflation in Slovenia was 11.5% higher than in the euro area. In the light of strong price chain pressures, inflationary pressures continue to spread, with core inflation, which excludes energy and food prices, strengthening to 4.3% in the euro area and 6.2% in Slovenia in August. Inflation is thus becoming more widely based; In addition to energy and food prices, prices of goods and services are also rising steadily. Let me also touch on our expectations, which also determine monetary policy. For the euro area, inflation is expected to be 8.1% this year and 5.5% and 2.3% over the next two years. In addition to the pandemic, the situation on the commodity market  energy and other  has been further exacerbated by Russia's military aggression in Ukraine. Inflation also reflects the uneven recovery in supply and demand. For example, during the pandemic, there was an above-average demand for durable goods, the supply of which was hampered by supply disruptions, and in the last year  after the end of restrictive measures  demand for services, especially travel, increased sharply. Higher inflation requires us to react decisively, but it is important to take into account the fact that the nature of inflation is different this time around  it is mainly the result of supply shocks. Supply shocks cannot be influenced, nor can energy prices. Our task, however, is to consolidate confidence in medium-term price stability through credible and decisive action and to prevent inflation expectations from being broadened. Already in June, our macroeconomic forecasts for the euro area confirmed that inflation would exceed our 2% target over the medium term. As a result, we completed net purchases under the APP at the beginning of July, and raised interest rates by a total of 125 basis points at the July and then September meetings, thus exiting the negative interest rate zone. However, it should be emphasised, as bankers are well aware, that even in the current situation, as it was during the pandemic, constructive cooperation between different economic policies will be necessary if we are to achieve the set goal. This time, the responsibility for curbing inflation cannot lie solely with monetary policy. The fact is that many major central banks are responding to the current inflation by raising key interest rates, the Fed and the Central Bank of Australia and the United Kingdom are responding even faster and stronger than the ECB. Given the current macroeconomic outlook in the euro area and the response of other monetary policies, the direction taken by our monetary policy in the coming months is clear. Further interest rate hikes are expected in the future, with the size of the hikes depending on the medium-term inflation outlook. In doing so, we are continuing our transition from a highly accommodative monetary policy stance  amid a protracted period of deflationary pressures and a pandemic shock  to an interest rate range that will ensure inflation returns to our 2% medium-term aim. Interest rate hikes have an impact on broader financing conditions, and thus on demand and inflation expectations, which, if "unanchored", would make it difficult for inflation to stabilise at 2% over the medium term. But how do the current and expected situations relate to the situation in the banking system? Just yesterday, we published the Financial Stability Report, which will be presented to you in more detail later today by my colleague Damjana Igli. If, as the end of the pandemic crisis approached, we expected a gradual normalisation of the situation in the financial system, then of course the Russian military aggression has once again changed the way we think about the risks that the financial system is currently facing and will continue to face in the near future. In general, it can be said that geopolitical tensions in our wider surroundings, and consequently also in Slovenia, result in increased risks to financial stability, only the focus of these risks changes slightly compared to the estimates from a year ago. It is interesting to note that the dichotomy in the view of the situation by supervisors and banks is re-emerging. Supervisors are a little more cautious, but at the same time banks are much more optimistic. But this does not only apply to Slovenia, as colleagues from other countries also make similar observations, and last but not least, the conclusions of our joint forums in which we participate within the EU are similar. Let me just briefly touch on credit risk in this context. The pandemic has significantly increased the credit risk of the banking system, which has not (yet) materialised due to all the economic policy measures and adjustments of banks and, last but not least, bank customers. On the contrary, the share of non-performing loans in Slovenia, as well as in general, has been steadily declining in recent years. However, there is no denying that geopolitical tensions will not have negative consequences for bank customers and the banking system. Although Slovenian banks have relatively little exposure to countries that are in direct conflict, indirect negative effects can be expected. Banks in the European area have responded to this by increasing the share of loans with increased credit risk (the so-called Stage 2 according to IFRS 9), while this share is still declining in Slovenia. Therefore, credit risk management remains one of our priorities in this context as well. Let me move on to the normalisation of monetary policy, the rise in the general level of interest rates and the implications for the banking system. The banking system has undergone significant turmoil and structural changes over the past 15 years. In Slovenia, the assets of the banking system have been completely transformed, with loans to households now predominantly important, but on the other hand, liabilities have also been adjusted in the light of interest rate cuts, and so we currently have 84% of all deposits in the form of insight deposits. In recent years, the net interest margin of the banking system in Slovenia has fallen below 1.5 percentage points, while in 2015 it was over two percentage points, which has strongly determined your business. It is therefore no wonder that in recent years our guidelines and warnings have constantly gone in the direction of rethinking the future of banking, services, products, and business model in general. In this context, I must point out that you have made progress in the banks, which can be a good way forward. Thus, with current forecasts for future interest rates, the outlook for bank income generation is slightly better today than it was months or years ago. If the banks manage to continue with the current pricing policy for loans amid a restrained increase in deposit interest rates and maintain favourable trends in the achievement of non-interest income, then we can expect that the conditions for generating income of banks will improve. Of course, a special question is how the future needs for the formation of impairments and provisions, which have significantly determined the banks' operations in recent years, will develop. However, I would not go back to credit risk, where  as I mentioned a little earlier  our view of the future is more reserved than yours probably is. Let me return to the impact of the interest rate hike on the banking system and say as a starting point that there is quite little hedging against interest rate risk on assets in our country. According to the information we have received from you, only a handful of banks use derivatives hedging, and even then for a small proportion of investments (less than 15% of a fixed-rate portfolio). This is data for the end of last year, so this proportion is now slightly lower. Anyway. A rise in interest rates is likely to have a positive impact on your business, unless there is a significant negative impact through an increase in NPE and value adjustments due to a decline in securities prices. In the first half of 2022, banks' interest rate sensitivity increased mainly due to higher long-term exposures linked to a fixed interest rate (of course, mainly housing and consumer loans), which also increased interest rate risk. Banks still have extensive and currently cost-effective resources to finance long-term investments. Let me mention at this point that although insight deposits pose an inherent risk to bank financing, we nevertheless assess that this risk is quite limited given the habits of depositors in Slovenia and under normal circumstances we do not see a risk of these funds fleeing the banking system. Of course, under normal circumstances, but that can change quickly, as we saw at the beginning of the year. However, given the fundamental part of sight deposits, which is stable and which banks tend to allocate to time pockets of longer maturities when managing interest rate risk, a rise in interest rates could have a positive impact on interest income. The impact on the economic value of capital and net interest income depends, however, to a large extent on the way in which this allocation is made. Given the current structure and trend of changes in the interest rate-sensitive position of the system, the risk is greater in the event of a rapid and strong increase in interest rates, which could be reflected in a faster increase in the price of short-term sources of financing compared to the income of long-term investments, which are largely linked to a fixed interest rate in the long term. Ignoring the uncertain effect on credit risk, an increase in interest rates works in two directions. In the first half of 2022, interest rate hikes have already had a negative impact on some categories of banks' balance sheets. In the first half of the year, there was a significant negative impact on financial assets, which are measured at fair value through other comprehensive income and directly reduce banks' capital. The volume of debt securities in banks' investments, measured at fair value through the second comprehensive return, decreased by EUR 570 million at the banking system level this year, with a total increase of EUR 370 million in the total position of all securities/financial assets held by banks. The negative effects from the revaluation of debt securities were also reflected in the reduction of banks' capital through the accumulated all-encompassing return. Banks recorded a negative result of EUR 144 million in the part of capital where these effects are included, compared to the positive accumulated position of EUR 47 million in December 2021, the difference amounted to EUR 191 million. Due to the negative effects from the revaluation, banks' regulatory capital also decreased and, consequently, the banks' capital adequacy. The simplified calculation shows that, if this effect were eliminated, the capital adequacy of the banking system on an individual basis would be 0.75 percentage points higher than actually achieved in the middle of 2022. If interest rates continue to rise in the second half of the year, further negative effects can be expected in the event of a revaluation of the value of this type of bank investment. On the other hand, we can expect a relatively rapid increase in banks' net interest income in the future, even as the current growth in banks' lending activity slows down. Following the ECB and international financial market interest rate hikes, we can expect an immediate impact on interest income in the second half of the year on the most liquid forms of investment that banks have held in excess reserves until recently. The same applies to loans that are linked to a variable interest rate, the effects of which will gradually be reflected in higher interest income on securities. On the other hand, banks' interest expenditure on deposits from the non-banking sector remains minimal, reflecting an exceptionally high share of insight deposits and low interest rates. The key question here is, of course, how quickly passive interest rates will be adjusted, or how much pressure depositors will put on banks. What is the overall effect, then? Our more detailed assessments or a look ahead will be published after the discussion of the "top-down" stress tests in October, so it is difficult for me to give an estimate for the future at this point. But I can comment on what the effect of a parallel rise in interest rates shows us. With the assumed distribution of the core part of the deposits on view, which follows the Basel guidelines, a parallel increase in interest rates by two percentage points leads to an increase in net interest income. By June 2022, the positive impact had decreased to EUR 226 million, which is 28% less than at the beginning of 2022 and 34% less than a year ago, as a result of the aforementioned increase in the share of loans linked to a fixed interest rate. To conclude  even after the pandemic, which has drastically marked our personal and business lives, the situation is unfortunately not calming down. Economic risks are increasing, inflation is well above our target, and in the euro area, the likelihood of a recession next year is increasing. This is also reflected in the financial system, where the general level of risk is assessed as increased. And this perception is not only ours, but colleagues from the competent EU institutions are also coming to similar conclusions. The normalisation of monetary policy is expected to have a positive impact on banking operations, but it remains unclear how the remaining risks will spill over into the banking system, mainly through the deterioration of loan portfolios. In this part, there is a feeling that the perception of the banking system is more optimistic than ours. Caution should be exercised, as this time the effects of economic policies may not be as successful in limiting the realisation of risks as in the case of a pandemic. However, we have a situation where we are objectively limited on the supply side, where the possibility of reacting quickly with economic policies is significantly more difficult. Therefore, caution and capital conservation in the banking system remain our recommendations in advance. I wish you success and all the best in the future. Thank you very much!
text_original: Nagovor Primoa Dolenca na Strokovnem sreanju lanov nadzornih svetov in uprav bank 05.10.2022 / Javni nastopi Velja govorjena beseda. Spotovane dame in spotovani gospodje, drage bannice in banniki! Najlepa hvala za povabilo na vae tradicionalno sreanje, kjer so kot vedno izbrane aktualne teme in govorci. Jaz naj bi govoril o inaciji in njenem vplivu na denarno politiko in obrestno tveganje v bankah. Glede na to, da se sreanju pozneje pridruijo tudi moji kolegi, ki bodo natanneje opisali makroekonomsko stanje v Sloveniji in ire ter predstavili poroilo o nanni stabilnosti, bom skual predstaviti samo nekaj kljunih poudarkov na omenjeno temo ali e kaj ve, ne da bi se spual v podrobnosti. Tako bom predstavil dve temi, in sicer denarno politiko v povezavi z aktualnimi gospodarskimi razmerami in vpliv prepleta teh dejavnikov na poslovanje bank s poudarkom na obrestnem tveganju. V zadnjih dveh letih, dveh letih in pol je bilo gospodarsko in nanno dogajanje posebej intenzivno. Ob tem, ko smo se borili e s pandemijo in njenimi posledicami, je zaetek letonjega leta zaznamoval zaetek ruske vojake agresije na Ukrajino, ki se je razvil v uniujoo vojno in nov ok za naa gospodarstva. Izjemno sta se poveali negotovost ter volatilnost na nannih trgih in trgih surovin. Takno okolje je za denarno politiko poseben izziv. Ob vztrajnem zvievanju inacije na ravni ECB nadaljujemo z odlono normalizacijo denarne politike, ki smo jo prieli konec lanskega leta. Kljune obrestne mere ECB so septembra z dvigom za dodatnih 75 bazinih tok prvi po letu 2011 prele v obmoje pozitivnih obrestnih mer. Glede na trenutne gospodarske okoliine je prioriteta denarne politike jasna, kot bom pojasnil v nadaljevanju, je pa tudi javno objavljena. Kljub negativnim okom lahko reemo, da sta tako nae kot evrsko gospodarstvo izkazala visoko stopnjo odpornosti. Gospodarsko okrevanje po pandemiji je bilo hitro, mnogo hitreje in moneje od priakovanj. Ekonomske politike, tudi denarna politika, so namre uspele zagotoviti dovoljno mero podpore gospodarstvu, gospodarski subjekti pa so se uspeli relativno uspeno prilagoditi novim razmeram. Ugodna gospodarska rast se je nadaljevala tudi v prvi polovici letonjega leta, in sicer ob rekordno visoki zaposlenosti in nizki brezposelnosti. Tako je bila medletna gospodarska rast v evrskem obmoju v drugem etrtletju 3,9-odstotna, v Sloveniji pa je bila zaradi prepleta razlinih dejavnikov precej vija, in sicer ve kot 8-odstotna. Pomembni determinanti gospodarskih razmer v Sloveniji sta e vedno zasebna potronja in izvoz. Vendar se izgledi za gospodarsko rast v Sloveniji in celotnem evrskem obmoju v nadaljevanju leta in naslednjih letih poslabujejo. Visoke cene energentov, nadaljevanje ruske vojake agresije v Ukrajini ter e vedno prisotne omejitve v dobavnih verigah bodo po priakovanjih vplivali na obutno upoasnitev gospodarske rasti. Zaradi vijih ivljenjskih strokov in negotovosti glede prihodnjih gospodarskih gibanj se ohlaja tudi rast povpraevanja po storitvah, ki je mono poraslo po umiku ukrepov, povezanih s koronavirusom. Po zadnjih napovedih ECB, objavljenih septembra, priakujemo stagnacijo evrskega gospodarstva v nadaljevanju tega leta in zaetku prihodnjega. Upada BDP v evrskem obmoju v prihodnjih etrtletjih sicer ne moremo povsem izkljuiti, vendar ne predstavlja naega osnovnega scenarija. Tudi za Slovenijo upada BDP ne priakujemo; modelske ocene za tretje etrtletje trenutno nakazujejo nizko, vendar e vedno pozitivno rast. Smo pa v okviru Evrosistema pripravili poleg osnovnega tudi neugodni scenarij, ki predpostavlja popolno in trajno prekinitev dobav energentov iz Rusije in delne zaustavitve proizvodnje v evrskem obmoju, po katerem bi se realni BDP prihodnje leto skril za 0,9 % v nasprotju z osnovnim scenarijem, po katerem priakujemo 0,9-odstotno rast. Inacija v Sloveniji in evrskem obmoju kontinuirano naraa e od konca leta 2020, ostaja visoka in bo po priakovanjih ostala nad naim ciljem 2 % e nekaj asa. Po zadnjih podatkih je bila inacija v evrskem obmoju 9,1odstotna z velikim razponom med posameznimi dravami lanicami (ta je bil med 6,5 % v Franciji in celo prek 20 % v baltskih dravah). V Sloveniji je bila avgusta inacija z 11,5 % vija kot v evrskem obmoju. V lui monih pritiskov vzdol cenovne verige se inacijski pritiski e naprej irijo, mera osnovne inacije, ki izkljuuje cene energentov in hrane, pa se je avgusta okrepila na 4,3 % v evrskem obmoju in 6,2 % v Sloveniji. Inacija tako postaja vse ire osnovana; poleg cen energentov in hrane vztrajno naraajo tudi cene blaga in storitev. Naj se dotaknem e naih priakovanj, ki determinirajo tudi denarno politiko. Za evrsko obmoje priakujemo inacijo 8,1 % v tem letu ter 5,5 % in 2,3 % v naslednjih dveh letih. Situacijo na trgu surovin  energetskih in ostalih  je poleg pandemije dodatno zaostrila ruska vojaka agresija v Ukrajini. Prav tako se na inaciji odraa neenakomerno okrevanje ponudbe in povpraevanja. Tako smo na primer v asu pandemije nadpovpreno povpraevali po trajnih dobrinah, katerih dobava je bila oteena zaradi motenj v dobavi, v zadnjem letu  po prenehanju omejevalnih ukrepov  pa je mono poraslo povpraevanje po storitvah, predvsem potovanjih. Vija inacija od nas terja odloen odziv, pri emer je vendarle treba upotevati dejstvo, da je narava inacije tokrat drugana  je predvsem posledica ponudbenih okov. Na ponudbene oke sicer ne moremo vplivati, prav tako ne na cene energentov. Naa naloga pa je, da s kredibilnim in odlonim ukrepanjem utrdimo zaupanje v srednjerono stabilnost cen in prepreimo razsidranje inacijskih priakovanj. e junija so nae napovedi makroekonomskih gibanj za evrsko obmoje potrdile, da bo inacija v srednjeronem obdobju presegala na dvoodstotni cilj. Posledino smo v zaetku julija zakljuili z izvajanjem neto nakupov v okviru programa APP, na julijski in nato e na septembrski seji pa smo dvignili obrestne mere za skupno 125 bazinih tok in tako izli iz obmoja negativnih obrestnih mer. Vendar je treba poudariti, kar banniki sicer dobro vemo, da bo tudi v trenutnih razmerah, tako kot je bilo v asu pandemije, nujno tvorno sodelovanje razlinih ekonomskih politik, e elimo dosei zastavljeni cilj. Tokrat odgovornost za brzdanje inacije ne more biti samo na denarni politiki. Dejstvo je, da se tevilne pomembneje centralne banke na trenutno inacijo odzivajo z dvigi kljunih obrestnih mer, Fed ter centralni banki Avstralije in Zdruenega kraljestva e hitreje in moneje kot ECB. Glede na trenutne makroekonomske izglede v evrskem obmoju in odziv drugih denarnih politik je smer nae denarne politike v naslednjih mesecih jasna. Nadaljnje dvige obrestnih mer priakujemo tudi v prihodnje, pri emer bodo velikosti dvigov odvisne od srednjeronih inacijskih izgledov. Tako nadaljujemo prehod iz izjemno spodbujevalne denarne politike  prisotne ob dolgotrajnem obdobju deacijskih pritiskov in pandemskem oku  v obmoje obrestnih mer, ki bodo zagotavljale vrnitev inacije na na 2odstotni srednjeroni cilj. Dvigi obrestnih mer vplivajo na ire pogoje nanciranja ter s tem na povpraevanje in inacijska priakovanja, ki bi v primeru njihovega razsidranja oteevala stabilizacijo inacije na srednji rok pri 2 %. Kako pa so trenutne in priakovane razmere povezane s stanjem v bannem sistemu? Ravno veraj smo objavili Poroilo o nanni stabilnosti, ki vam ga bo pozneje danes podrobneje predstavila kolegica Damjana Igli. e smo ob priblievanju konca pandemine krize priakovali postopno normalizacijo razmer v nannem sistemu, pa je seveda ruska vojaka agresija ponovno spremenila razmislek o tveganjih, s katerimi se trenutno sooa nanni sistem in se bo tudi v blinji prihodnosti. Na splono lahko reemo, da geopolitine napetosti v nai iri okolici, posledino tudi v Sloveniji, rezultirajo v povianih tveganjih za nanno stabilnost, le teie teh tveganj se nekoliko spreminja glede na ocene izpred enega leta. Pri tem je zanimivo, da se ponovno pojavlja dihotomija v pogledu na razmere s strani nadzornikov in bank. Nadzorniki smo nekoliko bolj previdni, banke pa so hkrati precej bolj optimistine. Ampak to ne velja samo za Slovenijo, saj podobno ugotavljajo tudi kolegi iz drugih drav in ne nazadnje so podobni tudi zakljuki naih skupnih forumov, na katerih sodelujemo v okviru EU. Naj se v tem kontekstu samo na kratko dotaknem kreditnega tveganja. Pandemija je izrazito poviala kreditno tveganje bannega sistema, ki se zaradi vseh ukrepov ekonomskih politik in prilagajanja bank ter ne nazadnje tudi bannih strank k srei (e) ni realiziralo. Nasprotno, dele nedonosnih posojil je v Sloveniji, podobno kot tudi ire, v zadnjih letih stabilno upadal. Vendar pa ne moremo zanikati, da geopolitine napetosti ne bodo imele negativnih posledic za banne komitente in banni sistem. Slovenske banke so do drav, ki so v neposrednem koniktu, sicer precej malo izpostavljene, vendar lahko priakujemo posredne negativne uinke. Banke v evropskem prostoru so se na to odzvale s povianjem delea posojil s povianim kreditnim tveganjem (t. i. Stage 2 po MSRP9), medtem ko pri nas ta dele e vedno upada. Zato tudi v tem okviru ostaja upravljanje kreditnega tveganja ena od naih prioritet. Naj preidem na normalizacijo denarne politike, dvig splone ravni obrestnih mer in posledice za banni sistem. Banni sistem je v zadnjih 15 letih doivel precejnje pretrese in strukturne spremembe. V Sloveniji se je popolnoma preobrazila aktiva bannega sistema z zdaj prevladujoim pomenom posojil gospodinjstvom, po drugi strani pa se je v lui znievanja obrestnih mer prilagajala tudi pasiva in tako imamo trenutno e 84 % vseh vlog v obliki vpoglednih vlog. Bannemu sistemu v Sloveniji je v zadnjih letih neto obrestna mara padla pod 1,5 odstotne toke, pri emer je bila e leta 2015 preko dveh odstotnih tok, kar je mono determiniralo vae poslovanje. Tako ni udno, da so nae usmeritve in opozorila v zadnjih letih konstantno la v smeri premisleka o prihodnosti bannega poslovanja, storitev, produktov, poslovnega modela na splono. V tem kontekstu moram poudariti, da ste v bankah naredili napredek, ki je lahko dobra popotnica za naprej. Tako so  ob trenutnih napovedih glede prihodnjih obrestnih mer  obeti za ustvarjanje dohodka bank danes nekoliko bolji kot pred meseci ali leti. V kolikor boste v bankah uspeli nadaljevati s trenutno cenovno politiko pri posojilih ob zadrani rasti depozitnih obrestnih mer in boste ohranili ugodne trende pri doseganju neobrestnih prihodkov, potem lahko priakujemo, da se bodo pogoji za ustvarjanje dohodka bank izboljali. Seveda je posebno vpraanje, kako se bodo gibale prihodnje potrebe po oblikovanju oslabitev in rezervacij, ki so v preteklih letih bistveno determinirale poslovanje bank. Pa se ne bi vraal na kreditno tveganje, kjer je  kot sem omenil malo prej  na pogled na prihodnost bolj zadran, kot je verjetno va. Naj se vrnem na vpliv dviga obrestnih mer na banni sistem in za izhodie povem, da je varovanja pred obrestnim tveganjem na aktivi pri nas precej malo. Po podatkih, ki smo jih dobili od vas, samo peica bank uporablja itenje z izvedenimi nannimi instrumenti, pa e to za manji del nalob (manj kot 15 % portfelja s ksno obrestno mero). To so podatki za konec lanskega leta, tako da je ta dele zdaj e nekoliko niji. Pa vseeno. Dvig obrestnih mer bo po vsej verjetnosti, e ne bo znatnega negativnega vpliva prek poveanja NPE in popravkov vrednosti zaradi upada cen vrednostnih papirjev, pozitivno vplival na vae poslovanje. Obrestna obutljivost bank se je v prvi polovici leta 2022 predvsem zaradi vejih dolgoronih izpostavljenosti, ki so vezane na ksno obrestno mero (tukaj gre seveda predvsem za stanovanjska in potronika posojila), poveala, s imer se je povealo tudi obrestno tveganje. Banke sicer e vedno razpolagate z obsenimi in trenutno e strokovno ugodnimi viri, s katerimi lahko nancirate dolgorone nalobe. Naj na tem mestu omenim, da eprav vpogledne vloge predstavljajo neko inherentno tveganje za nanciranje bank, vseeno ocenjujemo, da je to tveganje glede na navade deponentov v Sloveniji precej omejeno in v normalnih okoliinah ne vidimo nevarnosti bega teh sredstev iz bannega sistema. Seveda v normalnih okoliinah, kar pa se lahko hitro spremeni, kot smo videli v zaetku leta. Kakor koli, ob upotevanju temeljnega dela vlog na vpogled, ki je stabilen in ga banke pri upravljanju obrestnega tveganja po navadi razporejate v asovne epke daljih ronosti, bi lahko dvig obrestnih mer pozitivno vplival na obrestne prihodke. Uinek na ekonomsko vrednost kapitala in neto obrestne prihodke je sicer v veliki meri odvisen od naina te razporeditve. Ob trenutni strukturi in trendu sprememb obrestno obutljive pozicije sistema je tveganje veje v primeru hitrega in monega zvianja obrestnih mer, ki bi se lahko odrazilo v hitreji podraitvi kratkoronih virov nanciranja v primerjavi s prihodki dolgoronih nalob, ki so v veliki meri dolgorono vezane na ksno obrestno mero. e zanemarimo negotov uinek na kreditno tveganje, zvianje obrestnih mer deluje v dveh smereh. V prvi polovici leta 2022 se je zvianje obrestnih mer e negativno odrazilo v nekaterih kategorijah bilanc bank. V prvi polovici leta je bil pomemben negativni uinek iz naslova nannih sredstev, ki se merijo po poteni vrednosti prek drugega vseobsegajoega donosa in neposredno zmanjujejo kapital bank. Obseg dolnikih vrednostnih papirjev v nalobah bank, merjenih po poteni vrednosti prek drugega vseobsegajoega donosa, se je na ravni bannega sistema letos zmanjal za 570 mio EUR, ob skupnem poveanju celotnega stanja vseh vrednostnih papirjev/nannih sredstev v aktivah bank za 370 mio EUR.
