Prvo je posledica prevrednotenja njihove vrednosti zaradi omenjenega znianja cen ali dejanskega zmanjanja zaradi dospelosti ali prodaje. Negativni uinki iz prevrednotenja dolnikih vrednostnih papirjev so se prek akumuliranega vseobsegajoega donosa odrazili tudi v zmanjanju kapitala bank. Banke ste v delu kapitala, kjer se vkljuujejo omenjeni uinki, zabeleile negativen rezultat v viini 144 mio EUR, glede na pozitivno akumulirano stanje decembra 2021, ki je znaalo 47 mio EUR, pa je razlika znaala 191 mio EUR. Zaradi negativnih uinkov iz prevrednotenja se je zmanjal tudi regulatorni kapital bank in posledino kapitalska ustreznost bank. Poenostavljen izraun pokae, da bi bila ob izloitvi omenjenega uinka kapitalska ustreznost bannega sistema na posamini osnovi ob polovici leta 2022 vija za 0,75 odstotne toke od dejansko doseene. Ob nadaljevanju zvievanja obrestnih mer v drugi polovici leta lahko ob prevrednotenju vrednosti te vrste nalob bank priakujemo dodatne negativne uinke iz tega naslova. Po drugi strani lahko v prihodnje priakujemo razmeroma hitro poveevanje neto obrestnih prihodkov bank tudi ob upoasnitvi trenutne rasti posojilne aktivnosti bank. Po zvianju obrestnih mer ECB in na mednarodnih nannih trgih lahko v drugi polovici leta priakujemo takojen uinek na obrestne prihodke pri najbolj likvidnih oblikah nalob, ki ste jih banke do nedavnega drale v presenih rezervah bank. Podobno velja za posojila, ki so vezana na spremenljivo obrestno mero, uinki pa se bodo postopoma odraali tudi v vijih obrestnih prihodkih iz vrednostnih papirjev. Po drugi strani ostajajo obrestni odhodki bank iz vlog nebannega sektorja minimalni, kar je posledica izjemno visokega delea vpoglednih vlog in nizkih obrestnih mer. Tukaj je seveda kljuno vpraanje, kako hitro se bodo prilagajale pasivne obrestne mere oz. kako velik bo pritisk deponentov na banke. Kaken je potem skupni uinek? Nae podrobneje ocene oz. pogled vnaprej bomo objavili po obravnavi top-down stresnih testov v oktobru, zato ta trenutek teko postreem z oceno za naprej. Lahko pa komentiram, kaj nam kae uinek paralelnega dviga obrestnih mer. Pri predpostavljeni distribuciji temeljnega dela vlog na vpogled, ki upoteva Baselske smernice, pride ob paralelnem dvigu obrestnih mer za dve odstotni toki do poveanja neto obrestnih prihodkov. Pozitiven uinek se je do junija 2022 sicer zmanjal na 226 mio EUR, kar je za 28 % manj kot na zaetku leta 2022 in za 34 % manj kot pred enim letom, kar je posledica omenjenega poveanja delea posojil, ki so vezana na ksno obrestno mero. Naj zakljuim  tudi po pandemiji, ki je drastino zaznamovala nae osebno in poslovno ivljenje, se razmere al ne umirjajo. Gospodarska tveganja se poveujejo, inacija je precej vija od naega cilja, v evrskem obmoju se verjetnost recesije v naslednjem letu poveuje. To se odraa tudi v nannem sistemu, kjer sploni nivo tveganj ocenjujemo kot povean. In ta zaznava je ne samo naa, ampak do podobnih zakljukov prihajajo tudi kolegi iz pristojnih EU institucij. Normalizacija denarne politike naj bi pozitivno vplivala na banno poslovanje, vendar ostaja neznanka, kako se bodo ostala tveganja prelila v banni sistem, predvsem prek poslabanja kreditnih portfeljev. V tem delu vlada obutek, da je percepcija bannega sistema bolj optimistina, kot je naa. Treba je biti previden, saj tokrat ni nujno, da bodo uinki ekonomskih politik tako uspeno zamejili realizacijo tveganj kot pri pandemiji. Vendarle imamo razmere, kjer smo objektivno omejeni na ponudbeni strani, kjer je monost hitre reakcije z ekonomskimi politikami bistveno teja. Zato previdnost in ohranjanje kapitala v bannem sistemu ostajata nai priporoili tudi vnaprej. elim vam uspeno delo in vse dobro v prihodnje. Hvala lepa!

Title: Opening remarks by Vice-Governor Joef Bradeek at the event Statistical Day 2022: In light of price increasesThe event was organized by the Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia and the Statistical Society of Slovenia.
text: Introductory address by Vicegovernor Jozef Bradesek at the Statistical Day 2022: In the light of price increases 12.10.2022 / Public appearances The spoken word counts. Dear Ladies and Gentlemen, Hello. Thank you very much for inviting me to your meeting. I agree with the introductory speakers, who highlighted the topicality of today's event. Inflation should be low, predictable, and stable, but it's none of that. Therefore, inflation has also become relevant to the general public; Households and businesses are already feeling the accelerated price increases in their daily lives, while uncertainty about the future outlook is increasing, especially for those parts of the population that remember prolonged periods of high inflation. Inflation is, of course, always relevant for central banks  institutions whose primary goal is to ensure price stability. The central bank's view of inflation is multifaceted, covering both content and measurement aspects. Both aspects were addressed as part of the ECB's recent review of its monetary policy strategy, including in cooperation with Eurostat. It is interesting to look at the strategy review period, which was marked by low inflation and interest rates, from a current perspective. In these circumstances, a key challenge has been to understand the long-term downward trend in inflation, which has called into question the ability of monetary policy to achieve the 2% inflation target. Particular emphasis has also been placed on measuring inflation itself, which is understandable, given the need for credible, reliable, comparable and time-bound data on inflation for the conduct of monetary policy. Statisticians know even better than central bankers that the quality of inflation data is a major challenge, among other things, due to rapid changes in the set and quality of goods and services, changes in consumption habits and substitution, and the emergence of online trade with different dynamics and inhomogeneity in the price of each product. However, the biggest measurement challenge when reviewing the strategy identified the prices of properties that owners use for their own residence. For the majority of the population, the purchase of real estate represents the most important single expense in life. And due to the rapid growth of real estate prices, coupled with low official inflation, the official measure of inflation and thus monetary policy, at least in some settings, has begun to lose credibility. The lack of a foothold in this area has created a situation in which a significant part of the public disagrees with central banks that prices or the cost of living are rising slowly when real estate prices have been rising at double-digit growth rates for several years. At the same time, this part of the public did not even agree that low price growth would be bad, even if it were credible in their eyes. Finally, a comparison with other central banks of the developed world shows that the inflation indices tracked by central banks typically include the implicit cost of living in their own real estate. The review of the strategy was thus followed by an initiative by EU legislators and statisticians to include residential real estate intended for own use in the ongoing official measurement of consumer price growth. The Eurosystem is aware that both potential ways of measuring the cost of living pose a number of conceptual challenges. While the imputed rent method adequately reflects the value of the service provided by one's own property, it is not based on actual transactions. However, the method based on net purchases, that is to say, actual transactions, also unduly takes into account the investment aspect of own real estate. We are also aware that the production of such homogeneous statistics will pose both technical and operational challenges, for example in terms of time availability, length of time series and comparability between euro area countries, which will have a significant impact on lowering the technical quality of the enlarged consumer price index. Following the publication of the strategy review, the inflation story has been increasingly shaped by the pandemic and, more recently, Russia's military invasion of Ukraine. The outbreak of the pandemic in the euro area triggered a strong response in financial markets at the beginning of 2020. Due to pandemic-related risks, sovereign bond spreads widened sharply, putting pressure on financing conditions. At the same time, companies deprived of cash flow due to restrictive measures increased the demand for loans to address liquidity problems. This adverse situation was reflected in a decline in economic activity and a weak inflation outlook. The ECB's monetary policy response has been decisive. The measures were designed to initially prevent the amplification of the pandemic shock through the financial system and to allow for economic recovery over the rest of the period by providing an accommodative monetary policy stance. The two main instruments used by the Eurosystem to respond to the pandemic in line with these objectives were the pandemic asset purchase programme (APP) and the targeted longer-term refinancing operations, which provided favourable lending conditions for firms and their investment activity. The economic recovery from the pandemic has been swift. In contrast to aggregate demand, the recovery of the supply side tends to be more gradual and largely beyond the reach of cyclical economic policies such as monetary policy. At the same time, the pandemic has severely reduced the supply of some raw materials and temporarily disrupted many supply chains in international trade. These supply disruptions and the imbalanced demand focused on goods led to an increase in the aggregate price index, with the temporary supply-side nature of the shock suggesting that the acceleration in price growth would also be temporary and would fade away as supply adjusts and disrupted supply chains are gradually restored. However, the situation on the supply side, especially in the markets for energy and non-energy raw materials, has been further exacerbated by Russia's military aggression in Ukraine. The situation quickly translated into even higher inflation. It has been growing continuously since the end of 2020 and has already exceeded 10% in the euro area and Slovenia. As mentioned, the main driver of the high price growth was the high growth in the prices of energy products and partly of other raw materials on world markets. Nevertheless, inflation is steadily becoming more broad-based. Core inflation measures, which exclude some of the more volatile components such as energy and food, climbed above six percent in September. The strengthening of core inflation can be attributed to the increasingly intense pass-through of energy prices to other price groups, elevated inflation expectations and labour market conditions with stronger wage growth. A detailed breakdown of inflation confirms the broad basis of inflation: the majority (about 70 percent) of components in the basket of goods and services are growing faster than 2.5 percent on an annual basis; approximately half of the contribution to headline inflation can be attributed to supply factors or negative external shocks, particularly in the energy and food segments; half it stems from demand, which unequivocally indicates a certain persistence in inflation, even if the external situation were to stabilise; This segment is also the only one on which monetary policy can act; Expectations of further elevated consumer inflation are also supported by high producer price increases, which exceed 40 percent, according to data for the euro area. An interesting insight into the expectations of financial markets regarding the further path of inflation is interesting and relevant for monetary policy. The latest official Eurosystem forecasts project inflation to converge to around two percent in 2024. Financial markets believe the official forecasts, at least to the extent that inflation-related financial instruments require money to be invested. For example, inflationary swaps point to a rapid normalisation as early as the second half of 2023. According to pure survey data, according to which inflation is expected to roughly halve in a year, the expected normalization is slower. Higher inflation requires a monetary policy response from the ECB and the Eurosystem. Thus, we ended the summer with net asset purchases, and at the July and September sessions, we also raised interest rates by a total of 125 basis points, thus exiting and moving away from the negative interest rate zone. The rise in key interest rates has been successfully passed on to money market interest rates. Market expectations suggest further interest rate hikes for the remainder of this year and early next year. Current expectations point to a 75 basis point hike again in October, followed relatively quickly by short-term interest rates at levels just below three percent by mid-2023. By taking action, we will ensure stable price growth, which in the medium term ensures adequate operating conditions for both businesses and the population, as well as for the state. We expect that interest rate hikes will continue to pass through to the borrowing conditions of households and corporations in Slovenia. This is because interbank reference rates, such as the Euribor, are to a large extent linked to the key ECB monetary policy rates, while the interbank reference rates are also linked to household and corporate interest rates. On the other hand, with the gradual increase in borrowing costs, interest rates on saved funds in the form of deposits will also rise. I can conclude my speech by concluding that an understanding of inflation dynamics is crucial for the successful implementation of monetary policy. In both respects, the price statistics that you and your colleagues help us develop play a major role. An appropriate inflation measure enables an up-to-date and all-encompassing perception of price pressures that have a significant impact on the decisions of economic agents and on the functioning of the economy itself. At the same time, high-quality and sufficiently granular statistics provide an in-depth understanding of the structural and cyclical factors of inflation dynamics, demand and supply, which is the basis for the formulation of appropriate economic policy measures. Past experience related to monetary policy strategy and the very different current inflation environment demonstrate the need for adjustments in both the measurement and substantive aspects of the understanding of inflation. The cooperation of all participating institutions, statistical institutes and the European System of Central Banks is crucial in this regard. We remain committed and focused on taking the measures needed to converge as quickly as possible to a situation with low, stable and predictable inflation of around two percent.
text_original: Uvodni nagovor viceguvernerja Joefa Bradeka na dogodku Statistini dan 2022: V lui podraitev 12.10.2022 / Javni nastopi Velja govorjena beseda. Spotovane dame in spotovani gospodje, pozdravljeni. Najlepa hvala za povabilo na vae sreanje. Strinjam se z uvodnima govorcema, ki sta izpostavila aktualnost dananjega dogodka. Inacija bi morala biti nizka, predvidljiva in stabilna, vendar ni ni od tega. Zato je inacija postala relevantna tudi za iro javnost; pospeeno rast cen v vsakdanu e obutijo gospodinjstva in podjetja, hkrati pa se poveuje negotovost glede prihodnjih izgledov, zlasti pri tistem delu prebivalstva, ki se spomni dolgotrajnejih obdobij visoke inacije. Inacija pa je seveda vedno relevantna za centralne banke  institucije, ki jim je skrb za stabilnost cen primarni cilj delovanja. Pogled centralne banke na inacijo je veplasten in zajema tako vsebinski kot merski vidik. Oba vidika sta bila naslovljena v sklopu revizije strategije denarne politike, ki jo je nedavno izvajala ECB, tudi v sodelovanju z Eurostatom. Zanimiv je pogled s trenutne perspektive na obdobje pregleda strategije, ki sta ga zaznamovali nizka inacija in obrestne mere. V teh okoliinah je bil kljuni izziv razumevanje dolgoronega padajoega trenda inacije, ki je pod vpraaj postavljal zmonost denarne politike za doseganje inacijskega cilja dveh odstotkov. Poseben poudarek prenove strategije je bil namenjen tudi samemu merjenju inacije, kar je razumljivo, glede na nujnost kredibilnih, zanesljivih, primerljivih in asovno razpololjivih podatkov o inaciji za vodenje denarne politike. Statistiki e bolje kot centralni bankirji veste, da je kakovost podatkov o inaciji velik izziv, med drugim zaradi hitrih sprememb nabora ter kakovosti izdelkov in storitev, sprememb potronih navad in substitucije ter zaradi pojava spletne trgovine z drugano dinamiko in nehomogenostjo cene posameznega izdelka. Kot najveji merski izziv pa so bile ob pregledu strategije opredeljene cene nepreminin, ki jih lastniki uporabljajo za lastno bivanje. Nakup nepreminine za veino prebivalstva predstavlja najpomembneji posamini izdatek v ivljenju. In zaradi hitre rasti cen nepreminin, ob istoasni nizki uradni inaciji, je uradna mera inacije in s tem tudi denarna politika, vsaj v nekaterih okoljih, zaela izgubljati kredibilnost. Pomanjkljiva podlaga na tem podroju je namre ustvarila razmere, v katerih se znaten del javnosti ni strinjal s centralnimi bankami, da cene oz. ivljenjski stroki rastejo poasi, e se nepreminine ve let draijo tudi z dvomestno stopnjo rasti. Ob tem pa se ta del javnosti niti ni strinjal, da bi bila nizka rast cen slaba, tudi e bi bila v njihovih oeh kredibilna. Nenazadnje tudi primerjava z ostalimi centralnimi bankami razvitega sveta pokae, da inacijski indeksi, ki jih zasledujejo centralne banke, tipino vkljuujejo implicitne stroke bivanja v lastnih nepremininah. Pregledu strategije je tako sledila pobuda EU zakonodajalcem in statistikom, da se v tekoe uradno merjenje rasti potronih cen vkljui tudi stanovanjske nepreminine, namenjene lastni rabi. Evrosistem se ob tem zaveda, da oba potencialna naina merjenja bivanjskih strokov prinaata tevilne konceptualne izzive. Metoda imputiranih najemnin sicer ustrezno odraa vrednost storitve, ki jo zagotavlja lastna nepreminina, vendar ne temelji na dejanskih transakcijah. Metoda, ki temelji na neto nakupih, torej dejanskih transakcijah, pa neupravieno upoteva tudi nalobeni vidik lastnih nepreminin. Prav tako se zavedamo, da bo oblikovanje tovrstne homogene statistike predstavljajo tako tehnini kot operativni izziv, na primer z vidika asovne razpololjivosti, doline asovne vrste in primerljivosti med dravami evrskega obmoja, kar bo pomembno vplivalo na to, da bo tehnina kakovost razirjenega indeksa potronih cen nija. Po objavi pregleda strategije sta inacijsko zgodbo vedno bolj krojila pandemija in v zadnjem obdobju ruska vojaka invazija na Ukrajino. Izbruh pandemije v evrskem obmoju je v zaetku leta 2020 sproil moan odziv na nannih trgih. Zaradi tveganj, povezanih s pandemijo, so se razponi dravnih obveznic mono poveali, kar je pritiskalo na pogoje nanciranja. Hkrati so podjetja, ki so bila zaradi omejevalnih ukrepov prikrajana za denarni tok, poveala povpraevanje po posojilih za reevanje likvidnostnih teav. Ta neugodna situacija se je odraala v padcu gospodarske aktivnosti in v ibkih obetih glede inacije. Odziv denarne politike ECB je bil odloen. Ukrepi so bili oblikovani tako, da so prvotno prepreili amplikacijo pandeminega oka skozi nanni sistem in v nadaljevanju obdobja omogoili gospodarsko okrevanje skozi zagotavljanja spodbujevalne naravnanosti denarne politike. Dva glavna instrumenta, ki ju je Evrosistem uporabil za odziv na pandemijo v skladu z navedenimi cilji, sta bila pandemini program nakupov vrednostnih papirjev in ciljno usmerjene operacije dolgoronejega renanciranja, ki so omogoile ugodne posojilne pogoje za podjetja in njihovo investicijsko aktivnost. Gospodarsko okrevanje po pandemiji je bilo hitro. V nasprotju z agregatnim povpraevanjem je okrevanje ponudbene strani obiajno bolj postopno in v veliki meri zunaj dosega ciklinih ekonomskih politik, kot je denarna politika. Istoasno je pandemija mono okrnila ponudbo nekaterih surovin in zaasno prekinila tevilne dobavne verige v mednarodni trgovini. Te motnje dobav in neuravnoteeno povpraevanje, ki je bilo usmerjeno na blago, sta povzroila dvig skupnega indeksa cen, pri emer je zaasna ponudbena narava oka kazala, da bo tudi pospeek rasti cen zaasen in bo izzvenel, ko se ponudba prilagodi in se postopno ponovno vzpostavijo prekinjene dobavne verige. A je situacijo na strani ponudbe, zlasti na trgih energetskih in neenergetskih surovin, dodatno zaostrila ruska vojaka agresija v Ukrajini. Razmere so se hitro odrazile v e viji inaciji. Ta kontinuirano naraa od konca leta 2020 ter v evrskem obmoju in v Sloveniji e presega 10 odstotkov. Kot reeno, je bilo glavno gonilo visoke rasti cen visoka rast cen energentov in delno ostalih surovin na svetovnih trgih. Kljub temu inacija vztrajno postaja vse ira zasnovana. Mere osnovne inacije, ki ne upotevajo nekaterih bolj volatilnih komponent, kot so energenti in hrana, so se v septembru tako povzpele e nad est odstotkov. Krepitev osnovne inacije je mogoe pripisati vse intenzivnejemu prehajanju cen energentov v ostale cenovne skupine, povianim inacijskim priakovanjem ter razmeram na trgu dela z okrepljeno rastjo pla. Podrobna razlenitev inacije potrjuje iroko osnovanost inacije: veina (priblino 70 odstotkov) komponent v koarici blaga in storitev raste hitreje kot 2,5 odstotka na letni ravni; priblino polovico prispevka k skupni inaciji lahko pripiemo ponudbenim faktorjem oz. negativnim zunanjim okom, zlasti v segmentu energije in hrane; polovica izhaja iz povpraevanja, kar nedvoumno kae na doloeno vztrajnost inacije, tudi v primeru, e bi se zunanje razmere umirile; ta segment je tudi edini, na katerega denarna politika lahko deluje; priakovanja o nadaljnji poviani potroni inflaciji podpirajo tudi visoke rasti cen pri proizvajalcih, ki po podatkih za evrsko obmoje presegajo 40 odstotkov. Zanimiv in za denarno politiko relevanten je vpogled v priakovanja nannih trgov glede nadaljnjega gibanja inacije. Zadnje uradne napovedi Evrosistema predvidevajo konvergenco inacije do priblino dveh odstotkov v letu 2024. Finanni trgi uradnim napovedim verjamejo, vsaj v delu, kjer z inacijo povezani nanni instrumenti zahtevajo investiranje denarja. Inacijske zamenjave kaejo denimo na hitro normalizacijo e v drugi polovici leta 2023. Po istih anketnih podatkih, po katerih naj bi bila inacija ez eno leto priblino prepolovljena, je priakovana normalizacija poasneja. Vija inacija terja odziv denarne politike ECB oz. Evrosistema. Tako smo poleti zakljuili z neto nakupi vrednostnih papirjev, na julijski in septembrski seji pa tudi dvignili obrestne mere za skupno 125 bazinih tok, ter s tem izstopili in se oddaljili od obmoja negativnih obrestnih mer. Dvig kljunih obrestnih mer se je uspeno prenesel na obrestne mere na denarnem trgu. Trna priakovanja nakazujejo nadaljnje dvige obrestnih mer v preostanku letonjega in zaetku prihodnjega leta. Trenutna priakovanja kaejo na ponovni dvig za 75 bazinih tok v oktobru, nato pa do sredine leta 2023 razmeroma hitro sledi stabilizacija kratkoronih obrestnih mer na nivojih malo pod tremi odstotki. Z ukrepanjem bomo zagotovili stabilno rast cen, ki srednjerono zagotavlja ustrezne pogoje delovanja tako za podjetja in prebivalstvo kot za dravo. Priakujemo, da bodo dvigi obrestnih mer e naprej prehajali tudi v pogoje zadolevanja gospodinjstev in podjetij v Sloveniji. Medbanne referenne obrestne mere, kot je Euribor, so namre v veliki meri vezane na kljune obrestne mere denarne politike ECB, na referenne medbanne obrestne mere pa so vezane tudi obrestne mere za gospodinjstva in podjetja. S postopnim vianjem strokov zadolevanja se bodo po drugi strani dvigovale tudi obrestne mere na privarevana sredstva v obliki depozitov. Svoj govor lahko sklenem z zakljukom, da je za uspeno izvajanje denarne politike kljunega pomena tako mersko kot vsebinsko razumevanje dinamike inacije. Pri obeh vidikih poglavitno vlogo igra statistika cen, ki nam jo s kolegi pomagate oblikovati. Ustrezna mera inacije omogoa aurno in vseobsegajoo zaznavo cenovnih pritiskov, ki pomembno vplivajo na odloitve ekonomskih subjektov in na samo delovanje ekonomije. Hkrati kakovostna in dovolj granularna statistika omogoa poglobljeno razumevanje strukturnih in ciklinih dejavnikov dinamike inacije, povpraevalnih in ponudbenih, kar je osnova za oblikovanje ustreznih ukrepov ekonomskih politik. Pretekle izkunje, povezane s strategijo denarne politike, in povsem drugano trenutno inacijsko okolje kaejo zahtevo po prilagajanju pri obeh vidikih razumevanja inacije, merskem in vsebinskem. Pri tem je kljuno sodelovanje vseh udeleenih institucij, statistinih uradov in evropskega sistema centralnih bank. Ostajamo zavezani in osredotoeni na sprejemanje ukrepov, ki so potrebni za im hitrejo konvergenco v stanje z nizko, stabilno in predvidljivo inacijo okrog dveh odstotkov.

Title: Primo Dolenc's address at the ACI General Meeting, CroatiaPrimo Dolenc, addressed the participants of the 30th anniversary Annual General Meeting of ACI FMA Croatia. The text is only available in English.
text: BANKA SLOVENIJE EVROSISTEM Keynote speech by Primoz Dolenc at ACI FMA Croatia 10/24/2022 / Public apperances The spoken word applies. Ladies and gentlemen, good morning! First of all I would like to thank the organisers for the invitation to this event. Its good to be here, especially at this specific event - at the 30th Financial Markets Conference which coincides with the upcoming Croatian adoption of the euro. Its also nice to be in Split at this quieter time of year. I am supposed to talk about the Slovenian experience with adopting the euro. However, sharing our experience might have been more useful a couple of years ago, when Croatia was preparing for the euro. Now the preparations are more or less over, and Croatia will enter the eurozone and adopt the currency as of January 1st, 2023, and so we warmly welcome you into the euro family. Even though it has been already 15 years since Slovenia introduced the euro, there are still some valuable lessons from this period. In this speech I will try to share some thoughts on the Slovenian experience of introducing the euro, and then touch upon some contemporary issues regarding common policies in this context. Slovenia introduced the euro on January 1st, 2007, and its experience has long been a case study for other countries aiming to adopt our common currency. It is in fact an interesting example. Slovenia was the first case when euro notes and coins were introduced by a single country in isolation, not joined by others at the same time. And Slovenia was in fact the first country in which the euro was introduced as both book money and cash on the same date, without a transition period. This is the so-called big-bang approach, which was considered the most effective method. As such, Slovenia has been an interesting case study for other countries in the last 15 years, including Croatia, and I am sure our experience has been of much help to our Croatian colleagues while they have been preparing for the introduction of the euro. I am also convinced that the process will be as smooth in Croatia as it was in Slovenia back in 2007. There are some points that need to be emphasised when a country decides to adopt a common currency. What we learned is that preparation is of crucial importance for the success of the project. It was the key success factor in Slovenia. We had at that time a so-called changeover board that conveyed clear messages throughout the process, and this showed a clear commitment to the project at the highest levels of the government and the central bank. Further, according to our experience, one of the key challenges in introducing the euro was explaining the breadth and depth of the impacts of the project to businesses, the public and others. I think the success of our introduction of the euro was also in part based on the fact that the public was very familiar with the currency. And here I think there are many parallels between Slovenia and Croatia, although that familiarity is perhaps now even greater in the latter than it was in the former. When we introduced the euro, the common currency had only been used as physical notes and coins for six years, whereas now it much more widely known, especially due to the fact that Croatia has such strong ties with eurozone countries, and not only due to tourism. Maybe it is strange to mention this, but in Slovenia we had a national campaign that targeted citizens who were most likely to be unfamiliar with the euro. However, I am sure that these groups are smaller and less numerous in Croatia today compared to Slovenia back in 2005 and 2006. At that time it was an interesting supporting factor that many Slovenians already held their savings in euros, often in physical form. This came from the time when we were saving in Deutschmarks, back in the days of Yugoslavia, and having cash under the mattress was nothing unusual. Since we share that sad part of our history, this is probably also true for many in Croatia, even though those years are now more than three decades behind us. The high level of legal certainty during the process was also very important in our case, and I have noticed that Croatia has fully followed our good practice in this regard, and the authorities have defined and communicated to the public the details of the planned changeover well in advance. One of the most interesting issues during the introduction of the euro, and also in the following years, was that of inflation caused by adopting the currency. Because I spend so much time in Croatia in a personal capacity, I have a feeling that the same thing is also happening here. I remember back in the early 2000s, when the euro was first introduced by some EU countries, there was a joke in Germany that the new currency was in fact the teuro - since teuer means expensive in German. The issue of perceived inflation, in contrast to the reality, was also apparent in Slovenia, just as it had been in the first wave countries. Here Slovenia did not fully succeed where others had failed, and thus did not avoid the perceived inflation rate from being higher than the actual rate during the changeover. The perception that some retailers saw the introduction of the euro as an opportunity to put up prices remained. And while this certainly happened in some instances, the statistical evidence shows that this was more the case for services than for goods, although consumers did not make that distinction. I must admit I do not know what the expectations are for inflationary pressures in Croatia with the adoption of the euro, so I can only hope that the authorities have managed to combat idea that the introduction of the euro is inflationary. It is a statistical fact that the effect of adopting the euro on inflation was just 0.3% points in Slovenia, even though public perceptions might have been very different. For a comparison, the introduction of VAT in 1999 had significantly stronger effect on inflation, up 2.5% points in the first year. Turning to a more topical consequence of adopting the euro, this development will further increase Croatias integration with the EU, even though the country had already de facto lost its sovereign monetary policy well before this. This implies that despite a remaining idiosyncratic component, the overall monetary policy will be the same for Croatia as it is for other economies in the monetary union. There is a question, of course, of how such economic policies will react to the specific situation in Croatia. What we found in these last 15 years in Slovenia is that the euro is in fact a good anchor in terms of inflationary pressures. Nevertheless, a common monetary policy does constrain the economic policy spectrum, and many, including in the general public, might argue that with the adoption of a single currency an important part of national sovereignty is lost. This is in a way true, but, to be honest, a small open economy cannot act as if it were an isolated island, even if it has its own monetary policy. In reality, however, there are still some economic policies at the disposal of national authorities, some also at the disposal of national central banks, which can be used to help smooth local economic cycles. Let me focus next on two sets of policies, macroprudential and fiscal. The experience of the first 20 years of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) has shown that the amplitude of the business cycle can be intensified by the financial cycle. Indeed, the severity of the downturn following the global financial crisis across eurozone member states can be traced to excessive leverage. As long as central banks maintain tools to smooth the financial cycle, an important element of absorbing severe shocks or their amplification remains tailored to local economies. The procyclical behaviour of the financial system, and especially of banks, can therefore amplify swings in economic activity. The strength with which the amplification mechanism operates depends on, among other things, financial imbalances accumulated in the pre-crisis period. For example, weakly capitalised banks, when under intense stress from a solvency or liquidity perspective, are more likely to deleverage or sell assets in fire sales, thereby potentially creating further problems in other areas of the interconnected financial system. Such procyclical behaviour among financial intermediaries could significantly amplify the downturn, particularly if these intermediaries become capital-constrained or risk-averse. In response to the global financial crisis, regulators introduced several macroprudential instruments. An important element of the new Basel III regulatory framework is the capital buffers, which are designed to increase banks resilience to macro-financial shocks and reduce procyclicality and excessive amplification of the financial cycle. The two key buffers included in the framework are the capital conservation buffer (CCoB) and the countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB), which ensure that banks have an additional layer of usable capital that can be drawn down when losses are incurred. Buffers for global and other systemically important institutions (G-Slls and O-Slls) and the systemic risk buffer (SyRB) are meant to provide additional loss-absorbing capacity for a specific set of institutions. Further, an additional element in the arsenal of macroprudential instruments are borrower-based measures that directly impose limits on the terms and conditions of lending related to the riskiness of loans. The two most typical examples of borrower based instruments are limits on the loan-to-value (LTV) and debt-to-income ratio (DTI) ratio. Macroprudential policy remains in hands of national authorities. However, under the SSM Regulation, the ECB is responsible for assessing the macroprudential measures adopted by national authorities in the countries subject to ECB banking supervision. The ECB has a top-up right for capital-based measures, meaning that it can impose stronger requirements beyond those any national supervisors propose. A recent episode shows that the ECB and national authorities can work in a coordinated manner. With the outbreak of COVID-19, banks supervised by the ECB were allowed to operate below the level of the Pillar 2 Guidance (P2G) capital and capital conservation buffer (CCoB) requirements. These measures were further enhanced by the relaxation of the countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) by national macroprudential authorities, and also by a relaxation of P2G for banks not under SSM supervision. Such an unprecedented relaxation of capital requirements was taken to support lending and mitigate any second-round effects of the lockdown measures via the banking sector. The second set of economic policies are of course fiscal policies. In an environment of constrained policy space, it is crucial that such policies play a pronounced role in smoothing local cycles. EU fiscal rules should therefore also strive for countercyclicality at the member state level. As a reaction to the global financial crisis, all major central banks resorted to unconventional monetary policies. However, the Eurozone faced a specific challenge in the interaction between the single monetary policy and the varied economic and fiscal positions of member states. This challenge was insufficiently addressed during the first decade of EMU, and was revealed - and, in part, worsened - by the two crises. After the financial crisis, both monetary and fiscal policies were strongly accommodative at the aggregate level in the period 2009-10. However, during the 2012-13 recession, monetary policy offered a stimulus that was modest by historical comparison, while fiscal policy switched to discretionary consolidation to address debt overhang and debt sustainability concerns in the aftermath of the sovereign debt crisis. The analysis of the Eurosystem staff during last years monetary policy strategy review showed that the contribution of discretionary fiscal policies to eurozone core inflation, which had been around 0.3-0.4 percentage points during most of the period of EMU, fell to around zero in the period 2014-15. The SGP aims at a countercyclical fiscal policy, but is not designed to sufficiently support monetary policy in a lower bound environment in which monetary and fiscal policies can become strategic complements rather than substitutes. And finally there are structural policies. It is not only country specific shocks which present an issue, but also common shocks with diverging effects due to the structural heterogeneity within the eurozone. Going forward it will be crucial that the EU works towards structural convergence, which will limit the divergent amplification and transmission of common shocks across the eurozone. Let me stress again, that in joining the monetary union a country does give up a certain degree of sovereignty, but that central banks still maintain important tools which can be deployed to smooth idiosyncratic shocks. In our opinion, and in our experience, the benefits of a single currency far outweigh the costs. Finally, let me briefly touch upon our current monetary policy, which Croatia will soon be part of. Just after our adoption of the euro, the economic and financial crisis hit economies around the world, and soon after the sovereign debt crisis also hit Europe. In that situation I am convinced that Slovenia was better off being part of the broader monetary area that if it were trying to deal with these issues alone. As you might remember, at that time a new era of monetary policy started. Central banks around the world did not hesitate to expand their balance sheets. The first wave of this was after the economic and financial crisis, and the second was more recently, during the pandemic. As a result, the Eurosystem's balance sheet peaked at a previously unimaginable EUR 8.8 trillion at the end of June 2022, and has declined very gradually since. It currently represents a 66% share of GDP. Assets purchased for monetary policy purposes represent around 55% of total Eurosystem assets, while lending operations around 25% of total assets. If we in the eurozone have been battling too low inflation over the last decade, the issue of high, or even too high inflation emerged at the end of last year, and of course things have only worsened in this regard due to geopolitical tensions in Ukraine. With inflation at multi-decade highs in many countries and with risks to the inflation outlook tilted to the upside, several central banks, including the ECB, have started with the tightening cycle of their monetary policy, in terms of both frequency and magnitude of rate hikes. Some central banks have also begun to reduce the size of their balance sheets, moving further toward normalisation of policy. Monetary policy normalisation means a gradual withdrawal of unconventional or non-standard monetary policy measures, which have been used for quite some time. This process began with the ECBs announcement that we would end net asset purchases under the pandemic emergency purchase programme (PEPP) in the first quarter of 2022, and later on the APP programme at the beginning of July. The exit from negative interest rates allowed us to make a transition to a meeting-by-meeting approach to interest rate decisions. The future policy rate path will continue to be data dependent. In July, the GovC also announced a new instrument - the so-called Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI) - with the aim to support the effective transmission of monetary policy. The TPI can be activated to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics that pose a serious threat to the transmission of monetary policy across the eurozone. In the next step, it is expected that we will start discussing the reduction of the balance sheet when the normalisation of interest rates has been completed. There is another important issue I would like to point out. As in many other economic policies, both in Europe and more broadly, we try to include the issue of the transition to a greener economy in our actions. As you probably know, we at the ECB have adopted a new strategy of monetary policy last year that also includes an emphasis on climate issues, and have adopted the so-called ECB pledge on climate change action. Both moves indicate, in fact promise, ambitious steps to further incorporate climate change considerations into our monetary policy framework. Among them are the following: tilting CSPP holdings toward issuers with better climate performance through reinvestments over the coming years, limiting the share of assets issued by entities with a high carbon footprint in the counterparties' collateral pools, and implementing climate-related disclosure requirements for collateral. Let me conclude on this final point. I strongly believe that further Croatian integration into the EU framework will enrich and strengthen not only Croatia, but also the whole eurozone. As such, we look forward to cooperating further with you, and wish you every success in these final preparations for the adoption of the euro.

Title: Address by the Governor on the presentation of the IMF's findings at the conclusion of consultations in Slovenia
text: Address by the Governor at the presentation of the International Monetary Fund's findings at the end of the consultations in Slovenia 21.11.2022 / Public appearances The spoken word counts. Welcome to the press conference at the end of the IMF mission to Slovenia. First of all, I would like to thank the Head of Mission of the International Monetary Fund for preparing (i) an assessment of the current situation, (ii) forecasts of economic developments and (iii) recommendations during this visit. The essence of the Bank of Slovenia's response to the presented findings and recommendations is that we agree with them. We share the assessment that the current economic situation is complex and associated with great uncertainty. Economic growth will moderate this year and even more so next year. However, I would like to point out that we are still talking about a high overall figure for this year, which will remain positive next year, with the recovery from the coronavirus crisis being among the fastest in the euro area. Inflation will remain high this year and next. Our baseline scenario is that it will peak in the coming months, and then by the end of next year it will have already calmed down significantly and will approach our target of 2% in 2024. Regarding the action needed in such a situation, we in the Bank have a similar view as the IMF: in order to calm inflation, it will be necessary to proceed with the normalization of monetary policy: Interest Dimensions move into the restricted area In Other instruments, I would like to mention the reduction in the volume of securities held by the central bank or the ECB. However, action will also be needed on other policies, especially fiscal policies. The tightened economic situation will also be reflected in the banking sector, which is why careful monitoring of the Bank of Slovenia is required, both through microprudential policy measures and macroprudential measures. The current situation in the Slovenian banking system is good: banks are capital-adequate, and liquidity remains high. High lending continues, with existing loans largely compliant  so the share of non-performing loans remains low. During this period, the Bank of Slovenia paid particular attention to energy dependence and dependence on "affected" markets in connection with the Russian military aggression in the supervision of individual banks. With regard to macro-prudential supervision, the measures in place ensure that the most vulnerable are not affected by the deterioration of the economic situation, and that our key objective for the future is to retain capital in banks. The recommendation on the retention of part of the capital in banks, which has been formed in recent quarters, is formulated as an additional safety element for a possible deterioration of the situation. This recommendation will therefore be taken into account in our reflection on the level of capital buffers, which we will carry out in the BS at one of the forthcoming council meetings. Finally, I would like to mention the structural reforms mentioned by the IMF in its report. I am also of the opinion that, in order to increase the potential for growth and thus accelerate the development of our country, it is crucial that, despite the fact that we have been facing major crises in recent years, we also focus on these issues. It will depend on them what our economic development will be in the coming years and thus the quality of our lives.
text_original: Nagovor guvernerja ob predstavitvi ugotovitev Mednarodnega denarnega sklada ob zakljuku posvetovanj v Sloveniji 21.11.2022 / Javni nastopi Velja govorjena beseda. Lepo pozdravljeni na novinarski konferenci ob zakljuku misije IMF v Sloveniji. Najprej bi se rad zahvalil vodji misije Mednarodnega denarnega sklada, da so v okviru tokratnega obiska pripravili (i) oceno trenutnega stanja, (ii) napovedi gospodarskih gibanj in (iii) priporoila. Bistvo odziva Banke Slovenije na predstavljene ugotovitve in priporoila je, da se z njimi strinjamo. Delimo oceno, da so trenutne gospodarske razmere kompleksne in povezane z veliko negotovostjo. Gospodarska rast se bo namre e letos umirila, e bolj pa v prihodnjem letu. Vendar bi elel izpostaviti, da za letonje leto e vedno govorimo o visoki skupni tevilki, ki bo ostala pozitivna tudi prihodnje leto, pri emer je bilo okrevanje po krizi, povezani s koronavirusom, med najhitrejimi v evrskem obmoju. Inacija bo letos in prihodnje leto ostala visoka. Na osnovni scenarij je, da bo dosegla vrh v naslednjih mesecih, nato pa se bo do konca prihodnjega leta e znatno umirila in se v 2024 pribliala naemu cilju, 2-odstotni ravni. Glede ukrepanja, ki je potrebno v taknih razmerah, imamo v BS podoben pogled kot MDS: za umiritev inacije bo treba nadaljevati z normalizacijo denarne politike: obrestne mere se pomikajo v restriktivno obmoje pri ostalih instrumentih naj omenim zmanjanje obsega vrednostnih papirjev, ki jih imamo v lasti centralne banke oz. ECB. Potrebno pa bo tudi ukrepanje ostalih politik, zlasti skalne. Zaostrene gospodarske razmere se bodo preslikale tudi v banni sektor, zato je potrebno skrbno spremljanje Banke Slovenije, in sicer tako z ukrepi mikrobonitetne politike kot tudi z makrobonitetnimi ukrepi. Trenutno stanje v slovenskem bannem sistemu je dobro: banke so kapitalsko ustrezne, likvidnost ostaja visoka. Nadaljuje se visoko kreditiranje, pri emer so obstojea posojila v veliki meri ustrezna  dele slabih posojil torej ostaja nizek. V Banki Slovenije smo v tem obdobju pri nadzoru posameznih bank posebej pozorni na energetsko odvisnost in odvisnost od "prizadetih" trgov v povezavi z rusko vojako agresijo. Ko govorimo o makrobonitetnem nadzoru pa obstojei ukrepi zagotavljajo, da najbolj izpostavljeni niso prizadeti zaradi slabanja gospodarskih razmer, za naprej pa je na kljuni cilj zadranje kapitala v bankah. Priporoilo o zadranju dela kapitala v bankah, ki se je oblikoval v zadnjih etrtletjih, je oblikovano kot dodatni varnostni element za morebitno poslabanje razmer. To priporoilo bomo tako upotevali pri naem razmisleku o viini kapitalskih blailnikov, ki jo bomo v BS opravili na eni izmed prihodnjih sej sveta. Na koncu bi omenil e strukturne reforme, ki jih je v svojem poroilu navedel MDS. Tudi moje mnenje je, da je za poveanje potenciala za rast in s tem hitreji razvoj nae drave kljunega pomena, da se, kljub temu da se v zadnjih letih sreujemo z velikimi krizami, osredotoimo tudi na ta vpraanja. Od njih bo namre odvisno, kaken bo na gospodarski razvoj v prihodnjih letih in s tem kakovost naega ivljenja.

Title: Address by the Governor at the event Bulgaria in the Eurozone  Benefits and OpportunitiesThe Governor participated in the panel entitled Adopting the Euro  relevant experiences and the way forward. He outlined the challenges we faced when adopting the euro in Slovenia and outlined the main factors that contributed to Slovenia's success in adopting the euro in such a short period of time. Speech is only available in English.
text: BANKA SLOVENIJE EVROSISTEM Governor's address at the event Bulgaria in the Eurozone - Benefits and Opportunities 12/09/2022 / Public apperances The spoken word applies. This year, on the twentieth anniversary of the introduction of euro banknotes and coins, we received good news regarding the further enlargement of the euro area. I am pleased that not only will theeuro family grow to include Croatia in less than a month, but that adoption of the euro has also been announced as a priority for Bulgaria.[1] The further expansion of the euro areastrengthens the international role of the euro and the euro economy, and adds to the economic resilience of the EU, which is of particular importance in a world of increased geopolitical tensions. We are only as strong as we are united, if I may borrow J.K. Rowlings words. And the public seem to agree on this, if we are to judge from the results of the most recent (November) Eurobarometer survey, showing one of the highest ever approval rates for the euro. The common currency is perceived as a good thing for the EU by almost 8 out of 10 EU citizens, with Slovenians being among the top supporters of the euro.[2] Slovenia adopted the euro more than fifteen years ago. In January 2007 we joined the euro area as the 13th EU Member State, which was in this case actually a lucky number. Slovenia was the first of the so-called new EU member states to adopt the currency. It was also the first country in which the eurcwas introduced as book money and as cash on the same date, without a 3-year transitional period typical for the previous euro adopters. Slovenia's adoption of the euro thus represented an interesting case study for other new EU member states. Our positive experience with the so-called "big bang" approach confirmed its status as the favoured option compared to a phase-out scenario with a transitional period for legal documents to be denoted in euros.[3] Slovenia adopted the euro less than three years after joining the EU. Regarding the Maastricht convergence criteria, inflation was the biggest challenge. With a combination of disinflationary monetary[4] and fiscal policies and pro- market structural reforms - including de-indexation of wages and contracts[5] - in just six years (2000-2006) Slovenia managed to reduce inflation from almost 9% to just over 2%, and long-term interest rates from almost 10% to below 4%, very close to the euro area average. At the same time economic growth remained relatively robust. The depreciation of the Slovene tolar, typical of the previous decade, was eliminated only gradually. The strategy of gradual stabilisation of the exchange rate of the tolar against the eurc[6] prolonged the disinflation process for a couple of years, but it may have facilitated the adjustment of the real economy. There were several success factors for the swift and smooth introduction of the euro in Slovenia. First and probably most important was the unified pro-euro attitude of policy makers, political parties and professionals, and a commitment to reforms and the achievement of the Maastricht criteria. Another crucial factor was thecomprehensive preparations starting three years in advance, along with good project management. These preparations concerned two overarching areas. One was the technical aspect of the changeover in the public and private sector (including adopting and adjusting the relevant legislation, setting up a 16-month mandatory dual display of prices in tolars and euros, adjustments of IT systems, conversion of ATMs and POS terminals, frontloading of euro banknotes, etc). Another success factor was agood communication strategy, with timely sharing of the details of the national changeover plan with the private sector, targeted training, a dedicated web page, strong advertising campaign and the distribution of euro calculators among households. The familiarity of Slovenes with the euro also played an important role. Specifically, the euro was already legal tender in neighbouring Austria and Italy, and many Slovenians already held a significant part of their savings in euros, a phenomenon which had roots in the former state of Yugoslavia, where low trust in the dinar as a store of value lead to massive savings in Deutschmarks. All these factors contributed to strong public support for the euro. In the 2006 Eurobarometer survey, 72% of Slovenes welcomed the introduction of the currency. This number then rose further after the adoption of the euro, showing that people's positive expectations had been satisfied. The euro, which has become part of the European identity, has brought us many economic and other benefits[7] Accession to the EU and the decision to adopt the euro were supportive of the momentum to reform and contributed to greater stability of the economic environment. Euro adoption simplified our lives by increasing the transparency of prices and reducing both transaction costs and exposure to exchange rate fluctuations. It made it easier and cheaper for business to trade and invest across borders, and contributed to the rise in the volume of international trade in Slovenia. On joining the euro area Slovenia imported the ECB's credibility, which helped ease the countrys access to capital markets and reduce the cost of funding and its volatility. Being part of the larger currency union in general mitigates the impact of external shocks on our small open economy. [8] This was also the case during the covid crisis and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, when with our own currency we would probably have faced greater depreciation and inflationary pressures and more volatile and less favourable financing conditions. Like the euro coin, membership in the euro area has two sides, advantages and challenges. A challenge often exposed is that a countrygives up the independence to formulate its own monetary policy, which can complicate its adjustment to shocks. I would add two thoughts to this. First, this challenge can also be an opportunity for a country to reform, to increase its flexibility and resilience to shocks and build up shock absorption capacity. Second, even in small open economies with their own currencies, the scope for independent monetary policy is limited, as in this highly integrated world such nations will still be importing the monetary stances of major central banks. Another challenge, related to gaining public support for the adoption of the euro, is the fear of price increases at the time of the changeover Upon the introduction of the euro in Germany, there was a joke that the name of the new currency was actually teuro, as teuer means expensive in German. In Slovenia, the adoption of the eurodid not cause a significant change in the general level of prices, but it had a more significant effect on the prices of some items, especially catering services and products with low prices, as well due to the effects of rounding up. This is probably why the public perception of price increases is generally higher than the reality. The short-term effect is estimated at 0.3 percentage points, while the medium-term effect is more difficult to estimate due to many overlapping factors. The last challenge I would touch upon is related todealing with improved access to cross-border funding and the lowering of interest rates, after Slovenia entered the ERM 2. Domestic bank borrowing on international wholesale markets quadrupled in the period from 2004-2008,[9] which allowed the rapid expansion of bank lending to firms and households.[1Q] This contributed to the overheating of the economy, especially in the construction and real estate sectors, and - together with bank financing of management buyouts -contributed significantly to the banking and public finance crisis. The global financial crisis revealed the shortcomings of banking regulation and oversight in the euro area in general, and prompted comprehensive EU reforms in this regard. Bulgaria's steps towards adopting the euro thus take place in a strengthened institutional framework.[11] To sum up. Two of the key factors for the successful adoption of the euro in Slovenia were - in addition to thorough preparations - broad social consensus[12] and credible communication from key stakeholders. Adoption of the euro brings both opportunities and challenges. In the case of Slovenia, the opportunities prevailed. The institutional framework of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is not yet complete, and with further progress in this area I anticipate that the scale will tip even more in favour of the benefits of joining the single currency. [1] In spring 2022 Bulgaria adopted a national changeover plan, and in October 2022 it announced its blueprint for adopting the euro. [2] Flash Eurobarometer 512: The euro area (Nov. 2022). [3] Deloitte (2007) for the Commission: Review of the Slovenian changeover to the euro; Scenarios for adopting the euro (europa.eu). [4] ECB (2006): During the period after ERM 211 entry, Banka Slovenije used its foreign exchange swap facility to maintain the stability of the euro-tolar exchange rate while keeping domestic interest rates above those in the euro area. This policy, which translated into a high short-term interest rate differential with the euro area, facilitated the disinflationary process. [5] Plus liberalisation of capital flows, prices and some other parts of the economy. [6] This was ensured by the use of foreign exchange swap arrangements with commercial banks while maintaining our short-time interest rates above those in the euro area before adopting the euro, limiting the possibility of an excessive aggregate demand and consequent inflationary pressures. Banka Slovenije je pospesevala inflacijo (finance.si) [7] Benefits (europa.eu); A decade of euro in Slovenia (stat.si). [8] 20 years of the euro - and now? (swp-berlin.org); How Countries Should Respond to the Strong Dollar (imf.org). [9] Domestic banks increased their exposure to foreign banks from less than EUR 4 billion to more than EUR 16 billion. [10] The growth in the volume of loans to the non-banking sector was almost three times that of the euro area. [11] As for banks, today we have stricter capital and liquidity requirements and a joint Supervisory Mechanism in which Bulgaria is already taking part. [12] Among important challenges in Bulgaria are political instability and low public support for the euro (supported by merely 40% of citizens, one of the lowest shares in the EU, after DK, SE and CZ).

Title: Governor statement following the Governing Council's monetary meetingThe members of the Governing Council decided yesterday to take further action on monetary policy. For the fourth time in a row, we raised our key interest rates, this time by 0.5 pps. We continued to normalise monetary policy on other instruments; We presented a framework for reducing the amount of securities purchased in previous years.
text: BANKA SLOVENIJE EVROSISTEM Governors statement following the ECBs monetary policy meeting 12/16/2022 / Press release Economic growth in the euro area will slow from 3.4% this year to 0.5% next year, before rising again to 1.9% and 1.8% over the next two years. The projections, which members of Governing Council of the ECB were briefed on yesterday, also assume that inflation will remain close to its current level for several months. It will then begin to gradually decline, but the decline over the entire projection horizon will be slower than forecast even in the autumn. In light of these projections, the Governing Council yesterday opted for further action. We raised our key interest rates for the fourth meeting in a row, by 0.5 percentage points on this occasion. Monetary policy normalisation was also continued via other instruments., and the framework for reducing the portfolio of securities purchased in previous years was outlined. The Governing Council decided to raise all three key ECB interest rates by 50 basis points. Given the substantial upward revision to the inflation outlook, our expectation is that interest rates will have to rise further before hitting a level that is sufficiently restrictive to ensure that inflation returns as quickly as possible to its 2% target over the medium term. Yesterdays discussions also addressed how to normalise the monetary policy securities portfolios. The decision was taken that as of the beginning of March 2023 we will no longer reinvest all principal payments from maturing securities under the APP. The APP portfolio will be reduced at a measured and predictable pace. The decline will amount to EUR 15 billion per month on average until the end of the second quarter of 2023. The subsequent pace of reduction will be determined over time, to ensure it remains consistent with the overall monetary policy strategy and stance, to preserve market functioning, and to maintain firm control over short-term money market conditions. By the end of 2023 we will also review the operational framework for steering short-term interest rates, which will provide information regarding the endpoint of the balance sheet normalisation process. The principal payments from maturing securities under the PEPP will be reinvested until at least the end of 2024. The latest forecasts discussed by the members of the Governing Council at yesterdays meeting suggest that economic growth in the euro area will be lower next year than previously forecast, while inflation will be higher over the projection horizon. According to the core projection, economic growth will slow from 3.4% this year to 0.5% next year, before strengthening again to 1.9% in 2024 and 1.8% in 2025. Inflation is expected to persist close to the current levels for some time yet, before beginning to fall more significantly next year under the assumption of the stabilisation of the energy markets, the elimination of disruptions to supply chains, and the normalisation of cost pressures, but will remain higher over the entire projection horizon than forecast in the autumn. Inflation is forecast to hit 8.4% this year, before easing to 6.3% in 2023, and then 3.4% in 2024 and 2.3% in 2025. Banka Slovenije will present the projections for Slovenia today.

Title: Governor's statement following the monetary meeting of the Governing Council in the euro area continued to moderate economic activity in the fourth quarter of last year, but it was not as strong as expected. Data suggest that the slowdown in economic activity will be less pronounced this year. Inflation has moderated somewhat over the past three months, but remains at high levels and core inflation remains high. Financial markets reflect improved economic activity prospects and interest rate hikes for major central banks.
text: BANKA SLOVENIJE EVROSISTEM Governors statement following the ECBs monetary policy meeting 02/03/2023 / Press release The slowdown in economic activity in the euro area continued in the final quarter of last year, but was not as sharp as expected. Data indicate that the aforementioned slowdown will be less pronounced again this year. Inflation eased slightly in the final three months of the year but remains high, as does core inflation. Improved outlooks regarding economic activity and interest rate hikes by major central banks are reflected on the financial markets. In these circumstances, the Governing Council of the ECB opted yesterday for further action, and raised key interest rates at the fifth consecutive monetary policy meeting, once again by 0.5 percentage points. It also expressed its expectations that interest rate hikes will continue, with another 0.5 percentage point hike in March. Monetary policy normalisation was also continued via other instruments. The Governing Council decided to raise all three key ECB interest rates again, by 50 basis points. Given persisting inflationary pressures, the Governing Council of the ECB expects to raise interest rates again by 50 basis points at its next meeting in March. Interest rates, on a restrictive level, will simultaneously lower inflation, as they will curb demand and mitigate the risk of rising inflation expectations. Further monetary policy decisions will be adjusted to current conditions and expectations. The normalisation of other monetary policy instruments will also continue. As announced in December 2022, the Governing Council will reduce the scope of purchases in the APP at the beginning of March. The average monthly reduction will amount to EUR 15 billion until the end of the second quarter of 2023. That reduction will be carried out proportionally with regard to maturity under individual programmes in the scope of the APP. Favour will be given to more climate-oriented issuers in the reinvestment of purchased corporate bonds. Todays decisions were adopted on the basis of data that indicate economic growth in the euro area is cooling, but remains more robust than previously expected given recent economic development. Euro area GDP rose by 0.1% in quarter-on-quarter terms in the final quarter of last year, despite an expected decline, while Januarys soft indicators of economic activity point to more favourable outlooks at the beginning of this year, as well. The probability of a recession in the euro area is thus falling significantly. In the context of the continuing war in Ukraine and slowing global economic growth, uncertainty regarding future outlooks for the euro area remains elevated, but is more equally distributed. Inflation was 8.5% in the euro area in January (according to Eurostats preliminary estimate), marking the third consecutive month of decline. The latter was almost exclusively the result of sharply lower growth in energy prices, which was a reflection, inter alia, of more favourable conditions on European energy markets, in the context of which natural gas and electricity prices were down notably. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, was unchanged in January, at 5.2%, and continues to indicate persistent, more broadly based inflationary pressures. Significant uncertainty regarding the continuation of inflation trends is linked in particular to rising food prices and developments in wages, the growth of which has accelerated in recent months. On the financial markets in early 2023, short-term interest rates gradually adjusted to expectations that the ECB will continue with interest rate hikes. Longer-term interest rates, on the other hand, remained relatively unchanged. The premiums on euro area government bonds over benchmark German government bonds fell, as did premiums on the yield of bonds of private issuers, while the values of share indices were up. Developments on the financial markets reflected the improved mood of investors in the context of improving economic forecasts for this year.

Title: Opening remarks by Governor Botjan Vaslet at the discussion Balance of payments  an indicator of the economic situation and a guide for economic policy makers
text: Introductory address by Governor Bostjan Vaslet at the discussion Balance of Payments  An Indicator of the Situation in the Economy and a Guide for Economic Policy Makers 28.03.2023 / Public appearances The spoken word counts. Dear Guests, Welcome to the round table, where we will discuss with today's distinguished guests the balance of payments, where certain upheavals have occurred in the last year, and the importance of balance of payments movements for the conduct of economic policies and for the economy. In the last decade, balance of payments developments have not been at the centre of economic reporting and discussions in Slovenia. In the decade until last year, both Slovenia and the euro area had a surplus in trade with other countries, which spilled over into a current account surplus. The eurozone countries are not homogeneous in this regard, which is occasionally the subject of controversy given the multi-year high surpluses of Germany and the Netherlands and the traditional deficits of Greece and Cyprus. The pandemic crisis and Russia's invasion of Ukraine have led to a global increase in commodity prices and an energy crisis in Europe. After a decade of current account surpluses, many commodity-importing countries turned into deficits last year. High growth in the prices of energy products and other raw materials has significantly increased the price of imports, while the increase in domestic consumption has also increased imports in quantity. Whether these are one-off and cyclical factors of the deficit, or whether there is also some structural shift in the background, is one of the questions for today's discussion. In a highly globalised world, countries are closely linked to each other economically and financially. We try to capture these links as comprehensively as possible in the balances of payments of individual countries. The balance of payments for Slovenia is prepared by the Bank of Slovenia in cooperation with the Statistical Office. In doing so, great attention is paid to the quality and timely availability of balance of payments data. They are an important source of information for economic policy decisions, as they help us to better understand economic developments, the financing of sectors and their competitiveness. They are also input for the production of other statistics, such as national accounts and thus GDP. The link between the balance of payments, i.e. background developments and economic policies, is a two-way street. In addition to the high increase in import prices, the recent deterioration in the current account balance in Slovenia and the euro area is also a reflection of high domestic consumption, supported by record-high employment and private sector savings. In recent years, both have also been influenced by monetary and fiscal policy, the combination of which has had a predominantly accommodative effect over the past eight years,[1] first by addressing disinflationary pressures, and then by mitigating the consequences of the pandemic, geopolitical and, fiscally, energy crisis. The drivers of the recent deterioration in balance-of-payments developments largely coincide with those of high inflation. The Eurosystem responded to the increase in inflation clearly above our 2% medium-term target last year by concluding net asset purchases, normalising interest rates, which had been raised by 3.5 percentage points since July last year, adjusting the terms of longer-term lending to banks, and in March this year we started reducing our holdings of securities. Our anti-inflationary measures are contributing to a decline in import growth by moderating domestic demand and, in the absence of new shocks, are expected to contribute to a gradual improvement in the current account balance. A gradual reduction in the state budget deficit is also expected to work in this direction. Let me conclude. External imbalances can reflect a variety of economic challenges. Policy responses depend on whether there are short-term or structural factors in the background, and on the sustainability of such developments, as we will highlight together with the guests in today's debate. Before the discussion, I would like to give the floor to Irena, who will present a more comprehensive picture of balance of payments statistics, together with data sources, developments in Slovenia and the euro area, as well as the background and trends. text_original: Uvodni nagovor guvernerja Botjana Vasleta na razpravi Plailna bilanca  pokazatelj stanja v gospodarstvu in vodilo za nosilce ekonomskih politik 28.03.2023 / Javni nastopi Velja govorjena beseda. Spotovani gostje, lepo pozdravljeni in dobrodoli na okrogli mizi, na kateri se bomo z dananjimi cenjenim gosti pogovarjali o plailni bilanci, kjer je v zadnjem letu prilo do doloenih preobratov, in o pomenu plailnobilannih gibanj za vodenje ekonomskih politik in za gospodarstvo. V zadnjem desetletju plailnobilanna gibanja pri nas niso bila v srediu gospodarskih poroanj in razprav. Tako Slovenija kot evrsko obmoje sta v desetletju do lani v trgovanju z drugimi dravami dosegala preseek, ki se je prelil v preseek na tekoem raunu plailne bilance. Drave evrskega obmoja pri tem sicer niso homogene, kar je ob veletnih visokih presekih Nemije in Nizozemske ter tradicionalnih primanjkljajih Grije in Cipra, obasno predmet polemike. Pod vplivom pandemske krize in ruske invazije na Ukrajino je prilo do globalnega povianja cen surovin in v Evropi do energetske krize. Po desetletju preseka na tekoem raunu plailne bilance smo mnoge drave uvoznice surovin lani doivele preobrat v primanjkljaj. Visoka rast cen energentov in drugih surovin je mono podraila uvoz, ob poveanju domae potronje pa smo uvoz poveali tudi koliinsko. Ali gre za enkratne in cikline dejavnike primanjkljaja, ali se v ozadju kae tudi kaken strukturni premik, je eno od vpraanj za dananjo razpravo. V mono globaliziranem svetu smo drave med seboj tesno ekonomsko in nanno povezane. Te povezave skuamo karseda celovito zajeti v plailnih bilancah posameznih drav. Za Slovenijo plailno bilanco pripravljamo v Banki Sloveniji v sodelovanju s statistinim uradom. Pri tem veliko pozornost poveamo kakovosti in pravoasni dostopnosti plailnobilannih podatkov. Ti so namre pomemben vir informacij za oblikovanje odloitev ekonomskih politik, saj nam pomagajo bolje razumeti gospodarska dogajanja, nanciranje sektorjev in njihovo konkurennost. So tudi input za pripravo drugih statistik, kot so nacionalni rauni in s tem BDP. Povezanost plailne bilance oziroma gibanj v ozadju in ekonomskih politik je obojesmerna. Nedavno poslabanje salda tekoega rauna v Sloveniji in evrskem obmoju je poleg visokega porasta uvoznih cen tudi odraz visoke domae potronje, ki jo podpirata rekordno visoka zaposlenost in prihranki zasebnega sektorja. Na oboje smo v zadnjih letih vplivali tudi z denarno in skalno politiko, katerih kombinacija je zadnjih osem let delovala preteno spodbujevalno,[1] naprej z naslavljanjem dezinacijskih pritiskov, nato z blaitvijo posledic pandemske, geopolitine in s skalne strani tudi energetske krize. Dejavniki nedavnega poslabanja plailnobilannih gibanj v veliki meri sovpadajo z dejavniki visoke inacije. Na povianje inacije vidno nad na 2odstotni srednjeroni cilj smo se v Evrosistemu lani odzvali z zakljukom neto nakupov vrednostih papirjev, z normalizacijo obrestnih mer, ki smo jih od julija lani do danes zviali za 3,5 odsotne toke, s prilagoditvijo pogojev dolgoronejega posojanja bankam, marca letos pa smo prieli z zmanjevanjem imetij vrednostnih papirjev. Nai protiinacijski ukrepi prek umirjanja domaega povpraevanja prispevajo k znievanju rasti uvoza ter bodo v odsotnosti novih okov predvidoma prispevali k postopnemu izboljanju salda tekoega rauna. V tej smeri naj bi delovalo tudi postopno znievanje decita dravnega prorauna. Naj zakljuim. Zunanja neravnovesja lahko odsevajo razline gospodarske izzive. Odzivi politik so odvisni od tega, ali so v ozadju kratkoroni ali strukturni dejavniki, ter kakna je vzdrnost taknih gibanj, kot bomo skupaj z gosti osvetlili v dananji razpravi. Pred razpravo besedo predajam Ireni, ki bo predstavila celovitejo sliko o plailnobilanni statistiki, skupaj s podatkovnimi viri, gibanji v Sloveniji in evrskem obmoju ter ozadjem ter gibanj.
